艾伦·查尔默斯是悉尼大学的兼职副教授，他自1971年起在该校任教，最初在哲学学院，1987年起在科学史与科学哲学研究中心任教，该研究中心由他一手创建。查尔默斯1939年出生于英国布里斯托尔，1961年毕业于布里斯托尔大学物理系，1964年获得曼彻斯特大学物理学硕士学位。他曾任教两年，教授物理学和科学史，之后重返伦敦大学攻读全日制学位，并于1971年获得科学史与科学哲学博士学位。1997年，他当选为人文科学院院士，并于2000年至2010年担任弗林德斯大学哲学系访问学者。

Alan Chalmers is Adjunct Associate Professor at the University of Sydney, where he taught from 1971, first in the School of Philosophy, and from 1987 in the Unit for the History and Philosophy of Science, which he was instrumental in setting up. Born in Bristol, England, in 1939, he graduated in physics at the University of Bristol in 1961, and received an MSc in physics from the University of Manchester in 1964. He taught physics and the history of science for two years before returning to full-time study at the University of London, where he received his PhD in history and philosophy of science in 1971. He was elected a Fellow of the Academy of Humanities in 1997 and was a Visiting Scholar in the Philosophy Department at Flinders University from 2000 to 2010.

第一版序言

Preface to the first edition

本书旨在以简洁明了的方式，对现代科学本质观进行入门介绍。在教授科学哲学课程时，无论是面向哲学专业的本科生，还是面向希望了解最新科学理论的科研人员，我都越来越意识到，目前并没有一本合适的书，甚至几本书，可以推荐给初学者。关于现代科学本质观，唯一可用的资料来源是原始文献。然而，这些原始文献对初学者来说往往过于深奥，而且数量庞大，难以让所有学生都能轻松获取。当然，对于那些希望认真研究这一主题的人来说，本书并不能完全替代原始文献，但我希望它能提供一个实用且易于理解的起点，而这在其他情况下是不存在的。

This book is intended to be a simple, clear and elementary introduction to modern views about the nature of science. When teaching philosophy of science, either to philosophy undergraduates or to scientists wishing to become familiar with recent theories about science, I have become increasingly aware that there is no suitable single book, or even a small number of books, that one can recommend to the beginner. The only sources on the modern views that are available are the original ones. Many of these are too difficult for beginners, and in any case they are too numerous to be made easily available to a large number of students. This book will be no substitute for the original sources for anyone wishing to pursue the topic seriously, of course, but I hope it will provide a useful and easily accessible starting point that does not otherwise exist.

我原本打算让讨论保持简洁，事实证明，在本书大约三分之二的篇幅里，这个目标基本实现了。当我写到那个阶段，开始批判现代观点时，我惊讶地发现：首先，我比预想的更不认同这些观点；其次，我的批判逐渐勾勒出一个相当连贯的替代方案。这个替代方案在本书的后几章中有所概述。我乐于看到，本书的后半部分不仅总结了当前关于科学本质的观点，也概述了下一代观点。

My intention of keeping the discussion simple proved to be reasonably realistic for about two-thirds of the book. By the time I had reached that stage and had begun to criticise the modern views, I found, to my surprise, first, that I disagreed with those views more than I had thought and, second, that from my criticism a fairly coherent alternative was emerging. That alternative is sketched in the latter chapters of the book. It would be pleasant for me to think that the second half of this book contains not only summaries of current views on the nature of science but also a summary of the next view.

我对科学史和科学哲学的专业兴趣始于伦敦，当时的学术氛围深受卡尔·波普尔教授的影响。本书的内容充分体现了我对波普尔教授及其著作、讲座和研讨会，以及已故的伊姆雷·拉卡托斯教授的感激之情。本书前半部分的结构很大程度上借鉴了拉卡托斯关于研究纲领方法论的精彩文章。波普尔学派的一个显著特点是，它要求学者明确自己感兴趣的问题，并以简洁明了的方式表达自己的观点。虽然我在这方面深受波普尔和拉卡托斯的影响，但我简洁清晰的表达能力主要源于我与海因茨·波斯特教授的互动。在切尔西学院科学史与科学哲学系攻读博士学位期间，波斯特教授是我的导师。我始终无法摆脱一种不安的感觉，担心他会把这本书还给我，并要求我重写他看不懂的部分。我在伦敦的同事中，我尤其要感谢他们，他们当时大多还是学生，其中，现任教于印第安纳大学的诺雷塔·科尔特格（Noretta Koertge）给予了我极大的帮助。

My professional interest in history and philosophy of science began in London, in a climate that was dominated by the views of Professor Karl Popper. My debt to him, his writings, his lectures and his seminars, and also to the late Professor Imre Lakatos, must be very evident from the contents of this book. The form of the first half of it owes much to Lakatos’s brilliant article on the methodology of research programs. A noteworthy feature of the Popperian school was the pressure it put on one to be clear about the problem one was interested in and to express one’s views on it in a simple and straightforward way. Although I owe much to the example of Popper and Lakatos in this respect, any ability that I have to express myself simply and clearly stems mostly from my interaction with Professor Heinz Post, who was my supervisor at Chelsea College while I was working on my doctorial thesis in the Department of History and Philosophy of Science there. I cannot rid myself of an uneasy feeling that his copy of this book will be returned to me along with the demand that I rewrite the bits he does not understand. Of my colleagues in London to whom I owe a special debt, most of them students at the time, Noretta Koertge, now at Indiana University, helped me considerably.

我之前提到波普尔学派是一个学派，然而直到我从伦敦来到悉尼，我才真正意识到自己之前身处其中的程度。令我惊讶的是，我发现一些受维特根斯坦、奎因或马克思影响的哲学家认为波普尔在许多问题上都大错特错，甚至有人认为他的观点极其危险。我认为我从这段经历中获益匪浅。其中一点是，正如本书后半部分所论证的，波普尔在一些重要问题上的确是错误的。然而，这并不改变波普尔学派的进路远胜于我所接触过的大多数哲学系所采用的进路这一事实。

I referred above to the Popperian school as a school, and yet it was not until I came to Sydney from London that I fully realised the extent to which I had been in a school. I found, to my surprise, that there were philosophers influenced by Wittgenstein or Quine or Marx who thought that Popper was quite wrong on many issues, and some who even thought that his views were positively dangerous. I think I have learnt much from that experience. One of the things that I have learnt is that on a number of major issues Popper is indeed wrong, as is argued in the latter portions of this book. However, this does not alter the fact that the Popperian approach is infinitely better than the approach adopted in most philosophy departments that I have encountered.

我非常感谢悉尼的朋友们，是他们让我从沉睡中醒来。我这么说并非暗示我接受他们的观点而非波普尔的观点。他们比我更清楚这一点。但我实在没时间去理会那些关于框架不可通约的晦涩废话（波普尔主义者们肯定会对此竖起耳朵），因此，我不得不承认并反驳悉尼的同事和对手们的观点，这让我得以理解他们观点的优势以及我自身观点的不足。我希望在此特别提及让·柯索伊斯和沃尔·苏奇廷不会冒犯到任何人。

I owe much to my friends in Sydney who have helped to waken me from my slumber. I do not wish to imply by this that I accept their views rather than Popperian ones. They know better than that. But since I have no time for obscurantist nonsense about the incommensurability of frameworks (here Popperians prick up their ears), the extent to which I have been forced to acknowledge and counter the views of my Sydney colleagues and adversaries has led me to understand the strengths of their views and the weaknesses of my own. I hope I will not upset anyone by singling out Jean Curthoys and Wal Suchting for special mention here.

幸运且细心的读者会在本书中发现从弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫那里偷来的奇怪比喻，并意识到我应该向他表示感谢（或道歉）。

Lucky and attentive readers will detect in this book the odd metaphor stolen from Vladimir Nabokov, and will realise that I owe him some ackowledgment (or apology).

最后，我要向那些不在乎这本书、不会读这本书，以及在我写作期间不得不忍受我的朋友们致以亲切的问候。

I conclude with a warm ‘hello’ to those friends who don’t care about the book, who won’t read the book, and who had to put up with me while I wrote it.

艾伦·查尔默斯

Alan Chalmers

悉尼，1976年

Sydney, 1976

第二版序言

Preface to the second edition

从本书第一版的反响来看，前八章作为“对现代科学本质观点的简明、清晰、基础的介绍”相当出色。但似乎也普遍认为后四章未能达到这一目标。因此，在本次修订扩充版中，我基本保留了前八章的内容，并用六章全新的章节替换了后四章。第一版后半部分的问题之一在于它不再简洁易懂。我力求使新章节保持简洁，但恐怕在处理最后两章的难题时，我并未完全做到。尽管我努力使讨论简明扼要，但我希望这不会使我的观点变得毫无争议。

Judging by responses to the first edition of this book it would seem that the first eight chapters of it function quite well as ‘a simple, clear and elementary introduction to modern views about the nature of science’. It also seems to be fairly universally agreed that the last four chapters fail to do so. Consequently, in this revised and extended edition I have left chapters 1–8 virtually unchanged and have replaced the last four chapters by six entirely new ones. One of the problems with the latter part of the first edition was that it ceased to be simple and elementary. I have tried to keep my new chapters simple, although I fear I have not entirely succeeded when dealing with the difficult issues of the final two chapters. Although I have tried to keep the discussion simple, I hope I have not thereby become uncontroversial.

第一版后半部分的另一个问题是缺乏清晰度。尽管我仍然坚信，我当时摸索的大部分方向都是正确的，但我确实未能表达出一个连贯且论证充分的观点，正如我的批评者所指出的那样。这并非完全可以归咎于路易·阿尔都塞，他的观点在当时非常流行，而且在新版中仍然能感受到他的影响。我已经吸取了教训，今后会非常谨慎地避免过度受巴黎最新潮流的影响。

Another problem with the latter part of the first edition is lack of clarity. Although I remain convinced that most of what I was groping for there was on the right track, I certainly failed to express a coherent and well-argued position, as my critics have made clear. Not all of this can be blamed on Louis Althusser, whose views were very much in vogue at the time of writing, and whose influence can still be discerned to some extent in this new edition. I have learnt my lesson and in future will be very wary of being unduly influenced by the latest Paris fashions.

我的朋友特里·布莱克和丹尼斯·罗素让我相信，保罗·费耶阿本德的著作比我之前认为的更有价值。在新版中，我更加关注他的作品，并试图去伪存真，区分反方法论和达达主义。我也必须将重要的意义与“关于框架不可通约性的晦涩无稽之谈”区分开来。

My friends Terry Blake and Denise Russell have convinced me that there is more of importance in the writings of Paul Feyerabend than I was previously prepared to admit. I have given him more attention in this new edition and have tried to separate the wheat from the chaff, the anti-methodism from the dadaism. I have also been obliged to separate the important sense from ‘obscurantist nonsense about the incommensurability of frameworks’.

本书的修订得益于众多同事、评论家和来信者的批评指正。我在此不一一列举，但谨此致谢。

The revision of this book owes much to the criticism of numerous colleagues, reviewers and correspondents. I will not attempt to name them all, but acknowledge my debt and offer my thanks.

由于本书修订后采用了新的结局，封面上那只猫的原意已然丧失。然而，尽管它没有胡须，却似乎拥有相当数量的粉丝，因此我们保留了它，并请读者重新解读它那笑容的含义。

Since the revision of this book has resulted in a new ending, the original point of the cat on the cover has been lost. However, the cat does seem to have a considerable following, despite her lack of whiskers, so we have retained her, and merely ask readers to reinterpret her grin.

艾伦·查尔默斯

Alan Chalmers

悉尼，1981年

Sydney, 1981

第三版序言

Preface to the third edition

本版是对前一版的重大修订，原版章节几乎全部被修改，许多章节已被替换。此外，还新增了一些章节。做出这些改动是必要的，原因有二。首先，自本书初版出版以来的二十年间，我教授科学哲学入门课程，这使我能够更好地完成这项工作。其次，近一二十年来，科学哲学领域取得了重要的发展，任何入门教材都必须考虑到这些发展。

This edition represents a major reworking of the previous edition, in which very few of the original chapters have emerged unscathed and many have been replaced. There are also a number of new chapters. The changes were necessary for two reasons. First, the teaching of an introductory course in the philosophy of science that I have undertaken in the twenty years since first writing this book has taught me how to do the job better. Second, there have been important developments in the philosophy of science in the last decade or two that need to be taken account of in any introductory text.

目前，科学哲学领域一个颇具影响力的学派试图以贝叶斯定理（概率论中的一个定理）为基础构建科学理论。另一个趋势是“新实验主义”，它比以往更加关注实验在科学中的本质和作用。本书第12章和第13章分别对这两种思想流派进行了描述和评价。近期的研究，特别是南希·卡特赖特（Nancy Cartwright）的研究，凸显了科学中定律本质的问题，因此，新版新增了一章专门探讨这一主题，以及一章旨在紧跟科学现实主义和反现实主义解释之间争论的论述。

A currently influential school in the philosophy of science involves an attempt to erect an account of science on Bayes’ theorem, a theorem in the probability calculus. A second trend, ‘the new experimentalism’, involves paying more attention than hitherto to the nature and role of experiment in science. Chapters 12 and 13, respectively, contain a description and an appraisal of these schools of thought. Recent work, especially that of Nancy Cartwright, has brought to the fore questions about the nature of laws as they figure in science, so a chapter on this topic is included in this new edition, as is a chapter that aims to keep abreast of the debate between realist and anti-realist interpretations of science.

因此，尽管我并不声称已经找到了本书标题所提出问题的最终答案，但我努力跟上当代辩论的步伐，并力求以一种不那么晦涩难懂的方式向读者介绍相关内容。每章末尾都附有延伸阅读建议，对于那些希望更深入研究这些问题的人来说，这将是一个有用且最新的起点。

So while not pretending that I have arrived at the definitive answer to the question that forms the title of this book, I have endeavoured to keep abreast of the contemporary debate and to introduce the reader to it in a way that is not too technical. There are suggestions for further reading at the end of each chapter, which will be a useful and up-to-date starting point for those who wish to pursue these matters in greater depth.

我不会一一列举所有帮助我改进本书的同事和学生。1997年6月在悉尼举办的国际研讨会“科学究竟是什么？二十年后的反思”让我受益匪浅。我衷心感谢研讨会的赞助方：英国文化协会、昆士兰大学出版社、开放大学出版社、哈克特出版社和布姆出版社，以及所有出席并参与会议的同事和老朋友。这次研讨会极大地鼓舞了我的士气，也激励我着手进行重写本书这项艰巨的任务。大部分重写工作是在我担任麻省理工学院迪布纳科学史与技术史研究所研究员期间完成的，对此我深表感谢。我再也找不到比这更支持我的环境了，更有利于我集中精力工作。感谢张哈索克先生仔细阅读了书稿并提出了宝贵的意见。

I will not attempt to name all the colleagues and students from whom I have learnt how to improve this book. I learnt much at an international symposium held in Sydney in June 1997, ‘What Is This Thing Called Science? Twenty Years On’. I thank the sponsors of that symposium, The British Council, the University of Queensland Press, the Open University Press, Hackett Publishing Company and Uitgeverij Boom, and those colleagues and old friends who attended and participated in the proceedings. The event did much to boost my morale and gave me the incentive to undertake the major task that was involved in rewriting the text. Much of the rewriting was done while I was a Research Fellow at the Dibner Institute for the History of Science and Technology, MIT, for which I express my appreciation. I could not have hoped for a more supportive environment, and one more conducive to some concentrated work. I thank Hasok Chang for his careful reading of the manuscript and his helpful comments.

我已经搞不清楚这只猫到底在咧嘴笑什么了，但我似乎从中感受到了一种持续的赞许，这让人感到安心。

I have lost track of what the cat is meant to be grinning about, but I seem to detect a note of continuing approval, which is reassuring.

艾伦·查尔默斯

Alan Chalmers

马萨诸塞州剑桥，1998年

Cambridge, Mass., 1998

第四版序言

Preface to the fourth edition

自本书1976年首次出版以来，我曾两次修订此书，删去了我认为无益、错误或不够清晰的段落甚至整章内容，并根据相关文献的发展以及我自身思想的澄清，增添了新的段落或章节。鉴于此，我最近对第三版进行了批判性阅读。与我重新评估第一版和第二版时的情况不同，这次我并没有发现太多令我不满的地方。尽管如此，我仍然发现了一些可以进一步阐明和拓展书中关键主题的方法。这种重新思考的主要来源是我撰写《科学家的原子与哲人的石头：科学如何成功而哲学如何失败地获得原子知识》一书的过程。关于原子科学知识如何产生的历程，为阐明和支持我关于科学知识与其他知识类型区别的主要观点提供了丰富的例证。因此，我在第四版中加入了一篇附录，引用这些内容来帮助阐明科学的本质。

Since this book first appeared in 1976 I have twice seen fit to write a new edition of it, removing passages, or even whole chapters, that I found unhelpful, wrong-headed or insufficiently clear, and adding new passages or chapters drawing on developments in the literature as well as on clarifications of my own thoughts. With such an end in view, I recently subjected the third edition to a critical reading. I did not find much with which I was dissatisfied as had been the case with my reappraisal of the first and second editions. I did, nevertheless, discern ways in which key themes in the book could be clarified and extended. The main source for this rethinking was the work that went into the writing of my book The Scientist’s Atom and the Philosopher’s Stone: How Science Succeeded and Philosophy Failed to Gain Knowledge of Atoms. The story of how scientific knowledge of atoms became possible proves to be a ready source of examples to illustrate and support my main points concerning the distinctive character of scientific as opposed to other kinds of knowledge. Accordingly, I have included a Postscript in this fourth edition that draws on this material to help clarify what this thing called science is.

二十一世纪初的十年，我的学术之家是阿德莱德弗林德斯大学哲学系。我衷心感谢那里的同事们，特别是罗德尼·艾伦、乔治·库瓦利斯和格雷格·奥黑尔，感谢他们帮助我度过了这段富有成效的时光。在众多给予我帮助、支持和建设性批评的学者中，乌苏拉·克莱因、黛博拉·梅奥、艾伦·马斯格雷夫和约翰·诺顿尤其值得一提。2003年至2005年，我的研究工作得到了澳大利亚研究理事会的资助。我曾获得新西兰坎特伯雷大学和匹兹堡大学的研究奖学金，并在布里斯托大学哲学系进行了一个学期的学习。所有这些支持都对我帮助极大，我对此深表感激。桑德拉·格莱姆斯一直以来都给予我莫大的支持，我对此感激不尽，尽管她的贡献常常被低估。

My academic home for the first decade of the twenty-first century was the Philosophy Department at Flinders University in Adelaide. I thank my colleagues there, especially Rodney Allen, George Couvalis and Greg O’Hair, for helping to make that period productive. Of the many academics that have provided me with help, support and constructive criticism, Ursula Klein, Deborah Mayo, Alan Musgrave and John Norton deserve special mention. From 2003 to 2005 my work was supported by a grant from the Australian Research Council. I benefited from Research Fellowships at the University of Canterbury, New Zealand, and the University of Pittsburgh and from a semester in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Bristol. All of this support was very helpful and much appreciated. Sandra Grimes has been a constant and much appreciated and valued, if unduly acknowledged, support.

艾伦·查尔默斯

Alan Chalmers

悉尼，2012年

Sydney, 2012

介绍

Introduction

科学备受推崇。人们普遍认为科学及其方法具有某种特殊之处。将某些论断、推理或研究成果冠以“科学”之名，意在暗示其具有某种价值或特殊的可靠性。但科学究竟有何特别之处？这种号称能得出特别有价值或可靠结果的“科学方法”究竟是什么？本书旨在阐明并解答此类问题。

Science is highly esteemed. Apparently it is a widely held belief that there is something special about science and its methods. The naming of some claim or line of reasoning or piece of research ‘scientific’ is done in a way that is intended to imply some kind of merit or special kind of reliability. But what, if anything, is so special about science? What is this ‘scientific method’ that allegedly leads to especially meritorious or reliable results? This book is an attempt to elucidate and answer questions of that kind.

尽管有些人因为氢弹和污染等后果而对科学感到失望，但日常生活中仍有大量证据表明，科学备受推崇。广告经常宣称，某种产品经科学证明更白、更有效、更具性吸引力，或在某些方面优于竞争对手。这意在暗示这些说法特别有理有据，甚至无可辩驳。最近一则宣传基督教科学的报纸广告标题为“科学证明基督教圣经是真理”，并声称“如今连科学家自己都相信这一点”。这直接诉诸于科学和科学家的权威。我们不禁要问，这种权威的依据是什么？对科学的高度推崇不仅体现在日常生活和大众媒体中，在学术界也同样显而易见。许多研究领域如今都被其支持者称为科学，大概是为了暗示这些领域的方法与物理学或生物学等传统科学一样，具有坚实的基础和潜在的成效。政治学和社会科学如今已司空见惯。许多马克思主义者热衷于强调历史唯物主义是一门科学。此外，图书馆学、行政学、语言学、林学、乳品学、肉类与动物学以及殡葬学也都已出现在大学课程大纲中。关于“创造科学”地位的争论仍在继续。值得注意的是，辩论双方都假定存在某种特殊的“科学”范畴。他们的分歧在于创造科学是否符合科学的定义。

There is an abundance of evidence from everyday life that science is held in high regard, in spite of some disenchantment with science because of consequences for which some hold it responsible, such as hydrogen bombs and pollution. Advertisements frequently assert that a particular product has been scientifically shown to be whiter, more potent, more sexually appealing or in some way superior to rival products. This is intended to imply that the claims are particularly well founded and perhaps beyond dispute. A recent newspaper advertisement advocating Christian Science was headed ‘Science speaks and says the Christian Bible is provedly true’ and went on to tell us that ‘even the scientists themselves believe it these days’. Here we have a direct appeal to the authority of science and scientists. We might well ask what the basis for such authority is. The high regard for science is not restricted to everyday life and the popular media. It is evident in the scholarly and academic world too. Many areas of study are now described as sciences by their supporters, presumably in an effort to imply that the methods used are as firmly based and as potentially fruitful as in a traditional science such as physics or biology. Political science and social science are by now commonplace. Many Marxists are keen to insist that historical materialism is a science. In addition, Library Science, Administrative Science, Speech Science, Forest Science, Dairy Science, Meat and Animal Science and Mortuary Science have all made their appearance on university syllabuses.1 The debate about the status of ‘creation science’ is still active. It is noteworthy in this context that participants on both sides of the debate assume that there is some special category ‘science’. What they disagree about is whether creation science qualifies as a science or not.

许多所谓的社会科学或人文科学领域的学者都认同这样一种论点，大致如下：“过去三百年来物理学取得的巨大成功，被认为应归功于一种特殊方法——‘科学方法’的应用。因此，如果社会科学和人文科学想要效仿物理学的成功，就必须首先理解并阐述这种方法，然后再将其应用于社会科学和人文科学领域。”这种论点引出了两个根本性问题，即“这种被认为是物理学成功关键的科学方法究竟是什么？”以及“将物理学的这种方法移植到其他领域是否合理？”

Many in the so-called social or human sciences subscribe to a line of argument that runs roughly as follows. ‘The undoubted success of physics over the last three hundred years, it is assumed, is to be attributed to the application of a special method, “the scientific method”. Therefore, if the social and human sciences are to emulate the success of physics then that is to be achieved by first understanding and formulating this method and then applying it to the social and human sciences.’ Two fundamental questions are raised by this line of argument, namely, ‘what is this scientific method that is alleged to be the key to the success of physics?’ and ‘is it legitimate to transfer that method from physics and apply it elsewhere?’

这一切都凸显了这样一个事实：关于科学知识与其他知识类型的区别，以及科学方法的精确定义等问题，被视为至关重要且意义深远。然而，正如我们将看到的，回答这些问题绝非易事。或许，对这些问题答案的普遍直觉可以概括为：科学的特殊之处在于它源于事实，而非基于个人观点。这或许可以解释，尽管人们对查尔斯·狄更斯和D·H·劳伦斯的小说孰优孰劣可能持有不同意见，但在伽利略和爱因斯坦的相对论孰优孰劣的问题上，却不存在这种意见分歧。正是事实决定了爱因斯坦的创新优于以往的相对论观点，任何未能理解这一点的人都大错特错。

All this highlights the fact that questions concerning the distinctiveness of scientific knowledge, as opposed to other kinds of knowledge, and the exact identification of the scientific method are seen as fundamentally important and consequential. As we shall see, however, answering these questions is by no means straightforward. A fair attempt to capture widespread intuitions about the answers to them is encapsulated, perhaps, in the idea that what is so special about science is that it is derived from the facts, rather than being based on personal opinion. This maybe captures the idea that, whereas personal opinions may differ over the relative merits of the novels of Charles Dickens and D. H. Lawrence, there is no room for such variation of opinions on the relative merits of Galileo’s and Einstein’s theories of relativity. It is the facts that are presumed to determine the superiority of Einstein’s innovations over previous views on relativity, and anyone who fails to appreciate this is simply wrong.

我们稍后将看到，认为科学知识的显著特征在于其源于经验事实的观点，即便要被认可，也必须以谨慎且高度限定的形式加以认可。我们将遇到种种理由，质疑通过观察和实验获得的事实是否如传统假设的那样直接可靠。我们还将发现，即使假定这些事实的存在，也有充分的理由认为，科学知识既不能通过参照事实来最终证明，也不能最终证伪。支持这种怀疑论的部分论据基于对观察本质以及逻辑推理本质及其能力的分析。另一些论据则源于对科学史和当代科学实践的深入考察。现代科学理论和科学方法论发展的一个显著特征是，人们越来越重视科学史。对于许多科学哲学家来说，这带来的一个尴尬结果是，科学史上那些通常被认为是重大进步最具代表性的事件，无论是伽利略、牛顿、达尔文还是爱因斯坦的创新，都与标准的科学哲学描述相悖。

As well shall see, the idea that the distinctive feature of scientific knowledge is that it is derived from the facts of experience can only be sanctioned in a carefully and highly qualified form, if it is to be sanctioned at all. We will encounter reasons for doubting that facts acquired by observation and experiment are as straightforward and secure as has traditionally been assumed. We will also find that a strong case can be made for the claim that scientific knowledge can neither be conclusively proved nor conclusively disproved by reference to the facts, even if the availability of those facts is assumed. Some of the arguments to support this skepticism are based on an analysis of the nature of observation and on the nature of logical reasoning and its capabilities. Others stem from a close look at the history of science and contemporary scientific practice. It has been a feature of modern developments in theories of science and scientific method that increasing attention has been paid to the history of science. One of the embarrassing results of this for many philosophers of science is that those episodes in the history of science that are commonly regarded as most characteristic of major advances, whether they be the innovations of Galileo, Newton, Darwin or Einstein, do not match what standard philosophical accounts of science say they should be like.

人们逐渐意识到科学理论既不能被确凿地证实也不能被证伪，哲学家们的重构与科学的实际运作几乎毫无相似之处，于是便出现了一种反应：彻底放弃科学是一种遵循某种特殊方法的理性活动这一观念。正是这种反应促使哲学家保罗·费耶阿本德（1975）撰写了《反对方法：无政府主义知识论纲要》一书。根据对费耶阿本德后期著作最极端的解读，科学并不具备任何使其本质上优于其他知识类型（例如古代神话或巫术）的特殊属性。对科学的高度推崇被视为一种现代宗教，其作用类似于基督教在早期欧洲所扮演的角色。这种观点认为，对不同科学理论的选择最终取决于个人的主观价值观和意愿。

One reaction to the realisation that scientific theories cannot be conclusively proved or disproved and that the reconstructions of philosophers bear little resemblance to what actually goes on in science is to give up altogether the idea that science is a rational activity operating according to some special method. It is a reaction somewhat like this that led the philosopher Paul Feyerabend (1975) to write a book with the title Against Method: Outline of an Anarchistic Theory of Knowledge. According to the most extreme view that has been read into Feyerabend’s later writings, science has no special features that render it intrinsically superior to other kinds of knowledge such as ancient myths or voodoo. A high regard for science is seen as a modern religion, playing a similar role to that played by Christianity in Europe in earlier eras. It is suggested that the choices between scientific theories boil down to choices determined by the subjective values and wishes of individuals.

费耶阿本德对试图将科学理性化的尝试持怀疑态度，而从社会学或所谓的后现代主义视角出发的近来作家也持有类似的观点。

Feyerabend’s skepticism about attempts to rationalise science is shared by more recent authors from a sociological or so-called postmodernist perspective.

本书对这种应对传统科学理论和科学方法论难题的方式持保留态度。本书试图接受费耶阿本德等人提出的挑战中合理的观点，但同时又力求对科学进行阐述，以展现其独特性和特殊性，从而回应这些挑战。

This kind of response to the difficulties with traditional accounts of science and scientific method is resisted in this book. An attempt is made to accept what is valid in the challenges by Feyerabend and many others, but yet to give an account of science that captures its distinctive and special features in a way that can answer those challenges.

第一章

CHAPTER 1

科学是从经验事实中获得的知识。

Science as knowledge derived from the facts of experience

一种被广泛接受的科学常识观点

A widely held commonsense view of science

在引言中，我曾提出一个观点，即“科学源于事实”这一口号概括了人们对科学知识独特特征的一种普遍认知。本书前四章将对这一观点进行批判性审视。我们会发现，这句口号通常所隐含的许多内容都站不住脚。然而，我们也会发现，这句口号并非完全错误，我将尝试构建一个站得住脚的版本。

In the Introduction I ventured the suggestion that a popular conception of the distinctive feature of scientific knowledge is captured by the slogan ‘science is derived from the facts’. In the first four chapters of this book this view is subjected to a critical scrutiny. We will find that much of what is typically taken to be implied by the slogan cannot be defended. Nevertheless, we will find that the slogan is not entirely misguided and I will attempt to formulate a defensible version of it.

当人们声称科学的特殊之处在于它基于事实时，这些事实被假定为对世界的描述，可以通过谨慎、客观地运用感官直接证实。科学应当基于我们所见、所闻、所触，而非个人意见或臆测。如果对世界的观察以谨慎、客观的方式进行，那么由此确立的事实将构成科学可靠、客观的基础。此外，如果从这一事实基础推导出构成科学知识的规律和理论的推理是合理的，那么由此产生的知识本身也可以被认为是可靠且客观的。

When it is claimed that science is special because it is based on the facts, the facts are presumed to be claims about the world that can be directly established by a careful, unprejudiced use of the senses. Science is to be based on what we can see, hear and touch rather than on personal opinions or speculative imaginings. If observation of the world is carried out in a careful, unprejudiced way then the facts established in this way will constitute a secure, objective basis for science. If, further, the reasoning that takes us from this factual basis to the laws and theories that constitute scientific knowledge is sound, then the resulting knowledge can itself be taken to be securely established and objective.

以上论述概括了一个人们耳熟能详的故事，这个故事在大量的科学文献中都有所体现。JJ Davies（1968，第8页）在其关于科学方法的著作中写道：“科学是建立在事实之上的体系”，H.D. Anthony（1948，第145页）对此主题进行了详细阐述：

The above remarks are the bare bones of a familiar story that is reflected in a wide range of literature about science. ‘Science is a structure built upon facts’ writes J. J. Davies (1968, p. 8) in his book on the scientific method, a theme elaborated on by H. D. Anthony (1948, p. 145):

伽利略打破传统的并非他所做的观察和实验本身，而是他对它们的态度。对他而言，基于这些观察和实验的事实就是事实，而非与某种先入为主的观念挂钩……观察的事实或许符合，或许不符合公认的宇宙体系，但在伽利略看来，重要的是接受事实，并据此构建理论。

It was not so much the observations and experiments which Galileo made that caused the break with tradition as his attitude to them. For him, the facts based on them were taken as facts, and not related to some preconceived idea . . . The facts of observation might, or might not, fit into an acknowledged scheme of the universe, but the important thing, in Galileo’s opinion, was to accept the facts and build the theory to fit them.

安东尼在此不仅清晰地表达了科学知识建立在观察和实验所确立的事实之上的观点，而且还赋予了这一观点历史性的解读，而持此观点的人绝非孤例。一个颇具影响力的论断是，从历史事实的角度来看，现代科学诞生于十七世纪初，当时人们首次认真地采纳了将观察事实作为科学基础的策略。那些接受并利用这一科学起源叙事的人认为，在十七世纪之前，可观察的事实并未被认真对待，也未被视为知识的基础。相反，正如人们所熟知的那样，知识主要建立在权威之上，尤其是哲学家亚里士多德的权威和《圣经》的权威。只有当伽利略等新科学的先驱们以经验为依据挑战这种权威时，现代科学才成为可能。以下摘自 Rowbotham (1918 年，第 27-29 页) 的关于伽利略和比萨斜塔的常见故事的描述，很好地概括了这一观点。

Anthony here not only gives clear expression to the view that scientific knowledge is based on the facts established by observation and experiment, but also gives a historical twist to the idea, and he is by no means alone in this. An influential claim is that, as a matter of historical fact, modern science was born in the early seventeenth century when the strategy of taking the facts of observation seriously as the basis for science was first seriously adopted. It is held by those who embrace and exploit this story about the birth of science that, prior to the seventeenth century, the observable facts were not taken seriously as the foundation for knowledge. Rather, so the familiar story goes, knowledge was based largely on authority, especially the authority of the philosopher Aristotle and the authority of the Bible. It was only when this authority was challenged by an appeal to experience, by pioneers of the new science such as Galileo, that modern science became possible. The following account of the oft-told story of Galileo and the Leaning Tower of Pisa, taken from Rowbotham (1918, pp. 27–9), nicely captured the idea.

伽利略与大学教授们进行的第一次力量测试，与他研究物体下落运动规律有关。亚里士多德曾提出一个公认的公理：物体下落的速度取决于其重量，例如，一块两磅重的石头下落的速度是仅重一磅的石头的两倍，以此类推。似乎没有人质疑过这条规律的正确性，直到伽利略提出异议。他宣称，重量与此无关，而且……两个重量不同的物体……会同时落地。由于伽利略的说法遭到教授们的质疑，他决定公开验证。于是，他邀请全校师生前来观看他即将从比萨斜塔上进行的实验。在预定的那天清晨，伽利略在聚集的大学师生和市民的见证下，登上塔顶，他带着两个球，一个重一百磅，另一个重一磅。他小心翼翼地将两个球放在栏杆边缘，然后将它们一起滚动；人们看到它们均匀地落下，紧接着，随着一声巨响，它们同时撞击地面。古老的传说被证明是错误的，而现代科学，通过这位年轻的发现者，证明了它的观点。

Galileo’s first trial of strength with the university professors was connected with his researches into the laws of motion as illustrated by falling bodies. It was an accepted axiom of Aristotle that the speed of falling bodies was regulated by their respective weights: thus, a stone weighing two pounds would fall twice as quick as one weighing only a single pound and so on. No one seems to have questioned the correctness of this rule, until Galileo gave it his denial. He declared that weight had nothing to do with the matter, and that . . . two bodies of unequal weight . . . would reach the ground at the same moment. As Galileo’s statement was flouted by the body of professors, he determined to put it to a public test. So he invited the whole University to witness the experiment which he was about to perform from the leaning tower. On the morning of the day fixed, Galileo, in the presence of the assesmbled University and townsfolk, mounted to the top of the tower, carrying with him two balls, one weighing one hundred pounds and the other weighing one pound. Balancing the balls carefully on the edge of the parapet, he rolled them over together; they were seen to fall evenly, and the next instant, with a loud clang, they struck the ground together. The old tradition was false, and modern science, in the person of the young discoverer, had vindicated her position.

试图将我称之为科学共同观点——即科学知识来源于事实——形式化的两种思想流派分别是经验主义者和实证主义者。十七、十八世纪的英国经验主义者，尤其是约翰·洛克、乔治·贝克莱和大卫·休谟，认为所有知识都应来源于通过感官知觉植入心灵的观念。实证主义者对事实的本质有着更为宽泛、较少受心理学影响的观点，但他们与经验主义者一样，都认为知识应来源于经验事实。逻辑实证主义者，一个起源于20世纪20年代维也纳的哲学流派，继承了奥古斯特·孔德在十九世纪提出的实证主义，并试图将其形式化，他们尤其关注科学知识与事实之间关系的逻辑形式。经验主义和实证主义的共同观点是，科学知识应该在某种程度上来源于观察所得的事实。

Two schools of thought that involve attempts to formalise what I have called a common view of science, that scientific knowledge is derived from the fact, are the empiricists and the positivists. The British empiricists of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, notably John Locke, George Berkeley and David Hume, held that all knowledge should be derived from ideas implanted in the mind by way of sense perception. The positivists had a somewhat broader and less psychologically orientated view of what facts amount to, but shared the view of the empiricists that knowledge should be derived from the facts of experience. The logical positivists, a school of philosophy that originated in Vienna in the 1920s, took up the positivism that had been introduced by Auguste Comte in the nineteenth century and attempted to formalise it, paying close attention to the logical form of the relationship between scientific knowledge and the facts. Empiricism and positivism share the common view that scientific knowledge should in some way be derived from the facts arrived at by observation.

关于“科学源于事实”这一论断，还涉及另外两个截然不同的问题。其一是这些“事实”的性质，以及科学家如何获取它们。其二是构成我们知识的定律和理论，在获得事实之后，又是如何从中推导出来的。我们将依次探讨这两个问题，本章及接下来的两章将专门讨论科学据称赖以建立的事实的性质，而第四章则探讨科学知识如何被认为源于这些事实。

There are two other rather distinct issues involved in the claim that science is derived from the facts. One concerns the nature of these ‘facts’ and how scientists are meant to have access to them. The second concerns how the laws and theories that constitute our knowledge are derived from the facts once they have been obtained. We will investigate these two issues in turn, devoting this and the next two chapters to a discussion of the nature of the facts on which science is alleged to be based and chapter 4 to the question of how scientific knowledge might be thought to be derived from them.

在普遍观点中，关于科学事实的立场可以分为三个组成部分。它们是：

Three components of the stand on the facts assumed to be the basis of science in the common view can be distinguished. They are:

（a）事实通过感官直接传递给谨慎、公正的观察者。

(a) Facts are directly given to careful, unprejudiced observers via the senses.

（b）事实先于理论，并且独立于理论。

(b) Facts are prior to and independent of theory.

（c）事实构成科学知识的坚实可靠的基础。

(c) Facts constitute a firm and reliable foundation for scientific knowledge.

正如我们将看到的，这些说法都面临着诸多困难，充其量只能以高度限定的形式被接受。

As we shall see, each of these claims is faced with difficulties and, at best, can only be accepted in a highly qualified form.

眼见为实

Seeing is believing

部分原因是视觉是人类观察世界最广泛使用的感官，部分原因也是为了方便起见，我将把对观察的讨论限定在视觉领域。在大多数情况下，不难看出，本文提出的论点可以稍作修改，使其适用于其他感官。关于视觉的简单描述如下：人类用眼睛看东西。人眼最重要的组成部分是晶状体和视网膜，视网膜就像一块屏幕，晶状体将外部物体的图像成像在视网膜上。来自被观察物体的光线通过中间介质从物体到达晶状体。这些光线被晶状体的材料折射，最终聚焦在视网膜上，从而形成物体的图像。到目前为止，眼睛的工作原理与照相机类似。一个很大的区别在于最终图像的记录方式。视神经从视网膜延伸到大脑的中央皮层。这些视网膜细胞携带着光线照射到视网膜各个区域的信息。大脑对这些信息的记录，构成了人类观察者对物体的视觉感知。当然，这个简化的描述还可以添加许多细节，但以上内容已经概括了其基本原理。

Partly because the sense of sight is the sense most extensively used to observe the world, and partly for convenience, I will restrict my discussion of observation to the realm of seeing. In most cases, it will not be difficult to see how the argument presented could be re-cast so as to be applicable to the other senses. A simple account of seeing might run as follows. Humans see using their eyes. The most important components of the human eye are a lens and a retina, the latter acting as a screen on which images of objects external to the eye are formed by the lens. Rays of light from a viewed object pass from the object to the lens via the intervening medium. These rays are refracted by the material of the lens in such a way that they are brought to a focus on the retina, so forming an image of the object. Thus far, the functioning of the eye is analogous to that of a camera. A big difference is in the way the final image is recorded. Optic nerves pass from the retina to the central cortex of the brain. These carry information concerning the light striking the various regions of the retina. It is the recording of this information by the brain that constitutes the seeing of the object by the human observer. Of course, many details could be added to this simplified description, but the account offered captures the general idea.

上述关于视觉观察的描述强烈暗示了两点，而这两点也融入了常见的或经验主义的科学观点中。第一点是，人类观察者或多或少能够直接获取关于世界的某些事实的知识，因为这些信息会在视觉过程中被大脑记录下来。第二点是，两个正常的观察者从同一地点观察同一物体或场景时，会“看到”相同的东西。相同的光线组合会照射到每个观察者的眼睛，并由他们正常的眼球晶状体聚焦在他们正常的视网膜上，从而形成相似的图像。然后，相似的信息会通过他们正常的视神经传递到每个观察者的大脑，最终导致两个观察者看到相同的事物。在后续章节中，我们将看到为什么这种说法具有严重的误导性。

Two points are strongly suggested by the foregoing account of observation through the sense of sight that are incorporated into the common or empiricist view of science. The first is that a human observer has more or less direct access to knowledge of some facts about the world insofar as they are recorded by the brain in the act of seeing. The second is that two normal observers viewing the same object or scene from the same place will ‘see’ the same thing. An identical combination of light rays will strike the eyes of each observer, will be focused on their normal retinas by their normal eye lenses and give rise to similar images. Similar information will then travel to the brain of each observer via their normal optic nerves, resulting in the two observers seeing the same thing. In subsequent sections we will see why this kind of picture is seriously misleading.

视觉体验并非完全由所观看的物体决定。

Visual experiences not determined solely by the object viewed

最简单粗暴的观点认为，关于外部世界的事实直接通过视觉传递给我们。我们只需面对眼前的世界，记录所见之物即可。我只需观察眼前之物，就能确定桌上有一盏灯，或者我的铅笔是黄色的。正如我们所见，这种观点可以用眼睛的工作原理来佐证。如果仅此而已，那么所见之物将取决于被观察对象的性质，观察者面对同一场景时，视觉体验也应始终相同。然而，大量证据表明事实并非如此。两个正常的观察者在相同的物理环境下，从相同的位置观察同一物体，即使他们视网膜上的图像几乎完全相同，他们的视觉体验也未必相同。从某种重要意义上讲，两个观察者未必“看到”的是同一事物。正如N.R. Hanson（1958）所说，“视觉的奥秘远不止肉眼所见”。以下几个简单的例子可以说明这一点。

In its starkest form, the common view has it that facts about the external world are directly given to us through the sense of sight. All we need to do is confront the world before us and record what is there to be seen. I can establish that there is a lamp on my desk or that my pencil is yellow simply by noting what is before my eyes. Such a view can be backed up by a story about how the eye works, as we have seen. If this was all there was to it, then what is seen would be determined by the nature of what is looked at, and observers would always have the same visual experiences when confronting the same scene. However, there is plenty of evidence to indicate that this is simply not the case. Two normal observers viewing the same object from the same place under the same physical circumstances do not necessarily have identical visual experiences, even though the images on their respective retinas may be virtually identical. There is an important sense in which two observers need not ‘see’ the same thing. As N. R. Hanson (1958) has put it, ‘there is more to seeing than meets the eyeball’. Some simple examples will illustrate the point.

图 1

Figure 1

我们大多数人在初看图1时，都会看到一个楼梯，楼梯的上表面清晰可见。但这并非它唯一的呈现方式。同样，我们也可以轻松地将其视为一个楼梯，楼梯的下表面也清晰可见。此外，如果长时间观察这幅图，通常会发现所见景象会频繁且不由自主地在俯视视角和仰视视角之间切换。然而，由于观察者看到的始终是同一个物体，因此视网膜上的图像应该没有改变。这幅图究竟是呈现为俯视视角还是仰视视角，似乎取决于除观察者视网膜上的图像之外的其他因素。我猜想，本书的读者应该不会质疑我关于图1描绘的是楼梯的论断。然而，对一些非洲部落成员进行的实验结果表明，这些部落的文化中既没有用二维透视图描绘三维物体的习俗，也没有描绘楼梯的习俗，因此他们根本不会把图1视为楼梯。由此可见，个体在视觉过程中获得的感知体验并非完全由视网膜上的图像决定。汉森（1958，第一章）提供了一些更引人入胜的例子来说明这一点。

Most of us, when first looking at Figure 1, see the drawing of a staircase with the upper surface of the stairs visible. But this is not the only way in which it can be seen. It can without difficulty be seen as a staircase with the under surface of the stairs visible. Further, if one looks at the picture for some time, one generally finds that what one sees changes frequently, and involuntarily, from a staircase viewed from above to one viewed from below and back again. And yet it seems reasonable to suppose that, since it remains the same object viewed by the observer, the retinal images do not change. Whether the picture is seen as a staircase viewed from above or one viewed from below seems to depend on something other than the image on the retina of the viewer. I suspect that no reader of this book has questioned my claim that Figure 1 depicts a staircase. However, the results of experiments on members of African tribes whose culture does not include the custom of depicting three-dimensional objects by two-dimensional perspective drawings, nor staircases for that matter, indicate that members of those tribes would not see Figure 1 as a staircase at all. Again, it seems to follow that the perceptual experiences that individuals have in the act of seeing are not uniquely determined by the images on their retinas. Hanson (1958, chapter 1) contains some more captivating examples that illustrate this point.

另一个例子是儿童拼图游戏，游戏要求在一棵树的树叶图案中找出人脸。首先，观看者看到的，也就是他们主观感受到的，是一棵树，有树干、树枝和树叶。但一旦发现了人脸，情况就发生了变化。原本看到的树枝和树叶变成了人脸。同样，在解谜前后看到的都是同一个物体，而且可以推测，在解谜找到人脸的那一刻，观察者视网膜上的图像并没有改变。如果之后再看这幅画，已经解过一次谜题的观察者也能很快地看到人脸。看来，观察者的所见确实会受到其过往经验的影响。

Another instance is provided by a children’s picture puzzle that involves finding the drawing of a human face among the foliage in the drawing of a tree. Here, what is seen, that is, the subjective impressions experienced by a person viewing the drawing, at first corresponds to a tree, with trunk, branches and leaves. But this changes once the human face has been detected. What was once seen as branches and leaves is now seen as a human face. Again, the same physical object is viewed before and after the solution of the puzzle, and presumably the image on the observer’s retina does not change at the moment the puzzle is solved and the face found. If the picture is viewed at some later time, the face is readily and quickly seen by an observer who has already solved the puzzle once. It would seem that there is a sense in which what an observer sees is affected by his or her past experience.

有人可能会问：“这些人为的例子跟科学有什么关系？”对此，我们很容易就能从科学实践中找到例子来说明同样的观点，即观察者在观察物体或场景时所看到的、他们所经历的主观体验，并非仅仅由视网膜上的图像决定，还取决于观察者的经验、知识和预期。这一点隐含在一个不言而喻的认知中：在科学领域，人们必须学习如何成为一名合格的观察者。任何有过学习使用显微镜观察经历的人对此都深有体会。当初学者通过显微镜观察老师制作的玻片时，即使老师在同一台显微镜下观察同一张玻片时能够轻松辨认出相应的细胞结构，初学者也很难做到这一点。值得注意的是，在此背景下，显微镜学家一旦意识到应该观察什么，便能在适当的条件下观察到细胞分裂，而在此发现之前，这些细胞分裂过程却未被观察到。尽管我们现在知道，在许多通过显微镜观察的样本中，这些细胞分裂必然存在。迈克尔·波兰尼（Michael Polanyi，1973，第101页）描述了一名医学生在学习如何通过观察X光片进行诊断时，其感知体验的变化。

‘What’, it might well be suggested, ‘have these contrived examples got to do with science?’ In response, it is not difficult to produce examples from the practice of science that illustrate the same point, namely, that what observers see, the subjective experiences that they undergo, when viewing an object or scene is not determined solely by the images on their retinas but depends also on the experience, knowledge and expectations of the observer. The point is implicit in the uncontroversial realisation that one has to learn to be a competent observer in science. Anyone who has been through the experience of having to learn to see through a microscope will need no convincing of this. When the beginner looks at a slide prepared by an instructor through a microscope it is rare that the appropriate cell structures can be discerned, even though the instructor has no difficulty discerning them when looking at the same slide through the same microscope. It is significant to note, in this context, that microscopists found no great difficulty observing cells divide in suitably prepared circumstances once they were alert for what to look for, whereas prior to this discovery these cell divisions went unobserved, although we now know they must have been there to be observed in many of the samples examined through a microscope. Michael Polanyi (1973, p. 101) describes the changes in a medical student’s perceptual experience when he is taught to make a diagnosis by inspecting an X-ray picture.

想象一下，一位医学生正在学习肺部疾病的X光诊断课程。在昏暗的房间里，他看着贴在病人胸口的荧光屏上投射出的阴影，听着放射科医生用专业术语向助手们讲解这些阴影的重要特征。起初，这位学生完全摸不着头脑。因为他只能在胸部X光片上看到心脏和肋骨的阴影，以及它们之间零星的蛛网状斑点。专家们似乎在谈论他们想象中的事物；他根本看不懂他们在说什么。然而，几周后，他继续听讲，仔细观察着不断更新的不同病例的X光片，渐渐地，他开始有所领悟；他逐渐忘记了肋骨，开始看到肺部。最终，如果他坚持不懈地学习，一幅包含丰富细节的全景图将展现在他面前：生理变异和病理变化、瘢痕、慢性感染和急性疾病的迹象。他进入了一个全新的世界。他仍然只能看到专家们所看到内容的一小部分，但现在这些图片确实变得有意义了，而且大多数对图片的评论也变得有意义了。

Think of a medical student attending a course in the X-ray diagnosis of pulmonary diseases. He watches, in a darkened room, shadowy traces on a fluorescent screen placed against a patient’s chest, and hears the radiologist commenting to his assistants, in technical language, on the significant features of these shadows. At first, the student is completely puzzled. For he can see in the X-ray picture of a chest only the shadows of the heart and ribs, with a few spidery blotches between them. The experts seem to be romancing about figments of their imagination; he can see nothing that they are talking about. Then, as he goes on listening for a few weeks, looking carefully at ever-new pictures of different cases, a tentative understanding will dawn on him; he will gradually forget about the ribs and begin to see the lungs. And eventually, if he perseveres intelligently, a rich panorama of significant details will be revealed to him; of physiological variations and pathological changes, of scars, of chronic infections and signs of acute disease. He has entered a new world. He still sees only a fraction of what the experts can see, but the pictures are definitely making sense now and so do most of the comments made on them.

经验丰富的观察者和未经训练的新手在面对相同情境时，其感知体验并不相同。这与“感知是通过感官直接传递的”这一论断的字面理解相悖。

The experienced and skilled observer does not have perceptual experiences identical to those of the untrained novice when the two confront the same situation. This clashes with a literal understanding of the claim that perceptions are given in a straightforward way via the senses.

针对我提出的关于观察的观点，以及我所举的例子，一种常见的反驳是：观察者从同一地点观察同一场景，看到的是同一事物，但对所见之物的解读却各不相同。我对此持不同意见。就感知而言，观察者唯一能直接且即时接触的事物是其自身的经验。这些经验并非一成不变、独一无二，而是会随着观察者的知识和预期而变化。我承认，物理情境独有的，是观察者视网膜上的图像，但观察者与该图像之间并无直接的感知联系。当那些拥护普遍观点的人假定感知中存在某种独有的、可以被多种方式解读的东西时，他们实际上是在不加论证地假定，视网膜上的图像能够唯一地决定我们的感知经验，尽管有大量证据与之相悖。他们过度解读了相机的比喻。

A common response to the claim that I am making about observation, supported by the kinds of examples I have utilised, is that observers viewing the same scene from the same place see the same thing but interpret what they see differently. I wish to dispute this. As far as perception is concerned, the only things with which an observer has direct and immediate contact are his or her experiences. These experiences are not uniquely given and unchanging but vary with the knowledge and expectations possessed by the observer. What is uniquely given by the physical situation, I am prepared to admit, is the image on the retina of an observer, but an observer does not have direct perceptual contact with that image. When defenders of the common view assume that there is something unique given to us in perception that can be interpreted in various ways, they are assuming without argument, and in spite of much evidence to the contrary, that the images on our retinas uniquely determine out perceptual experiences. They are taking the camera analogy too far.

说了这么多，我想先澄清一下本节中我并非意在提出什么论点，以免被误解为论证超出我本意。首先，我当然不是说视网膜上图像的物理成因与我们所见毫无关系。我们不可能只看到自己想看到的东西。然而，尽管视网膜上的图像是造成我们所见之物的部分原因，但另一个非常重要的成因是我们内心或大脑的状态，而这种状态本身取决于我们的文化背景、知识水平和预期，并非仅仅由我们眼睛的物理特性和所观察的场景决定。其次，在各种情况下，我们所见之物都相当稳定。我们所见之物对内心或大脑状态的依赖程度并不高，不会使交流和科学研究变得不可能。第三，在本文引用的所有例子中，某种程度上所有观察者看到的都是同一件事。本书始终秉持并预设一个单一的、独特的物理世界独立于观察者而存在。因此，当多个观察者观察一幅图片、一件仪器、一张显微镜载玻片或其他任何事物时，在某种意义上，他们面对、观察并因此看到的是同一事物。但这并不意味着他们拥有完全相同的感知体验。在非常重要的意义上，他们看到的并非同一事物，而正是基于后一种意义，我对“事实能够毫无问题地、直接地通过感官传递给观察者”这一观点提出了一些质疑。至于这在多大程度上动摇了“足以用于科学研究的事实可以通过感官确立”这一观点，还有待进一步探讨。

Having said all this, let me try to make clear what I do not mean to be claiming in this section, lest I be taken to be arguing for more than I intend to be. First, I am certainly not claiming that the physical causes of the images on our retinas have nothing to do with what we see. We cannot see just what we like. However, although the images on our retinas form part of the cause of what we see, another very important part of the cause is the inner state of our minds or brains, which will itself depend on our cultural upbringing, our knowledge and our expectations, and will not be determined solely by the physical properties of our eyes and the scene observed. Second, under a wide variety of circumstances, what we see in various situations remains fairly stable. The dependence of what we see on the state of our minds or brains is not so sensitive as to make communication, and science, impossible. Third, in all the examples quoted here, there is a sense in which all observers see the same thing. I accept and presuppose throughout this book that a single, unique, physical world exists independently of observers. Hence, when a number of observers look at a picture, a piece of apparatus, a microscope slide or whatever, there is a sense in which they are confronted by, look at, and hence see, the same thing. But it does not follow from this that they have identical perceptual experiences. There is a very important sense in which they do not see the same thing, and it is that latter sense on which I base some of my queries concerning the view that facts are unproblematically and directly given to observers through the senses. To what extent this undermines the view that facts adequate for science can be established by the senses remains to be seen.

以陈述形式表达的可观察事实

Observable facts expressed as statements

在日常语言使用中，“事实”一词的含义是模糊的。它可以指表达事实的陈述，也可以指该陈述所描述的状态。例如，“月球上有山脉和陨石坑”是一个事实。这里的“事实”既可以理解为山脉或陨石坑本身，也可以理解为“月球上有山脉和陨石坑”这一陈述构成了事实。当人们声称科学建立在事实之上并从中推导而来时，显然后一种解释更为恰当。关于月球表面的知识并非建立在山脉和陨石坑之上并从中推导而来，而是建立在关于山脉和陨石坑的事实性陈述之上。

In normal linguistic usage, the meaning of ‘fact’ is ambiguous. It can refer to a statement that expresses the fact and it can also refer to the state of affairs referred to by such a statement. For example, it is a fact that there are mountains and craters on the moon. Here the fact can be taken as referring to the mountains or craters themselves. Alternatively, the statement ‘there are mountains and craters on the moon’ can be taken as constituting the fact. When it is claimed that science is based on and derived from the facts, it is clearly the latter interpretation that is appropriate. Knowledge about the moon’s surface is not based on and derived from mountains and craters but from factual statements about mountains and craters.

除了区分事实（理解为陈述）与这些陈述所描述的事物状态之外，显然也有必要区分事实陈述与可能导致人们接受这些陈述为事实的感知。例如，毫无疑问，达尔文在著名的“贝格尔号”航行中遇到了许多新的动植物物种，因此经历了一系列新的感知体验。然而，如果他止步于此，他对科学的贡献将微乎其微。只有当他将这些新发现形成陈述并提供给其他科学家时，他才对生物学做出了重大贡献。如果说“贝格尔号”航行产生了可以与进化论相关的新事实，那么构成这些事实的正是这些陈述。那些声称知识来源于事实的人，他们心中想的必然是陈述，而不是感知，也不是山脉和陨石坑之类的物体。

As well as distinguishing facts, understood as statements, from the states of affairs described by those statements, it is also clearly necessary to distinguish statements of facts from the perceptions that might occasion the acceptance of those statements as facts. For example, it is undoubtedly the case that when Darwin underwent his famous voyage on the Beagle he encountered many novel species of plant and animal, and so was subject to a range of novel perceptual experiences. However, he would have made no significant contribution to science had he left it at that. It was only when he had formulated statements describing the novelties and made them available to other scientists that he made a significant contribution to biology. To the extent that the voyage on the Beagle yielded novel facts to which an evolutionary theory could be related, it was statements that constituted those facts. For those who wish to claim that knowledge is derived from facts, they must have statements in mind, and neither perceptions nor objects like mountains and craters.

澄清了这一点之后，让我们回到本章第一节结尾处关于事实本质的论断(a)至(c)。一旦回到这些论断，它们本身就立刻显得问题重重。鉴于构成科学基础的事实必须以陈述的形式出现，那么认为事实是通过感官直接传递的说法就显得十分荒谬。即使我们暂且搁置上一节中提到的种种困难，并假设感知是在视觉行为中直接传递的，但显然，描述可观察事物状态的陈述（我称之为观察陈述）并非通过感官传递给观察者。认为事实陈述是通过感官进入大脑的想法是荒谬的。

With this clarification behind us, let us return to the claims (a) to (c) about the nature of facts which concluded the first section of this chapter. Once we do so they immediately become highly problematic as they stand. Given that the facts that might constitute a suitable basis for science must be in the form of statements, the claim that facts are given in a straightforward way via the senses begins to look quite misconceived. For even if we set aside the difficulties highlighted in the previous section, and assume that perceptions are straightforwardly given in the act of seeing, it is clearly not the case that statements describing observable states of affairs (I will call them observation statements) are given to observers via the senses. It is absurd to think that statements of fact enter the brain by way of the senses.

观察者在形成并认同观察陈述之前，必须具备相应的概念框架，并了解如何恰当地运用该框架。这一点在我们思考儿童学习描述（即对世界做出事实陈述）世界的方式时便显而易见。试想一下，一位家长教孩子认识和描述苹果。家长向孩子展示一个苹果，指着它，并说出“苹果”这个词。孩子很快就学会模仿并重复“苹果”这个词。掌握了这项技能后，也许有一天，孩子遇到了兄弟姐妹的网球，指着它说“苹果”。这时，家长会介入并解释说网球不是苹果，例如，演示网球不能像苹果一样咬。如果孩子再次犯错，例如把佛手瓜认作苹果，家长就需要更详细的解释。当孩子能够准确地说出“这里有个苹果”时，他/她已经对苹果有了相当多的了解。因此，认为我们必须先观察苹果的客观事实才能从中得出关于苹果的知识，这种想法似乎是错误的，因为恰当的客观事实，以陈述的形式表达出来，本身就预设了我们对苹果的大量了解。

Before an observer can formulate and assent to an observation statement, he or she must be in possession of the appropriate conceptual framework and a knowledge of how to appropriately apply it. That this is so becomes clear when we contemplate the way in which a child learns to describe (that is, make factual statements about) the world. Think of a parent teaching a child to recognise and describe apples. The parent shows the child an apple, points to it, and utters the word ‘apple’. The child soon learns to repeat the word ‘apple’ in imitation. Having mastered this particular accomplishment, perhaps on a later day the child encounters its sibling’s tennis ball, points and says ‘apple’. At this point the parent intervenes to explain that the ball is not an apple, demonstrating, for example, that one cannot bite it like an apple. Further mistakes by the child, such as the identification of a choko as an apple, will require somewhat more elaborate explanations from the parent. By the time the child can successfully say there is an apple present when there is one, it has learnt quite a lot about apples. So it would seem that it is a mistake to presume that we must first observe the facts about apples before deriving knowledge about them from those facts, because the appropriate facts, formulated as statements, presuppose quite a lot of knowledge about apples.

让我们从谈论儿童转向一些与我们理解科学更相关的例子。想象一下，一位经验丰富的植物学家和像我这样对植物学知之甚少的人一起参加一次澳大利亚丛林实地考察，目的是收集关于当地植物的可观察事实。毫无疑问，这位植物学家能够收集到比我观察和总结的更多、更详尽的事实，原因显而易见。植物学家拥有比我更完善的概念框架，这是因为他/她比我了解更多的植物学知识。植物学知识是形成观察陈述的前提，而这些陈述可能构成观察陈述的事实基础。

Let us move from talk of children to some examples that are more relevant to our task of understanding science. Imagine a skilled botanist accompanied by someone like myself who is largely ignorant of botany taking part in a field trip into the Australian bush, with the objective of collecting observable facts about the native flora. It is undoubtedly the case that the botanist will be capable of collecting facts that are far more numerous and discerning than those I am able to observe and formulate, and the reason is clear. The botanist has a more elaborate conceptual scheme to exploit than myself, and that is because he or she knows more botany than I do. A knowledge of botany is a prerequisite for the formulation of the observation statements that might constitute its factual basis.

因此，记录可观察的事实不仅仅是接收照射到眼睛的光线刺激，它还需要掌握相应的概念框架以及如何运用它。从这个意义上讲，假设（a）和（b）不能直接接受。事实陈述并非由感官刺激直接决定，观察陈述也预设了知识，因此我们不可能先确定事实，然后从中推导出知识。

Thus, the recording of observable facts requires more than the reception of the stimuli, in the form of light rays, that impinge on the eye. It requires the knowledge of the appropriate conceptual scheme and how to apply it. In this sense, assumptions (a) and (b) cannot be accepted as they stand. Statements of fact are not determined in a straightforward way by sensual stimuli, and observation statements presuppose knowledge, so it cannot be the case that we first establish the facts and then derive our knowledge from them.

为什么事实应该先于理论？

Why should facts precede theory?

我以一种相当极端的解读作为出发点，来理解“科学源于事实”这一论断。我认为它意味着，必须先确立事实，才能从中推导出科学知识。先确立事实，再构建理论来与之相符。然而，我们的感知在某种程度上依赖于我们已有的知识，进而依赖于我们的准备状态和预期（本章前面已讨论过），而且观察陈述本身也预设了相应的概念框架（上一节已讨论过），这些都表明，这种要求根本无法实现。事实上，一旦仔细审视，就会发现这是一个相当荒谬的想法，荒谬到我怀疑任何严肃的科学哲学家都不会愿意为之辩护。如果我们对所寻求的知识类型或试图解决的问题没有任何指导，又如何通过观察来确立关于世界的重要事实呢？为了做出可能对植物学做出重大贡献的观察，我首先需要掌握大量的植物学知识。此外，如果严格意义上的科学要求相关事实必须始终先于可能由其支撑的知识，那么用可观察的事实来检验我们科学知识的充分性这一理念本身就毫无意义。我们对相关事实的探寻需要以我们现有的知识水平为指导，例如，测量大气中不同位置的臭氧浓度可以获得相关事实，而测量悉尼青少年的平均头发长度则不能。因此，让我们放弃“获取事实必须先于构建构成科学知识的定律和理论”这一要求，看看我们这样做之后还能保留多少关于科学以事实为基础的理念。

I have taken as my starting point a rather extreme interpretation of the claim that science is derived from the facts. I have taken it to imply that the facts must be established prior to the derivation of scientific knowledge from them. First establish the facts and then build your theory to fit them. Both the fact that our perceptions depend to some extent on our prior knowledge and hence on our state of preparedness and our expectations (discussed earlier in the chapter) and the fact that observation statements presuppose the appropriate conceptual framework (discussed in the previous section) indicate that it is a demand that is impossible to live up to. Indeed, once it is subject to a close inspection it is a rather silly idea, so silly that I doubt if any serious philosopher of science would wish to defend it. How can we establish significant facts about the world through observation if we do not have some guidance as to what kind of knowledge we are seeking or what problems we are trying to solve? In order to make observations that might make a significant contribution to botany, I need to know much botany to start with. What is more, the very idea that the adequacy of our scientific knowledge should be tested against the observable facts would make no sense if, in proper science, the relevant facts must always precede the knowledge that might be supported by them. Our search for relevant facts needs to be guided by our current state of knowledge, which tells us, for example, that measuring the ozone concentration at various locations in the atmosphere yields relevant facts, whereas measuring the average hair length of the youths in Sydney does not. So let us drop the demand that the acquisition of facts should come before the formulation of the laws and theories that constitute scientific knowledge, and see what we can salvage of the idea that science is based on facts once we have done so.

根据我们修正后的立场，我们坦诚地承认，观察性陈述的形成预设了重要的知识基础，而科学中对相关可观察事实的探寻也正是以这些知识为指导。这两种承认并不必然削弱“知识具有由观察确立的事实基础”这一论断。首先，让我们来探讨一下，重要的观察性陈述的形成预设了对适当概念框架的了解。在此，我们注意到，拥有形成观察性陈述所需的概念资源是一回事，而这些陈述的真假则是另一回事。翻阅我的固体物理教科书，我可以摘录出两个观察性陈述：“金刚石的晶体结构具有反演对称性”和“在硫化锌晶体中，每个晶胞包含四个分子”。要形成和理解这些陈述，就必须具备一定的晶体结构知识及其表征方法。即使你不具备这些知识，你也能意识到，还有其他类似的陈述可以用相同的术语表达出来，例如“金刚石的晶体结构不具有反演对称性”和“硫化锌晶体的每个晶胞包含六个分子”。所有这些陈述都是观察性陈述，因为一旦掌握了相应的观察技巧，就可以通过观察来验证它们的真假。这样做之后，只有我从教科书中提取的陈述得到了观察的证实，而由这些陈述构建的其他陈述则被驳斥了。这说明，尽管知识对于构建重要的观察性陈述是必要的，但仍然无法确定哪些陈述能够被观察证实，哪些不能。因此，即使认识到描述这些事实的陈述依赖于知识，知识应该基于被观察证实的事实这一观点也并不会因此而动摇。只有当人们坚持认为，在获取任何知识之前，必须先确认与某些知识体系相关的事实时，才会出现问题。

According to our modified stand, we freely acknowledge that the formulation of observation statements presupposes significant knowledge, and that the search for relevant observable facts in science is guided by that knowledge. Neither acknowledgment necessarily undermines the claim that knowledge has a factual basis established by observation. Let us first take the point that the formulation of significant observation statements presupposes knowledge of the appropriate conceptual framework. Here we note that the availability of the conceptual resources for formulating observation statements is one thing. The truth or falsity of those statements is another. Looking at my solid state physics textbook, I can extract two observation statements, ‘the crystal structure of diamond has inversion symmetry’ and ‘in a crystal of zinc sulphide there are four molecules per unit cell’. A degree of knowledge about crystal structures and how they are characterised is necessary for the formulation and understanding of these statements. But even if you do not have that knowledge, you will be able to recognise that there are other, similar, statements that can be formulated using the same terms, statements such as ‘the crystal structure of diamond does not have inversion symmetry’ and ‘the crystal of zinc sulphide has six molecules per unit cell’. All of these statements are observation statements in the sense that once one has mastered the appropriate observational techniques their truth or falsity can be established by observation. When this is done, only the statements I extracted from my textbook are confirmed by observation, while the alternatives constructed from them are refuted. This illustrates the point that the fact that knowledge is necessary for the formulation of significant observation statements still leaves open the question of which of the statements so formulated are borne out by observation and which are not. Consequently, the idea that knowledge should be based on facts that are confirmed by observation is not undermined by the recognition that the formulation of the statements describing those facts are knowledge-dependent. There is only a problem if one sticks to the silly demand that the confirmation of facts relevant to some body of knowledge should precede the acquisition of any knowledge.

因此，即使承认寻找和阐述这些事实本身依赖于知识，科学知识应当建立在观察所确立的事实之上的这一观点也并非不成立。如果观察陈述的真假能够通过观察直接确定，那么，无论这些陈述是如何形成的，以这种方式得到证实的观察陈述似乎都能为科学知识提供重要的事实基础。

The idea that scientific knowledge should be based on facts established by observation need not be undermined, then, by the acknowledgment that the search for and formulation of those facts are knowledge-dependent. If the truth or falsity of observation statements can be established in a direct way by observation, then, irrespective of the way in which those statements came to be formulated, it would seem that the observation statements confirmed in this way provide us with a significant factual basis for scientific knowledge.

观察陈述的可靠性

The fallibility of observation statements

我们在探寻科学观测基础的本质方面取得了一些进展，但仍面临诸多挑战。前文的分析预设了观测陈述的真伪可以通过观测以一种毫无问题的方式得到可靠验证。然而，这样的预设是否合理呢？我们已经看到，不同的观测者在观察同一场景时未必拥有相同的感知，这会导致对可观测状态的认知出现分歧，从而引发诸多问题。科学史上的诸多案例充分证明了这一点的重要性，例如奈伊（Nye，1980）描述的关于所谓N射线效应是否可观测的争论，以及埃奇和穆尔凯（Edge and Mulkay，1976）描述的悉尼和剑桥天文学家在射电天文学早期对可观测事实的争论。我们至今尚未充分阐述如何在这些困难面前建立可靠的科学观测基础。关于科学观测基础可靠性的其他困难，源于我们对观测陈述是否充分的判断，而这种判断方式依赖于预设的知识，这使得这些判断本身就可能出错。我将举例说明这一点。

We have made some headway in our search for a characterisation of the observational base of science, but we are not out of trouble yet. In the previous section our analysis presupposed that the truth or otherwise of observation statements can be securely established by observation in an unproblematic way. But is such a presupposition legitimate? We have already seen ways in which problems can arise from the fact that different observers do not necessarily have the same perceptions when viewing the same scene, and this can lead to disagreements about what the observable states of affairs are. The significance of this point for science is borne out by well-documented cases in the history of science, such as the dispute about whether or not the effects of so-called N-rays are observable, described by Nye (1980), and the disagreement between Sydney and Cambridge astronomers over what the observable facts were in the early years of radio astronomy, as described by Edge and Mulkay (1976). We have as yet said little to show how a secure observational basis for science can be established in the face of such difficulties. Further difficulties concerning the reliability of the observational basis of science arise from some of the ways in which judgments about the adequacy of observation statements draw on presupposed knowledge in a way that renders those judgments fallible. I will illustrate this with examples.

亚里士多德将火列入构成所有地球物体的四大元素之一。火是一种独特的物质（尽管非常轻）的假设持续了数百年，直到现代化学才彻底推翻了它。那些基于这种预设进行研究的人认为，当他们观察火焰升腾时，就等于直接观察了火本身，因此对他们来说，“火上升了”这一观察陈述常常能被直接观察所证实。而我们现在摒弃了这种观察陈述。关键在于，如果我们用来描述观察结果的范畴所依据的知识本身存在缺陷，那么预设这些范畴的观察陈述也同样存在缺陷。

Aristotle included fire among the four elements of which all terrestrial objects are made. The assumption that fire is a distinctive substance, albeit a very light one, persisted for hundreds of years, and it took modern chemistry to thoroughly undermine it. Those who worked with this presupposition considered themselves to be observing fire directly when watching flames rise into the air, so that for them ‘the fire ascended’ is an observation statement that was frequently borne out by direct observation. We now reject such observation statements. The point is that if the knowledge that provides the categories we use to describe our observations is defective, the observation statements that presuppose those categories are similarly defective.

我的第二个例子是关于十六、十七世纪人们认识到的地球运动——它自转并绕太阳公转。在人们认识到这一点之前，“地球静止不动”的说法可以说是已被观察证实的。毕竟，我们既看不到也感觉不到地球的运动，而且如果我们跳到空中，地球也不会在我们脚下旋转。然而，从现代视角来看，尽管表面看来如此，我们仍然知道上述观察结论是错误的。我们理解惯性，也知道如果我们因为地球自转而以超过每秒一百米的速度水平运动，那么当我们跳到空中时，这个速度并没有改变。改变速度需要外力，而在我们的例子中，并没有水平方向的力作用于我们。因此，我们保持着与地球表面共享的水平速度，并落在我们起跳的地方。“地球静止不动”的说法并没有像人们曾经认为的那样，被可观察的证据所证实。但要充分理解个中缘由，我们需要了解惯性。这种理解是十七世纪的一项创新。我们有一个例子可以说明，对观察陈述的真假判断取决于构成判断背景的知识。看来，科学革命不仅涉及科学理论的渐进式变革，也涉及对可观察事实的认知变革！

My second example concerns the realisation, established in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, that the earth moves, spinning on its axis and orbiting the sun. Prior to the circumstances that made this realisation possible, it can be said that the statement ‘the earth is stationary’ was a fact confirmed by observation. After all, one cannot see or feel it move, and if we jump in the air, the earth does not spin away beneath us. We, from a modern perspective, know that the observation statement in question is false in spite of these appearances. We understand inertia, and know that if we are moving in a horizontal direction at over one hundred metres per second because the earth is spinning, there is no reason why that should change when we jump in the air. It takes a force to change speed, and, in our example, there are no horizontal forces acting. So we retain the horizontal speed we share with the earth’s surface and land where we took off. ‘The earth is stationary’ is not established by the observable evidence in the way it was once thought to be. But to fully appreciate why this is so, we need to understand inertia. That understanding was a seventeenth-century innovation. We have an example that illustrates a way in which the judgment of the truth or otherwise of an observation statement depends on the knowledge that forms the background against which the judgment is made. It would seem that the scientific revolution involved not just a progressive transformation of scientific theory, but also a transformation in what were considered to be the observable facts!

我的第三个例子进一步说明了最后一点。这个例子涉及从地球上观测到的金星和火星在一年中的大小变化。哥白尼认为地球绕太阳公转，其轨道位于金星轨道之外、火星轨道之内，因此金星和火星的视大小在一年中会发生显著变化。这是因为当地球位于太阳的同一侧时，它与其中一颗行星的距离相对较近；而当地球位于太阳的另一侧时，它与其中一颗行星的距离相对较远。如果从定量角度来考虑这个问题（正如哥白尼自己的理论版本中所述），这种影响是相当大的，火星的视直径预计会变化约八倍，金星的视直径预计会变化约六倍。然而，当用肉眼仔细观察行星时，金星的大小并没有变化，火星的大小变化也不超过两倍。因此，“金星的视大小在一年中不会发生变化”这一观测结果得到了直接证实，并在哥白尼的《天体运行论》序言中被提及，作为“历代经验”所证实的事实（邓肯，1976，第22页）。该序言的作者奥西安德对哥白尼理论的推论与我们“可观测事实”之间的冲突印象深刻，并以此论证哥白尼理论不应被字面理解。我们现在知道，用肉眼观测行星大小是具有欺骗性的，而且在黑暗背景下，人眼对于测量微小光源的大小是非常不可靠的。但正是伽利略指出了这一点，并证明如果通过望远镜观测金星和火星，就能清晰地辨别出预测的大小变化。这清晰地展现了知识和技术进步如何纠正了关于可观测事实的错误认知。这个例子本身并不特别，也并不神秘。但它表明，任何认为科学知识建立在观测所得事实之上的观点，都必须承认事实和知识本身都可能出错，需要修正；而且科学知识与其所依据的事实是相互依存的。

This last point is further illustrated by my third example. It concerns the sizes of the planets Venus and Mars as viewed from earth during the course of the year. It is a consequence of Copernicus’s suggestion that the earth circulates the sun, in an orbit outside that of Venus and inside that of Mars, that the apparent size of both Venus and Mars should change appreciably during the course of the year. This is because when the earth is around the same side of the sun as one of those planets it is relatively close to it, whereas when it is on the opposite side of the sun to one of them it is relatively distant from it. When the matter is considered quantitatively, as it can be within Copernicus’s own version of his theory, the effect is a sizeable one, with a predicted change in apparent diameter by a factor of about eight in the case of Mars and about six in the case of Venus. However, when the planets are observed carefully with the naked eye, no change in size can be detected for Venus, and Mars changes in size by no more than a factor of two. So the observation statement ‘the apparent size of Venus does not change size during the course of the year’ was straightforwardly confirmed, and was referred to in the Preface to Copernicus’s On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres as a fact confirmed ‘by all the experience of the ages’ (Duncan, 1976, p. 22). Osiander, who was the author of the Preface in question, was so impressed by the clash between the consequences of the Copernican theory and our ‘observable fact’ that he used it to argue that the Copernican theory should not be taken literally. We now know that the naked-eye observations of planetary sizes are deceptive, and that the eye is a very unreliable device for gauging the size of small light sources against a dark background. But it took Galileo to point this out and to show how the predicted change in size can be clearly discerned if Venus and Mars are viewed through a telescope. Here we have a clear example of the correction of a mistake about the observable facts made possible by improved knowledge and technology. In itself the example is unremarkable and non-mysterious. But it does show that any view to the effect that scientific knowledge is based on the facts acquired by observation must allow that the facts as well as the knowledge are fallible and subject to correction and that scientific knowledge and the facts on which it might be said to be based are interdependent.

我原本想用“科学源于事实”这句口号来表达的直觉是：科学知识之所以具有特殊地位，部分原因在于它建立在坚实的基础之上，即通过观察而确立的可靠事实。然而，本章的一些思考却对这种安心的观点构成了挑战。其中一个难题在于，观察者的认知在多大程度上受到其背景和预期的影响，因此，对一个人而言的可观察事实，对另一个人而言未必如此。第二个难题则源于，对观察陈述真伪的判断在多大程度上取决于已知的或预设的前提，这使得可观察的事实与支撑这些事实的前提一样，都可能出错。这两种难题都表明，科学的可观察基础或许并不像人们普遍认为的那样简单可靠。在下一章中，我将尝试通过更深入地探讨观察的本质，尤其是在科学领域中的运用，来在一定程度上缓解这些担忧。

The intuition that I intended to capture with my slogan ‘science is derived from the facts’ was that scientific knowledge has a special status in part because it is founded on a secure basis, solid facts firmly established by observation. Some of the considerations of this chapter pose a threat to this comfortable view. One difficulty concerns the extent to which perceptions are influenced by the background and expectations of the observer, so that what appears to be an observable fact for one need not be for another. The second source of difficulty stems from the extent to which judgments about the truth of observation statements depend on what is already known or assumed, thus rendering the observable facts as fallible as the presuppositions underlying them. Both kinds of difficulty suggest that maybe the observable basis for science is not as straightforward and secure as is widely and traditionally supposed. In the next chapter I try to mitigate these fears to some extent by considering the nature of observation, especially as it is employed in science, in a more discerning way than has been involved in our discussion up until now.

延伸阅读

Further reading

关于经验主义者如何看待知识，认为知识来源于感官所感知的信息，可参见洛克（1967）；关于逻辑实证主义者如何看待知识，可参见艾耶尔（1940）。汉弗林（1981）对逻辑实证主义进行了总体介绍，包括其对科学观察基础的论述。汉森（1958，第一章）在感知层面对这些观点提出了挑战。布朗（1977）和巴恩斯、布洛尔和亨利（1996，第一至三章）对整个问题进行了有益的讨论。

For a classic discussion of how knowledge is seen by an empiricist as derived from what is delivered to the mind via the senses, see Locke (1967), and by a logical positivist, see Ayer (1940). Hanfling (1981) is an introduction to logical positivism generally, including its account of the observational basis of science. A challenge to these views at the level of perception is Hanson (1958, chapter 1). Useful discussions of the whole issue are to be found in Brown (1977) and Barnes, Bloor and Henry (1996, chapters 1–3).

第二章

CHAPTER 2

观察作为一种实际干预手段

Observation as practical intervention

观察：被动且私密，还是主动且公开？

Observation: passive and private or active and public?

许多哲学家对观察的常见理解是将其视为一种被动的、私人的行为。之所以说它是被动的，是因为人们假定，例如，当我们观看时，我们只是睁开眼睛，调整视线，让信息流入，然后记录所看到的东西。正是观察者头脑或大脑中的感知本身，直接验证了事实，例如“我面前有一个红番茄”。如果这样理解，那么可观察事实的确立就成了一件非常私人的事情。它是通过个人在感知过程中仔细关注呈现在眼前的内容而完成的。由于两个观察者无法了解彼此的感知，他们就无法就各自假定确立的事实的有效性展开对话。

A common way in which observation is understood by a range of philosophers is to see it as a passive, private affair. It is passive insofar as it is presumed that when seeing, for example, we simply open and direct our eyes, let the information flow in, and record what is there to be seen. It is the perception itself in the mind or brain of the observer that is taken to directly validate the fact, which may be ‘there is a red tomato in front of me’ for example. If it is understood in this way, then the establishment of observable facts is a very private affair. It is accomplished by the individual closely attending to what is presented to him or her in the act of perception. Since two observers do not have access to each other’s perceptions, there is no way they can enter into a dialogue about the validity of the facts they are presumed to establish.

这种将感知或观察视为被动和私密的观点完全不充分，无法准确解释日常生活中的感知，更遑论科学领域。日常观察远非被动。为了验证感知的有效性，人们会采取一系列行动，其中许多行动是自动的，甚至可能是无意识的。在观察的过程中，我们会扫描物体，移动头部来检验所观察场景中预期的变化等等。如果我们不确定透过窗户看到的景象是窗外的景象还是窗户上的倒影，我们可以移动头部来检查这会对景象的可见方向产生什么影响。总的来说，如果我们出于任何原因怀疑基于感知得出的结论的真实性，我们可以采取各种措施来消除疑虑。例如，如果我们有理由怀疑番茄的图像是某种巧妙设计的光学图像，而不是真正的番茄，我们可以触摸它，也可以观察它，如有必要，我们还可以品尝它或解剖它。

This view of perception or observation, as passive and private, is totally inadequate, and does not give an accurate account of perception in everyday life, let alone science. Everyday observation is far from passive. There is a range of things that are done, many of them automatically and perhaps unconsciously, to establish the validity of a perception. In the act of seeing we scan objects, move our heads to test for expected changes in the observed scene and so on. If we are not sure whether a scene viewed through a window is something out of the window or a reflection in the window, we can move our heads to check for the effect this has on the direction in which the scene is visible. It is a general point that if for any reason we doubt the validity of what seems to be the case on the basis of our perceptions, there are various actions we can take to remove the problem. If, in the example above, we have reason to suspect that the image of the tomato is some cleverly contrived optical image rather than a real tomato, we can touch it as well as look at it, and if necessary we can taste it or dissect it.

通过这些略显粗浅的观察，我仅仅触及了心理学家能够讲述的关于个体在感知行为中所做种种活动的详尽故事的冰山一角。对我们而言，更重要的是思考这一点对于观察在科学中的作用有何意义。显微镜在科学中的早期应用就是一个很好的例子。当罗伯特·胡克和亨利·鲍尔等科学家使用显微镜观察苍蝇和蚂蚁等小型昆虫时，他们常常对可观察到的事实产生分歧，至少在最初阶段是如此。胡克将一些分歧的根源追溯到不同的照明方式。他指出，在一种光线下，苍蝇的眼睛看起来像一个布满小孔的网格（顺便一提，这似乎让鲍尔相信事实的确如此），在另一种光线下，它看起来像一个布满圆锥的表面，而在另一种光线下，它又看起来像一个布满金字塔的表面。胡克随后采取了一些实际措施来解决这个问题。他力图通过均匀照射标本来消除眩光和复杂反射造成的虚假信息。他采用的方法是，用蜡烛的光线透过盐水扩散开来照明。他还从不同方向照射标本，以确定哪些特征在这些变化下保持不变。有些昆虫需要用白兰地彻底麻醉，才能使其静止不动且不受损伤。

With these few, somewhat elementary, observations I have only touched the surface of the detailed story psychologists can tell about the range of things that are done by individuals in the act of perception. More important for our task is to consider the significance of the point for the role of observation in science. An example that illustrates my point well is drawn from early uses of the microscope in science. When scientists such as Robert Hooke and Henry Power used the microscope to look at small insects such as flies and ants, they often disagreed about the observable facts, at least initially. Hooke traced the cause of some of the disagreements to different kinds of illumination. He pointed out that the eye of a fly appears like a lattice covered with holes in one kind of light (which, incidentally, seems to have led Power to believe that this was indeed the case), like a surface covered with cones in another and in yet another light like a surface covered with pyramids. Hooke proceeded to make practical interventions designed to clear up the problem. He endeavoured to eliminate spurious information arising from dazzle and complicated reflections by illuminating specimens uniformly. He did this by using for illumination the light of a candle diffused through a solution of brine. He also illuminated his specimens from various directions to determine which features remained invariant under such changes. Some of the insects needed to be thoroughly intoxicated with brandy to render them both motionless and undamaged.

胡克的著作《显微图谱》（1665年）包含许多基于胡克的行动和观察而得出的详细描述和图画。这些成果是公开的，而非私密的。其他人可以对其进行检验、批评和补充。如果苍蝇的复眼在某些光照条件下看起来布满了孔洞，那么仔细观察的观察者就无法有效地评估这种状况。胡克展示了如何检验此类情况下的表象真实性，他所推荐的方法可以由任何有意愿或技能的人执行。最终获得的关于苍蝇复眼结构的观察事实，源于一个积极且公开的过程。

Hooke’s book, Micrographia (1665), contains many detailed descriptions and drawings that resulted from Hooke’s actions and observations. These productions were and are public, not private. They can be checked, criticised and added to by others. If a fly’s eye, in some kinds of illumination, appears to be covered with holes, then that state of affairs cannot be usefully evaluated by the observer closely attending to his or her perceptions. Hooke showed what could be done to check the authenticity of the appearances in such cases, and the procedures he recommended could be carried out by anyone suitably inclined or skilled. The observable facts about the structure of a fly’s eye that eventuate result from a process that is both active and public.

采取行动探究作为可观察事实提出的论断是否充分，这一观点意味着感知的主观性并非科学难以解决的问题。前一章已讨论过，由于观察者的背景、文化和预期不同，他们对同一场景的感知也会有所差异。这一毋庸置疑的事实所引发的问题，可以通过采取适当的行动在很大程度上得到解决。众所周知，个人的感知判断可能由于各种原因而不可靠。科学面临的挑战在于，如何安排可观察的情境，从而最大限度地减少甚至消除对这类判断的依赖。以下示例将阐明这一点。

The point that action can be taken to explore the adequacy of claims put forward as observable facts has the consequence that subjective aspects of perception need not be an intractable problem for science. Ways in which perceptions of the same scene can vary from observer to observer depending on their background, culture and expectations were discussed in the previous chapter. Problems that eventuate from this undoubted fact can be countered to a large extent by taking appropriate action. It should be no news to anyone that the perceptual judgments of individuals can be unreliable for a range of reasons. The challenge, in science, is to arrange the observable situation in such a way that the reliance on such judgments is minimised if not eliminated. An example will illustrate the point.

月亮错觉是一种常见的现象。当月亮高悬于天际时，它看起来比在地平线附近时小得多。这是一种错觉。在月亮相对位置发生所需变化的几个小时内，月亮的大小和与地球的距离都不会改变。然而，我们不必依赖对月亮大小的主观判断。例如，我们可以安装一个带有十字线的瞄准管，以便通过刻度读取其方向。通过依次将十字线对准月亮的两侧，并记录相应刻度读数的​​差异，即可确定月亮在观测点的张角。我们可以在月亮高悬于天际时进行此操作，然后在月亮接近地平线时重复此操作。月亮的视大小保持不变，这体现在两种情况下刻度读数的​​差异没有显著变化。

The moon illusion is a common phenomenon. When it is high in the sky, the moon appears much smaller than when it is low on the horizon. This is an illusion. The moon does not change size nor does its distance from earth alter during the few hours that it takes for its relative position to undergo the required change. However, we do not have to put our trust in subjective judgments about the moon’s size. We can, for example, mount a sighting tube fitted with cross-wires in such a way that its orientation can be read on a scale. The angle subtended by the moon at the place of sighting can be determined by aligning the cross-wires with each side of the moon in turn and noting the difference in the corresponding scale readings. This can be done when the moon is high in the sky and repeated when it is near the horizon. The fact that the apparent size of the moon has remained unchanged is reflected in the fact that there is no significant variation in the differences between the scale readings in the two cases.

伽利略和木星的卫星

Galileo and the moons of Jupiter
