本节将通过一个历史实例来说明上一节讨论的意义。1609 年末，伽利略制造了一架强大的望远镜，并用它观测星空。在接下来的三个月里，他所做的许多新发现都引发了争议，并且与当时关于哥白尼日心说有效性的天文辩论密切相关，而伽利略正是哥白尼日心说的坚定拥护者。例如，伽利略声称他观测到了木星的四颗卫星，但他很难说服其他人相信他的观测结果。这件事意义重大。哥白尼日心说的核心观点是地球在运动，它每天自转一周，每年绕太阳公转一周。在上个世纪上半叶，人们普遍认为地球是静止的，太阳和行星围绕地球运行，而哥白尼挑战了这一观点。反对地球运动的众多论点中，有一个绝非无关紧要：如果地球像哥白尼所说的那样绕太阳公转，那么月球就会被抛在后面。然而，一旦承认木星有卫星，这个论点就站不住脚了。因为即使是哥白尼的反对者也承认木星在运动。因此，木星的任何卫星都会被它带动，这恰恰证明了哥白尼的反对者声称地球不可能出现这种现象。

In this section the relevance of the discussion in the previous section is illustrated with a historical example. Late in 1609 Galileo constructed a powerful telescope and used it to look at the heavens. Many of the novel observations he made in the ensuing three months were controversial, and very relevant to the astronomical debate concerning the validity of the Copernican theory, of which Galileo became an avid champion. Galileo claimed, for instance, to have sighted four moons orbiting the planet Jupiter, but he had trouble convincing others of the validity of his observations. The matter was of some moment. The Copernican theory involved the controversial claim that the earth moves, spinning on its axis once a day and orbiting the sun once a year. The received view that Copernicus had challenged in the first half of the previous century was that the earth is stationary, with the sun and planets orbiting it. One of the many, far from trivial, arguments against the motion of the earth was that, if it orbited the sun as Copernicus claimed, the moon would be left behind. This argument is undermined once it is acknowledged that Jupiter has moons. For even the opponents of Copernicus agreed that Jupiter moves. Consequently, any moons it has are carried with it, exhibiting the very phenomenon that the opponents of Copernicus claimed to be impossible in the case of the earth.

伽利略用望远镜观测木星卫星是否有效，在当时是一个备受关注的问题。尽管最初人们持怀疑态度，而且他的许多同时代人似乎也无法通过望远镜辨认出这些卫星，但伽利略在短短两年内就说服了他的竞争对手。让我们来看看他是如何做到这一点的——他是如何“客观化”他对木星卫星的观测结果的。

Whether Galileo’s telescopic observations of moons around Jupiter were valid was a question of some moment then. In spite of the initial skepticism, and the apparent inability of a range of his contemporaries to discern the moons through the telescope, Galileo had convinced his rivals within a period of two years. Let us see how he was able to achieve that – how he was able to ‘objectify’ his observations of Jupiter’s moons.

伽利略将一个刻度尺用一个环固定在望远镜上，刻度尺上标有等距的水平线和垂直线，使刻度尺正面朝向观测者，并可沿望远镜上下滑动。观测者用一只眼睛透过望远镜观察，另一只眼睛则可观察刻度尺。为了便于瞄准，他用一盏小灯照亮了刻度尺。将望远镜对准木星后，他沿着望远镜滑动刻度尺，直到一只眼睛透过望远镜看到的木星图像与另一只眼睛看到的刻度尺中心方格重合。这样，就可以通过刻度尺读取望远镜中观测到的卫星的位置，读数对应于该卫星与木星的距离，以木星直径的倍数表示。木星直径是一个方便的单位，因为用它作为标准会自动考虑木星视直径随其远离地球而变化的情况。

Galileo attached a scale, marked with equally spaced horizontal and vertical lines, to his telescope by a ring in such a way that the scale was face-on to the observer and could be slid up and down the length of the telescope. A viewer looking through the telescope with one eye could view the scale with the other. Sighting of the scale was facilitated by illuminating it with a small lamp. With the telescope trained on Jupiter, the scale was slid along the telescope until the image of Jupiter viewed through the telescope with one eye lay in the central square of the scale viewed with the other eye. With this accomplished, the position of a moon viewed through the telescope could be read on the scale, the reading corresponding to its distance from Jupiter in multiples of the diameter of Jupiter. The diameter of Jupiter was a convenient unit, since employing it as a standard automatically allowed for the fact that its apparent diameter as viewed from earth varies as that planet approaches and recedes from the earth.

利用这种方法，伽利略得以记录木星周围四颗“小星星”的每日运行轨迹。他证明，这些数据与“小星星”确实是木星的卫星，并以恒定周期绕其运行的假设相符。这一假设不仅得到了定量测量的证实，也得到了定性观察的佐证：当这些卫星从木星后方或前方经过，或进入木星阴影时，它们会偶尔从视野中消失。

Using this technique, Galileo was able to record the daily histories of the four ‘starlets’ accompanying Jupiter. He was able to show that the data were consistent with the assumption that the starlets were indeed moons orbiting Jupiter with a constant period. The assumption was borne out, not only by the quantitative measurements but also by the more qualitative observation that the satellites occasionally disappeared from view as they passed behind or in front of the parent planet or moved into its shadow.

尽管木星的卫星肉眼不可见，伽利略仍然有充分的理由来证明其观测结果的真实性。他能够也确实反驳了卫星是望远镜造成的错觉的说法，指出这种说法难以解释为什么卫星只出现在木星附近，而其他地方却看不到。伽利略还可以援引其测量结果的一致性和可重复性，以及这些结果与卫星以恒定周期绕木星运行的假设相符。伽利略的定量数据得到了独立观测者的验证，其中包括罗马学院和罗马教廷的观测者，他们都是哥白尼理论的反对者。此外，伽利略还能预测卫星的后续位置以及凌日和日食的发生，这些预测也得到了他本人和其他独立观测者的证实，正如斯蒂尔曼·德雷克（Stillman Drake，1978，第175-176页，236-237页）所记载的那样。

Galileo was in a strong position to argue for the veracity of his observations of Jupiter’s moons, in spite of the fact that they were invisible to the naked eye. He could, and did, argue against the suggestion that they were an illusion produced by the telescope by pointing out that that suggestion made it difficult to explain why the moons appeared near Jupiter and nowhere else. Galileo could also appeal to the consistency and repeatability of his measurements and their compatibility with the assumption that the moons orbit Jupiter with a constant period. Galileo’s quantitative data were verified by independent observers, including observers at the Collegio Romano and the Court of the Pope in Rome who were opponents of the Copernican theory. What is more, Galileo was able to predict further positions of the moons and the occurrence of transits and eclipses, and these too were confirmed by himself and independent observers, as documented by Stillman Drake (1978, pp. 175–6, 236–7).

伽利略用望远镜观测到的木星卫星的真实性很快就被他同时代那些具备观测能力的人所接受，甚至包括那些最初反对他的人。诚然，有些观测者始终无法辨认出这些卫星，但我认为这与詹姆斯·瑟伯（1933，第101-103页）无法通过显微镜辨认出植物细胞的结构一样，都无关紧要。伽利略论证其用望远镜观测木星卫星的真实性，在于他的说法经受住了各种实际的、客观的检验。尽管他的论证或许还不够确凿，但它比任何支持另一种观点的论证都更有说服力，即认为他的观测结果是错觉或望远镜造成的假象。

The veracity of the telescopic sightings was soon accepted by those of Galileo’s contemporaries who were competent observers, even by those who had initially opposed him. It is true that some observers could never manage to discern the moons, but I suggest that this is of no more significance than the inability of James Thurber (1933, pp. 101–3) to discern the structure of plant cells through a microscope. The strength of Galileo’s case for the veracity of his telescopic observations of the moons of Jupiter derives from the range of practical, objective tests that his claims could survive. Although his case might have stopped short of being absolutely conclusive, it was incomparably stronger than any that could be made for the alternative, namely, that his sightings were illusions or artifacts brought about by the telescope.

可观察的事实客观但易出错

Observable facts objective but fallible

为了从我们对“可观察事实”概念的批评中拯救出一个相对有力的版本，我们可以尝试以下思路。如果一个观察陈述能够通过感官直接检验，并且经得起这些检验，那么它就构成了一个值得作为科学基础的事实。这里的“直接”指的是，候选的观察陈述应该能够通过常规的、客观的程序来检验其有效性，而无需观察者做出精细的、主观的判断。强调检验凸显了验证观察陈述的积极性和公开性。通过这种方式，或许我们可以捕捉到一个可以通过观察而毫无争议地确立的事实概念。毕竟，只有那些对哲学极其痴迷的人才会花时间去怀疑诸如仪表读数之类的东西是否能够通过仔细运用视觉，在一定的误差范围内得到可靠的确定。

An attempt to rescue a reasonably strong version of what constitutes an observable fact from the criticisms that we have levelled at that notion might go along the following lines. An observation statement constitutes a fact worthy of forming part of the basis for science if it is such that it can be straightforwardly tested by the senses and withstands those tests. Here the ‘straightforward’ is intended to capture the idea that candidate observation statements should be such that their validity can be tested in ways that involve routine, objective procedures that do not necessitate fine, subjective judgments on the part of the observer. The emphasis on tests brings out the active, public character of the vindication of observation statements. In this way, perhaps we can capture a notion of fact unproblematically established by observation. After all, only a suitably addicted philosopher will wish to spend time doubting that such things as meter readings can be securely established, within some small margin of error, by careful use of the sense of sight.

前一段提出的“可观察事实”概念需要付出一定的代价。这个代价就是，可观察事实在某种程度上是会出错的，并且需要修正。如果一个陈述因为通过了迄今为止所有可能的检验而被认定为可观察事实，但这并不意味着它必然能够经受住随着知识和技术进步而出现的新型检验。我们已经遇到了两个重要的例子，这两个观察陈述最初被认为是事实，但最终却因为这些进步而被推翻，分别是“地球是静止的”和“火星和金星的视大小在一年中变化不大”。

A small price has to be paid for the notion of an observable fact put forward in the previous paragraph. That price is that observable facts are to some degree fallible and subject to revision. If a statement qualifies as an observable fact because it has passsed all the tests that can be levelled at it hitherto, this does not mean that it will necessarily survive new kinds of tests that become possible in the light of advances in knowledge and technology. We have already met two significant examples of observation statements that were accepted as facts on good grounds but were eventually rejected in the light of such advances, namely, ‘the earth is stationary’ and ‘the apparent size of Mars and Venus does not change appreciably during the course of the year’.

根据本文提出的观点，构成科学知识基础的观测结果既是客观的，也是易错的。它们之所以客观，是因为它们可以通过简单的程序进行公开检验；它们之所以易错，是因为它们可能会被科学技术进步带来的新型检验方法所推翻。伽利略的著作可以很好地说明这一点。在他的《关于两大世界体系的对话》（1967年，第361-363页）中，伽利略描述了一种测量恒星直径的客观方法。他在自己和恒星之间悬挂了一根绳子，绳子的距离刚好遮挡住恒星。伽利略认为，此时绳子在人眼中所成的角度等于恒星在人眼中所成的角度。我们现在知道，伽利略的结果是错误的。我们感知到的恒星视大小完全是由大气和其他噪声效应造成的，与恒星的实际大小没有任何确定的关系。伽利略对恒星大小的测量基于一些现已被否定的隐含假设。但这种否定与主观感知无关。伽利略的观测是客观的，因为它们采用了常规程序，即使今天重复这些程序，也能得到与伽利略当年所得结果大致相同的结果。在下一章中，我们将进一步阐述科学缺乏绝对可靠的观测基础并非仅仅源于主观感知。

According to the view put forward here, observations suitable for constituting a basis for scientific knowledge are both objective and fallible. They are objective insofar as they can be publicly tested by straightforward procedures, and they are fallible insofar as they may be undermined by new kinds of tests made possible by advances in science and technology. This point can be illustrated by another example from the work of Galileo. In his Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems (1967, pp. 361–3) Galileo described an objective method for measuring the diameter of a star. He hung a cord between himself and the star at a distance such that the cord just blocked out the star. Galileo argued that the angle subtended at the eye by the cord was then equal to the angle subtended at the eye by the star. We now know that Galileo’s results were spurious. The apparent size of a star as perceived by us is due entirely to atmospheric and other noise effects and has no determinate relation to the star’s physical size. Galileo’s measurements of star-size rested on implicit assumptions that are now rejected. But this rejection has nothing to do with subjective aspects of perception. Galileo’s observations were objective in the sense that they involved routine procedures which, if repeated today, would give much the same results as obtained by Galileo. In the next chapter we will have cause to develop further the point that the lack of an infallible observational base for science does not derive solely from subjective aspects of perception.

延伸阅读

Further reading

关于科学经验基础（即经得起检验的陈述）的经典论述，请参见波普尔（1972，第五章）。哈金（1983）的后半部分、波普尔（1979，第341-361页）以及查尔默斯（1990，第四章）都强调了观察的主动性。此外，沙佩尔（1982）的著作也值得参考。

For a classic discussion of the empirical basis of science as those statements that withstand tests, see Popper (1972, chapter 5). The active aspects of observation are stressed in the second half of Hacking (1983), in Popper (1979, pp. 341–61) and in Chalmers (1990, chapter 4). Also of relevance is Shapere (1982).

第三章

CHAPTER 3

实验

Experiment

不仅是事实，而且是相关的事实

Not just facts but relevant facts

在本章中，为了论证的需要，我假设通过仔细运用感官可以确立可靠的事实。毕竟，正如我之前所指出的，在与科学相关的诸多情境中，这一假设无疑是合理的。例如，数盖革计数器的咔嗒声，以及记录秤上指针的位置，都是简单易懂的例子。然而，这些事实的存在是否就能解决我们关于科学事实基础的问题呢？我们假设可以通过观察确立的那些陈述，是否就构成了科学知识所依据的事实呢？在本章中，我们将看到，这些问题的答案是明确的“否”。

In this chapter I assume for the sake of argument that secure facts can be established by careful use of the senses. After all, as I have already suggested, there is a range of situations relevant to science where this assumption is surely justified. Counting clicks on a Geiger counter and noting the position of a needle on a scale are unproblematic examples. Does the availability of such facts solve our problem about the factual basis for science? Do the statements that we assume can be established by observation constitute the facts from which scientific knowledge can be derived? In this chapter we will see that the answer to these questions is a decisive ‘no’.

需要指出的一点是，科学需要的不仅仅是事实，而是相关的事实。绝大多数可以通过观察确定的事实，例如我办公室里的书的数量或邻居汽车的颜色，与科学完全无关，科学家们收集这些事实纯属浪费时间。哪些事实与某一学科相关，哪些事实不相关，取决于该学科当前的进展阶段。科学提出问题，理想情况下，观察可以提供答案。这便是“何为科学相关的事实”这一问题的答案之一。

One point that should be noted is that what is needed in science is not just facts but relevant facts. The vast majority of facts that can be established by observation, such as the number of books in my office or the colour of my neighbour’s car, are totally irrelevant for science, and scientists would be wasting their time collecting them. Which facts are relevant and which are not relevant to a science will be relative to the current state of development of that science. Science poses the questions, and ideally observation can provide answers. This is part of the answer to the question of what constitutes a relevant fact for science.

然而，还有更重要的观点需要阐述，我将用一个故事来引出它。小时候，我和哥哥曾就一个现象争论不休：为什么田里牛粪周围的草比其他地方长得更高？当然，我们肯定不是第一个注意到这个现象的人。哥哥认为这是牛粪的肥力作用，而我则怀疑是牛粪的覆盖作用，它能锁住水分，抑制蒸发。现在我强烈怀疑我们俩的解释都不完全正确，主要原因可能是牛不太愿意吃自己粪便周围的草。或许这三种因素都起到了一定的作用，但仅凭我和哥哥当年的观察，我们无法分辨它们各自的影响程度。需要采取一些干预措施，例如，将牛群关在田地外一个季节，看看这是否能减少或消除牛粪中较长的杂草；或者将牛粪磨碎，以消除覆盖效果但保留施肥效果，等等。

However, there is a more substantial point to be made, which I will introduce with a story. When I was young, my brother and I disagreed about how to explain the fact that the grass grows longer among the cow pats in a field than elsewhere in the same field, a fact that I am sure we were not the first to notice. My brother was of the opinion that it was the fertilising effect of the dung that was responsible, whereas I suspected that it was a mulching effect, the dung trapping moisture beneath it and inhibiting evaporation. I now have a strong suspicion that neither of us was entirely right and that the main explanation is simply that cows are disinclined to eat the grass around their own dung. Presumably all three of these effects play some role, but it is not possible to sort out the relative magnitudes of the effects by observations of the kind made by my brother and me. Some intervention would be necessary, such as, for example, locking the cows out of a field for a season to see if this reduced or eliminated the longer growth among the cow pats, by grinding the dung in such a way that the mulching effect is eliminated but the fertilising effect retained, and so on.

这里所举的例子很典型。我们周围的世界里存在着许多不同的过程，它们彼此叠加、相互作用，错综复杂。一片落叶会受到重力、空气阻力和风力的影响，并且在下落过程中也会发生一定程度的腐烂。仅仅通过仔细观察这些自然发生的事件，是无法理解这些不同过程的。观察落叶并不能得出伽利略的落体定律。由此可知，要获得与识别和阐明自然界各种过程相关的知识，通常需要进行实际的干预，以分离出正在研究的过程并消除其他过程的影响。简而言之，必须进行实验。

The situation exemplified here is typical. Many kinds of processes are at work in the world around us, and they are all superimposed on, and interact with, each other in complicated ways. A falling leaf is subject to gravity, air resistance and the force of winds and will also rot to some small degree as it falls. It is not possible to arrive at an understanding of these various processes by careful observation of events as they typically and naturally occur. Observation of falling leaves will not yield Galileo’s law of fall. The lesson to be learnt here is rather straightforward. To acquire facts relevant for the identification and specification of the various processes at work in nature it is, in general, necessary to practically intervene to try to isolate the process under investigation and eliminate the effects of others. In short, it is necessary to do experiments.

我们花了些时间才得出这个结论，但或许显而易见的是，如果科学的基础是事实，那么这些事实必然是实验结果，而非任何可观察的客观事实。尽管这一点显而易见，但直到近二十年来，科学哲学家们才开始认真审视实验的本质及其在科学中的作用。事实上，本书的前几版很少关注这个问题。一旦我们将重点放在实验而非单纯的观察上，以此作为科学的基础，我们一直在讨论的问题就会呈现出不同的面貌，正如我们将在本章剩余部分看到的那样。

It has taken us a while to get to this point, but it should perhaps be somewhat obvious that if there are facts that constitute the basis for science, then those facts come in the form of experimental results rather than any old observable facts. As obvious as this might be, it is not until the last couple of decades that philosophers of science have taken a close look at the nature of experiment and the role it plays in science. Indeed, it is an issue that was given little attention in the previous editions of this book. Once we focus on experiment rather than mere observation as supplying the basis for science, the issues we have been discussing take on a somewhat different light, as we shall see in the remainder of this chapter.

实验结果的产生和更新

The production and updating of experimental results

实验结果绝非唾手可得。任何实验人员，乃至任何理科学生都知道，让实验成功进行绝非易事。一项意义重大的新实验可能需要数月甚至数年才能成功完成。我本人在20世纪60年代作为实验物理学家的经历可以很好地说明这一点。读者是否理解故事的细节并不重要。我的目的仅仅是让读者了解实验结果的产生过程中所涉及的复杂性和实际困难。

Experimental results are by no means straightforwardly given. As any experimentalist, and indeed any science student, knows, getting an experiment to work is no easy matter. A significant new experiment can take months or even years to successfully execute. A brief account of my own experiences as an experimental physicist in the 1960s will illustrate the point nicely. It is of no great importance whether the reader follows the detail of the story. I simply aim to give some idea of the complexity and practical struggle involved in the production of an experimental result.

我的实验目的是使低能电子从分子中散射出来，从而确定它们在散射过程中损失了多少能量，进而获得与分子自身能级相关的信息。为了实现这一目标，必须产生一束速度相同、能量也相同的电子束。必须确保这些电子在进入探测器之前只与一个目标分子发生碰撞，否则所需信息将会丢失。此外，还需要使用设计合适的探测器来测量散射电子的速度（或能量）。这些步骤中的每一个都极具挑战性。速度选择器由两块弯曲成同心圆的导电板组成，两板之间存在电势差。只有当电子的速度与两板间的电势差相匹配时，它们才能从圆周通道的另一端射出。否则，它们会被偏转到导电板上。为了确保电子几乎只与一个目标分子碰撞，实验必须在高度抽真空的环境中进行，该区域内含有低压的目标气体样品。这需要将现有的真空技术发挥到极致。散射电子的速度将通过类似于产生单能电子束的圆形电极阵列进行测量。通过设置电极间的电势差，使只有具有特定速度的电子才能穿过圆周并从分析器的另一端射出，即可测量特定速度散射电子的强度。检测射出的电子需要测量极其微小的电流，这再次考验了现有技术的极限。

The aim of my experiment was to scatter low-energy electrons from molecules to find out how much energy they lost in the process, thereby gaining information related to the energy levels in the molecules themselves. To reach this objective, it was necessary to produce a beam of electrons that all moved at the same velocity and hence had the same energy. It was necessary to arrange for them to collide with one target molecule only before entering the detector, otherwise the sought-for information would be lost, and it was necessary to measure the velocity, or energy, of the scattered electrons with a suitably designed detector. Each of these steps posed a practical challenge. The velocity selector involved two conducting plates bent into concentric circles with a potential difference between them. Electrons entering between the plates would only emerge from the other end of the circular channel if they had a velocity that matched the potential difference between the plates. Otherwise they would be deflected onto the conducting plates. To ensure that the electrons were likely to collide with only one target molecule it was necessary to do the experiment in a region that was highly evacuated, containing a sample of the target gas at very low pressure. This required pushing the available vacuum technology to its limits. The velocity of scattered electrons was to be measured by an arrangement of circular electrodes similar to that used in producing the mono-energetic beam. The intensity of electrons scattered with a particular velocity could be measured by setting the potential difference between the plates to a value that allowed only the electrons with that velocity to traverse the circle and emerge at the other end of the analyser. Detecting the emerging electrons involved measuring a minutely small current that again pushed the available technology to its limits.

大致思路就是这样，但每一步都遇到了一系列实际问题，任何从事过类似领域工作的人都会对此感到熟悉。要清除装置中各种金属释放出的有害气体非常困难。这些气体分子被电子束电离后，会在电极上凝结，造成虚假电势。我们的美国同行发现，给电极镀金可以大大减少这些问题。我们发现，用一种名为“aquadag”的碳基溶剂涂覆电极也很有帮助，虽然不如镀金有效，但更符合我们的研究预算。我的耐心（以及我的研究经费）在实验取得显著成果之前就耗尽了。据我所知，在最终获得重要结果之前，还有几位研究生也遭遇了同样的挫折。如今，几十年过去了，低能电子能谱技术已成为一项相当标准的技术。

That was the general idea, but each step presented a range of practical problems of a sort that will be familiar to anyone who has worked in this kind of field. It was very difficult to rid the apparatus of unwanted gases that were emitted from the various metals from which the apparatus was made. Molecules of these gases that were ionised by the electron beam could coagulate on the electrodes and cause spurious electric potentials. Our American rivals found that gold-plating the electrodes helped greatly to minimise these problems. We found that coating them with a carbon-based solvent called ‘aquadag’ was a big help, not quite as effective as gold-plating but more in keeping with our research budget. My patience (and my research scholarship) ran out well before this experiment was made to yield significant results. I understand that a few more research students came to grief before significant results were eventually obtained. Now, decades later, low-energy electron spectroscopy is a pretty standard technique.

我以及那些比我更成功的继任者们所做的努力的细节并不重要。我所说的应该足以阐明一个毋庸置疑的观点。如果实验结果构成了科学的基础，那么它们绝非感官所能直接感知。它们需要通过努力才能获得，其确立需要大量的专业知识、实践中的反复试验以及对现有技术的运用。

The details of my efforts, and those of my successors who were more successful, are not important. What I have said should be sufficient to illustrate what should be an uncontentious point. If experimental results constitute the facts on which science is based, then they are certainly not straightforwardly given via the senses. They have to be worked for, and their establishment involves considerable know-how and practical trial and error as well as exploitation of the available technology.

对实验结果是否充分的判断也并非易事。只有当实验设置恰当且干扰因素已被消除时，实验结果才是充分的，并且可以被解释为展示或测量了其预期展示或测量的内容。而这反过来又要求我们了解这些干扰因素是什么，以及如何消除它们。任何关于这些因素的相关知识不足都可能导致不恰当的实验措施和错误的结论。因此，实验事实和理论在某种重要意义上是相互关联的。如果作为实验依据的知识存在缺陷或错误，那么实验结果就可能是错误的。

Nor are judgments about the adequacy of experimental results straightforward. Experiments are adequate, and interpretable as displaying or measuring what they are intended to display or measure, only if the experimental set-up is appropriate and disturbing factors have been eliminated. This in turn will require that it is known what those disturbing factors are and how they can be eliminated. Any inadequacies in the relevant knowledge about these factors could lead to inappropriate experimental measures and faulty conclusions. So there is a significant sense in which experimental facts and theory are interrelated. Experimental results can be faulty if the knowledge informing them is deficient or faulty.

实验的这些普遍且在某种程度上相当平凡的特点导致的一个结果是，实验结果并非完美无缺，而且由于一些相当直接的原因，实验结果可能会被更新或替换。技术进步会导致实验结果过时，认知进步会导致实验装置被认为不完善，而理论理解的转变也会导致实验结果被认为无关紧要而被忽略。下一节将通过历史实例来说明这些要点及其意义。

A consequence of these general, and in a sense quite mundane, features of experiment is that experimental results are fallible, and can be updated or replaced for reasonably straightforward reasons. Experimental results can become outmoded because of advances in technology, they can be rejected because of some advance in understanding (in the light of which an experimental set-up comes to be seen as inadequate) and they can be ignored as irrelevant in the light of some shift in theoretical understanding. These points and their significance are illustrated by historical examples in the next section.

转变科学的实验基础：历史实例

Transforming the experimental base of science: historical examples

十九世纪末，放电管现象引起了科学界的极大兴趣。如果在封闭玻璃管两端插入金属板并施加高电压，就会发生放电，导致管内出现各种发光现象。如果管内气体压力不太大，就会产生连接负极板（阴极）和正极板（阳极）的流光。这些流光被称为阴极射线，其性质引起了当时科学家的极大兴趣。德国物理学家海因里希·赫兹在19世纪80年代初进行了一系列实验，旨在阐明阴极射线的性质。赫兹的实验结果表明，阴极射线并非带电粒子束。他得出这一结论的部分原因是，当阴极射线受到垂直于其运动方向的电场作用时，并没有像带电粒子束那样发生偏转。我们现在认为赫兹的结论是错误的，他的实验也不够充分。在本世纪结束之前，JJ·汤姆逊进行了一系列实验，令人信服地证明阴极射线在电场和磁场的作用下会发生偏转，这与它们是带电粒子束的性质相符，并且他还能够测量粒子的电荷与质量之比。

Discharge tube phenomena commanded great scientific interest in the final quarter of the nineteenth century. If a high voltage is connected across metal plates inserted at each end of an enclosed glass tube, an electric discharge occurs, causing various kinds of glowing within the tube. If the gas pressure within the tube is not too great, streamers are produced, joining the negative plate (the cathode) and the positive plate (the anode). These became known as cathode rays, and their nature was a matter of considerable interest to scientists of the time. The German physicist Heinrich Hertz conducted a series of experiments in the early 1880s intended to shed light on their nature. As a result of these experiments Hertz concluded that cathode rays are not beams of charged particles. He reached this conclusion in part because the rays did not seem to be deflected when they were subjected to an electric field perpendicular to their direction of motion as would be expected of a beam of charged particles. We now regard Hertz’s conclusion as false and his experiments inadequate. Before the century had ended, J. J. Thomson had conducted experiments that showed convincingly that cathode rays are deflected by electric and magnetic fields in a way that is consistent with their being beams of charged particles and was able to measure the ratio of the electric charge to the mass of the particles.

正是技术的进步和对情况理解的加深，使得汤姆逊能够改进并推翻赫兹的实验结果。构成阴极射线的电子能够电离管内气体的分子，即从分子中移除一个或两个电子，使其带正电。这些离子会聚集在装置内的金属板上，从而产生在当时实验中被视为虚假电场的现象。据推测，正是这些虚假电场阻碍了赫兹产生汤姆逊最终能够产生并测量的偏转现象。汤姆逊改进赫兹实验的主要方法是利用改进的真空技术，从管内去除更多的气体分子。他将装置长时间烘烤，以排出管内各表面残留的气体。他还连续运行真空泵数日，尽可能多地去除残留气体。凭借改进的真空度和更合适的电极排列，汤姆逊最终获得了赫兹曾断言不存在的偏转现象。当汤姆逊将他装置中的压力提升到赫兹装置中的水平时，他也没能检测到偏转。这里需要强调的是，赫兹得出这样的结论并非他的过错。基于他对当时情况的理解，以及他所掌握的知识，他有充分的理由相信他装置中的压力足够低，而且他的装置也布置得当。只是随着后来的理论和技术进步，他的实验才被发现存在缺陷。当然，这其中的寓意是：谁又能预知未来的技术进步会如何证明当时的实验结果存在缺陷呢？

It was improved technology and improved understanding of the situation that made it possible for Thomson to improve on and reject Hertz’s experimental results. The electrons that constitute the cathode rays can ionise the molecules of the gas in the tube, that is, displace an electron or two from them so that they become positively charged. These ions can collect on metal plates in the apparatus and lead to what, from the point of view of the experiments under consideration, are spurious electric fields. It was presumably such fields that prevented Hertz producing the deflections that Thomson was eventually to be able to produce and measure. The main way that Thomson was able to improve on Hertz’s efforts was to take advantage of improved vacuum technology to remove more gas molecules from the tube. He subjected his apparatus to prolonged baking to drive residual gas from the various surfaces within the tube. He ran the vacuum pump for several days to remove as much of the residual gas as possible. With an improved vacuum, and with a more appropriate arrangement of electrodes, Thomson was able to establish the deflections that Hertz had declared to be non-existent. When Thomson allowed the pressure in his apparatus to rise to what it had been in Hertz’s, Thomson could not detect a deflection either. It is important to realise here that Hertz is not to be blamed for drawing the conclusion that he did. Given his understanding of the situation, and drawing on the knowledge available to him, he had good reasons to believe that the pressure in his apparatus was sufficiently low and that his apparatus was appropriately arranged. It was only in the light of subsequent theoretical and technological advances that his experiment came to be seen as deficient. The moral, of course, is this: who knows which contemporary experimental results will be shown to be deficient by advances that lie ahead?

赫兹绝非平庸的实验家，事实上，他是当时最杰出的实验家之一。1888年，他首次成功产生无线电波，这证明了他的卓越成就。这一成果是他两年卓有成效的实验研究的结晶。赫兹的无线电波不仅揭示了一种值得探索和研究的新现象，而且具有重要的理论意义，因为它证实了麦克斯韦在19世纪60年代中期提出的电磁理论，该理论表明电磁波确实存在（尽管麦克斯韦本人当时并未意识到这一点）。赫兹的大部分实验结果至今仍然有效，并具有重要的意义。然而，他的一些实验结果需要修正，他对其中一种主要解释也需要推翻。这两点都表明，实验结果需要不断修正和改进。

Far from being a shoddy experimentalist, the fact that Hertz was one of the very best is borne out by his success in being the first to produce radio waves in 1888, as the culmination of two years of brilliant experimental research. Apart from revealing a new phenomenon to be explored and developed experimentally, Hertz’s waves had considerable theoretical significance, since they confirmed Maxwell’s electromagnetic theory, which he had formulated in the mid-1860s and which had the consequence that there be such waves (although Maxwell himself had not realised this). Most aspects of Hertz’s results remain acceptable and retain their significance today. However, some of his results needed to be replaced and one of his main interpretations of them rejected. Both of these points illustrate the way in which experimental results are subject to revision and improvement.

赫兹利用他的装置产生了驻波，从而测量了波的波长，并由此推导出波的传播速度。他的结果表明，波长较长的波在空气中的传播速度比在导线中更快，甚至超过光速。而麦克斯韦理论预测，无论在空气中还是在赫兹装置的导线中，波的传播速度都应为光速。赫兹已经怀疑，实验结果并不理想。实验室墙壁反射回来的波造成了不必要的干扰。赫兹本人（1962，第14页）对这些结果进行了如下反思：

Hertz was able to use his apparatus to generate standing waves, which enabled him to measure their wavelength, from which he could deduce their velocity. His results indicated that the waves of longer wavelength travelled at a greater speed in air than along wires, and faster than light, whereas Maxwell’s theory predicted that they would travel at the speed of light both in air and along the wires of Hertz’s apparatus. The results were inadequate for reasons that Hertz already suspected. Waves reflected back onto the apparatus from the walls of the laboratory were causing unwanted interference. Hertz (1962, p. 14) himself reflected on the results as follows:

读者或许会问，我为何没有尝试通过重复实验来解决这个疑点。我的确重复了实验，但正如预期的那样，在相同条件下简单地重复实验并不能消除疑虑，反而加深了疑虑。只有在更有利的条件下进行实验才能得出确切的结论。这里所说的更有利的条件指的是更大的实验空间，而我当时并没有这样的空间。我再次强调，观察时的细致程度并不能弥补空间不足的问题。如果长波无法发展，显然也就无法被观测到。

The reader may perhaps ask why I have not endeavored to settle the doubtful point myself by repeating the experiments. I have indeed repeated the experiments, but have only found, as might be expected, that a simple repetition under the same conditions cannot remove the doubt, but rather increases it. A definite decision can only be arrived at by experiments carried out under more favorable conditions. More favorable conditions here mean larger rooms, and such were not at my disposal. I again emphasise the statement that care in making the observations cannot make up for want of space. If the long waves cannot develop, they clearly cannot be observed.

赫兹的实验结果并不理想，因为他的实验装置并不适合当时的研究任务。为了消除反射波的干扰，所研究的波的波长必须远小于实验室的尺寸。后来，几年之内，人们在“更有利的条件下”进行了实验，并获得了与理论预测相符的速度值。

Hertz’s experimental results were inadequate because his experimental set-up was inappropriate for the task in hand. The wavelengths of the waves investigated needed to be small compared with the dimensions of the laboratory if unwanted interference from reflected waves was to be removed. As it transpired, within a few years experiments were carried out ‘under more favorable conditions’ and yielded velocities in line with the theoretical predictions.

这里需要强调的是，实验结果不仅需要足够充分，即准确记录所发生的事情，而且还需要具有相关性或重要性。它们通常旨在阐明某些重要问题。判断什么是重要问题，以及判断某组特定的实验是否是回答该问题的合适方法，很大程度上取决于对实际和理论情况的理解。正是由于存在相互竞争的电磁理论，以及其中一个主要竞争理论预测无线电波以光速传播，才使得赫兹测量其波速的尝试显得尤为重要；而正是对波的反射特性的理解，使人们认识到赫兹的实验装置并不合适。赫兹的这些特定结果很快就被否定并被取代，其原因从物理学的角度来看是简单明了的。

A point to be stressed here is that experimental results are required not only to be adequate, in the sense of being accurate recordings of what happened, but also to be appropriate or significant. They will typically be designed to cast light on some significant question. Judgments about what is a significant question and about whether some specific set of experiments is an adequate way of answering it will depend heavily on how the practical and theoretical situation is understood. It was the existence of competing theories of electromagnetism and the fact that one of the major contenders predicted radio waves travelling with the speed of light that made Hertz’s attempt to measure the velocity of his waves particularly significant, while it was an understanding of the reflection behaviour of the waves that led to the appreciation that Hertz’s experimental set-up was inappropriate. These particular results of Hertz’s were rejected and soon replaced for reasons that are straightforward and non-mysterious from the point of view of physics.

赫兹的这段研究经历以及他对此的反思，不仅阐明了实验必须恰当且有意义，以及当实验结果不再恰当或有意义时就应被替换或摒弃这一观点，而且还清楚地表明，他速度测量结果被否定与人类感知问题毫无关系。毫无疑问，赫兹认真观察了他的实验装置，测量距离，记录探测器间隙中是否存在火花，并记录了仪器读数。他的结果可以被认为是客观的，因为任何重复实验的人都会得到类似的结果。赫兹本人也强调了这一点。赫兹实验结果的问题既不在于他观察的不足，也不在于缺乏可重复性，而在于实验装置的缺陷。正如赫兹所指出的，“观察的细致程度无法弥补空间的不足”。即使我们承认赫兹能够通过仔细观察来确立可靠的事实，我们也可以看出，这本身并不足以产生足以完成所讨论的科学任务的实验结果。

As well as illustrating the point that experiments need to be appropriate or significant, and that experimental results are replaced or rejected when they cease to be so, this episode in Hertz’s researches and his own reflections on it clearly bring out the respect in which the rejection of his velocity measurements has nothing whatsoever to do with problems of human perception. There is no reason whatsoever to doubt that Hertz carefully observed his apparatus, measuring distances, noting the presence or absence of sparks across the gaps in his detectors, and recording instrument readings. His results can be assumed to be objective in the sense that anyone who repeats them will get similar results. Hertz himself stressed this point. The problem with Hertz’s experimental results stems neither from inadequacies in his observations nor from any lack of repeatability, but rather from the inadequacy of the experimental set-up. As Hertz pointed out, ‘care in making the observations cannot make up for want of space’. Even if we concede that Hertz was able to establish secure facts by way of careful observation, we can see that this in itself was insufficient to yield experimental results adequate for the scientific task in question.

上述讨论可以理解为阐明了实验结果的可接受性如何依赖于理论，以及这方面的判断如何随着我们科学理解的发展而改变。赫兹首次产生无线电波以来，其意义的演变更能体现这一点。当时，几种相互竞争的电磁理论之一是詹姆斯·克拉克·麦克斯韦的理论。麦克斯韦发展了迈克尔·法拉第的关键思想，并将电场和磁场状态理解为无处不在的以太的机械状态。与其他假设电流、电荷和磁体在一定距离内相互作用且不涉及以太的理论不同，麦克斯韦的理论预测了无线电波以光速传播的可能性。正是物理学发展的这一方面赋予了赫兹的实验结果以理论意义。因此，赫兹及其同时代的人能够将无线电波的产生解释为以太存在的证据之一。二十年后，随着爱因斯坦狭义相对论的出现，以太的概念被摒弃。赫兹的实验结果仍然被认为是证实了麦克斯韦理论，但那只是对麦克斯韦理论的一种改写，这种改写摒弃了以太的概念，并将电场和磁场视为独立存在的实体。

The above discussion can be construed as illustrating how the acceptability of experimental results is theory-dependent, and how judgments in this respect are subject to change as our scientific understanding develops. This is illustrated at a more general level by the way in which the significance of Hertz’s production of radio waves has changed since Hertz first produced them. At that time, one of the several competing theories of electromagnetism was that of James Clerk Maxwell, who had developed the key ideas of Michael Faraday and had understood electric and magnetic states as the mechanical states of an all-pervasive ether. This theory, unlike its competitors, which assumed that electric currents, charges and magnets acted on each other at a distance and did not involve an ether, predicted the possibility of radio waves moving at the speed of light. This is the aspect of the state of development of physics that gave Hertz’s results their theoretical significance. Consequently, Hertz and his contemporaries were able to construe the production of radio waves as, among other things, confirmation of the existence of an ether. Two decades later the ether was dispensed with in the light of Einstein’s special theory of relativity. Hertz’s results are still regarded as confirming Maxwell’s theory, but only a rewritten version of it that dispenses with the ether, and treats electric and magnetic fields as real entities in their own right.

另一个关于十九世纪分子量测量的例子进一步说明了实验结果的相关性和解释如何取决于理论背景。在十九世纪下半叶，化学家们根据化学结合的原子理论，认为测量天然元素和化合物的分子量至关重要。对于那些支持普劳特假说（即氢原子是构成其他原子的基本单元）的人来说尤其如此，因为这使得人们预期相对于氢原子测量的分子量应该是整数。然而，一旦人们意识到天然元素包含多种同位素的混合物，而这些同位素的比例并无特定的理论意义，那么十九世纪顶尖实验化学家们对分子量的艰苦测量，从理论化学的角度来看就变得基本无关紧要了。这种情况促使化学家F. Soddy对此发表了如下评论（Lakatos和Musgrave，1970，第140页）：

Another example, concerning nineteenth-century measurements of molecular weights, further illustrates the way in which the relevance and interpretation of experimental results depend on the theoretical context. Measurements of the molecular weights of naturally occurring elements and compounds were considered to be of fundamental importance by chemists in the second half of the nineteenth century in the light of the atomic theory of chemical combination. This was especially so for those who favoured Prout’s hypothesis that the hydrogen atom is the basic building block from which other atoms are constructed, for this led one to expect that molecular weights measured relative to hydrogen would be whole numbers. The painstaking measurements of molecular weights by the leading experimental chemists in the nineteenth century became largely irrelevant from the point of view of theoretical chemistry once it was realised that naturally occurring elements contain a mixture of isotopes in proportions that had no particular theoretical significance. This situation inspired the chemist F. Soddy to comment on its outcome as follows (Lakatos and Musgrave, 1970, p. 140):

对于这群杰出的十九世纪化学家而言，他们毕生心血的命运如今却黯然失色，这无疑是一种悲剧，甚至可以说是超越悲剧的悲剧。他们曾被同时代的人尊为精确科学测量的巅峰之作。然而，至少在目前看来，他们辛勤取得的成果似乎与测定一堆瓶子的平均重量一样微不足道，这些瓶子有的装满了液体，有的则几乎是空的。

There is something surely akin to if not transcending tragedy in the fate that has overtaken the life work of this distinguished galaxy of nineteenth-century chemists, rightly revered by their contemporaries as representing the crown and perfection of accurate scientific measurements. Their hard won results, for the moment at least, appear as of little significance as the determination of the average weight of a collection of bottles, some of them full and some of them more or less empty.

在这里，我们看到一些旧的实验结果被弃之不用，而原因并非源于人类感知的缺陷。参与其中的十九世纪化学家“被同时代的人尊为精确科学测量的巅峰和完美典范”，我们没有理由怀疑他们的观察结果。我们也无需怀疑其客观性。我毫不怀疑，如果当代化学家重复同样的实验，他们会得到类似的结果。实验的充分性是实验结果可接受的必要条件，但并非充分条件。实验结果还必须具有相关性和重要性。

Here we witness old experimental results being set aside as irrelevant, and for reasons that do not stem from problematic features of human perception. The nineteenth-century chemists involved were ‘revered by their contemporaries as representing the crown and perfection of accurate scientific measurement’ and we have no reason to doubt their observations. Nor need we doubt the objectivity of the latter. I have no doubt that similar results would be obtained by contemporary chemists if they were to repeat the same experiments. That they be adequately performed is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the acceptability of experimental results. They need also to be relevant and significant.

我借助实例阐述的观点，可以概括为一种我认为在物理学、化学及其实践层面都无可争议的方式。被视为科学基础的实验结果库一直在更新。旧的实验结果会因不充分而被摒弃，并被更充分的结果所取代，原因多种多样，也相当直接。它们被摒弃的原因可能是：实验中对潜在干扰源的防范措施不足；测量方法灵敏度低且过时；实验被认为无法解决当前问题；或者实验旨在解答的问题本身已被否定。尽管这些观察结果看似是对日常科学活动的显而易见的论断，但它们对许多正统的科学哲学却有着深远的影响，因为它们动摇了科学建立在稳固基础之上的普遍观念。更重要的是，科学基础不稳固的原因与人类感知的固有缺陷关系不大。

The points I have been making with the aid of examples can be summed up in a way that I believe is quite uncontentious from the point of view of physics and chemistry and their practice. The stock of experimental results regarded as an appropriate basis for science is constantly updated. Old experimental results are rejected as inadequate and replaced by more adequate ones, for a range of fairly straightforward reasons. They can be rejected because the experiment involved inadequate precautions against possible sources of interference, because the measurements employed insensitive and outmoded methods of detection, because the experiments came to be understood as incapable of solving the problem in hand, or because the questions they were designed to answer became discredited. Although these observations can be seen as fairly obvious comments on everyday scientific activity, they nevertheless have serious implications for much orthodox philosophy of science, for they undermine the widely held notion that science rests on secure foundations. What is more, the reasons why it does not has nothing much to do with problematic features of human perception.

实验是科学的充分基础

Experiment as an adequate basis for science

在本章前几节中，我对实验结果直接给出且完全可靠的观点进行了批判性审视。我论证了实验结果在某些方面依赖于理论，并且易出错且可修正。这可以被解读为对“科学知识之所以特殊，是因为它以某种特别严谨且令人信服的方式得到经验支持”这一观点的严重威胁。如果科学的实验基础真如我所论证的那样易出错且可修正，那么基于此的知识也必然同样易出错且可修正。这种担忧还可以通过指出科学理论被实验证实的方式中存在的循环论证风险来加强。如果用理论来判断实验结果的充分性，而这些实验结果又被用作理论的证据，那么我们似乎就陷入了一个循环。看来，科学很可能无法提供足够的资源，通过诉诸实验结果来解决对立理论支持者之间的争论。一方会诉诸其理论来证明某些实验结果的正确性，而另一方则会诉诸其对立理论来证明其他实验结果的正确性。本节将阐述反对这些极端结论的理由。

In the previous sections of this chapter I have subjected to critical scrutiny the idea that experimental results are straightforwardly given and totally secure. I have made a case to the effect that they are theory-dependent in certain respects and fallible and revisable. This can be interpreted as a serious threat to the idea that scientific knowledge is special because it is supported by experience in some especially demanding and convincing way. If, it might be argued, the experimental basis of science is as fallible and revisable as I have argued it to be, then the knowledge based on it must be equally fallible and revisable. The worry can be strengthened by pointing to a threat of circularity in the way scientific theories are alleged to be borne out by experiment. If theories are appealed to in order to judge the adequacy of experimental results, and those same experimental results are taken as the evidence for the theories, then it would seem that we are caught in a circle. It would seem that there is a strong possibility that science will not provide the resources to settle a dispute between the proponents of opposing theories by appeal to experimental results. One group would appeal to its theory to vindicate certain experimental results, and the opposing camp would appeal to its rival theory to vindicate different experimental results. In this section I give reasons for resisting these extreme conclusions.

必须承认，理论与实验之间的关系可能存在循环论证的可能性。我教书时的一个故事可以说明这一点。当时，我的学生被要求进行一项实验，实验内容如下：测量悬挂在蹄形磁铁两极之间的载流线圈的偏转，该线圈可以绕垂直于磁铁两极连线的轴线自由旋转。线圈是电路的一部分，电路中包含一个电池（用于提供电流）、一个电流表（用于测量电流）和一个可变电阻（用于调节电流大小）。实验的目的是记录电流表读数变化时，磁铁的偏转量。如果学生绘制出偏转量与电流的直线图，表明两者成正比，则实验被视为成功。我记得当时我对这个实验感到很困惑，但或许明智的是，我没有把这种担忧传递给我的学生。我的担忧源于我对电流表内部构造的了解。电流表内部是一个悬挂在磁铁两极之间的线圈，当电流流过线圈时，线圈会发生偏转，从而带动电流表上清晰可见且刻度均匀的指针移动。因此，在这个实验中，当电流表读数被用来衡量电流时，指针偏转与电流成正比的假设就已经被预设了。实验所支持的结论本身就是实验的预设，这确实存在循环论证的问题。

It must be acknowledged that there is the possibility that the relationship between theory and experiment might involve a circular argument. This can be illustrated by the following story from my schoolteaching days. My pupils were required to conduct an experiment along the following lines. The aim was to measure the deflection of a current-carrying coil suspended between the poles of a horseshoe magnet and free to rotate about an axis perpendicular to the line joining the poles of the magnet. The coil formed part of a circuit containing a battery to supply a current, an ammeter to measure the current and a variable resistance to make it possible to adjust the strength of the current. The aim was to note the deflection of the magnet corresponding to various values of the current in the circuit as registered by the ammeter. The experiment was to be deemed a success for those pupils who got a nice straight-line graph when they plotted deflection against current, revealing the proportionality of the two. I remember being disconcerted by this experiment, although, perhaps wisely, I did not transmit my worry to my pupils. My worry stemmed from the fact that I knew what was inside the ammeter. What was inside was a coil suspended between the poles of a magnet in such a way that it was deflected by a current through the coil causing a needle to move on the visible and evenly calibrated scale of the ammeter. In this experiment, then, the proportionality of deflection to current was already presupposed when the reading of the ammeter was taken as a measure of the current. What was taken to be supported by the experiment was already presupposed in it, and there was indeed a circularity.

我的例子说明了在诉诸实验的论证中，循环论证是如何产生的。但同样的例子也表明，这种情况并非必然发生。上述实验本可以，而且实际上应该，采用一种不利用磁场中线圈偏转来测量电路电流的方法。所有实验都会预设一些理论的正确性，以帮助判断实验装置是否充分，以及仪器读数是否准确。但这些预设理论不必与待检验的理论完全相同，而且，确保它们不相同似乎是良好实验设计的先决条件。

My example illustrates how circularity can arise in arguments that appeal to experiment. But the very same example serves to show that this need not be the case. The above experiment could have, and indeed should have, used a method of measuring the current in the circuit that did not employ the deflection of a coil in a magnetic field. All experiments will presume the truth of some theories to help judge that the set-up is adequate and the instruments are reading what they are meant to read. But these presupposed theories need not be identical to the theory under test, and it would seem reasonable to assume that a prerequisite of good experimental design is to ensure that they are not.

另一个有助于我们正确理解“实验对理论的依赖性”的观点是，无论实验多么依赖理论，实验结果在很大程度上是由现实世界而非理论决定的。一旦装置搭建完毕，电路接通，开关拨动等等，屏幕上是否会出现闪光，光束是否会发生偏转，电流表读数是否会增加，都取决于实验结果。我们无法使实验结果符合我们的理论。正是由于物理世界的本来面目，赫兹的实验才没有观察到阴极射线的偏转，而汤姆逊改进后的实验却观察到了偏转。导致两位物理学家实验结果不同的，并非源于他们理论的差异，而是实验装置本身的差异。正是由于实验结果是由现实世界的运行规律而非理论观点决定的，才使得我们能够用现实世界来检验理论。这并非意味着重要的成果唾手可得且绝对可靠，也并非意味着它们的意义总是显而易见的。但这确实有助于阐明这样一个观点：尝试用实验结果检验科学理论的正确性是一项意义非凡的探索。此外，科学史也为我们提供了成功应对挑战的例证。

Another point that serves to get the ‘theory-dependence of experiment’ in perspective is that, however informed by theory an experiment is, there is a strong sense in which the results of an experiment are determined by the world and not by the theories. Once the apparatus is set up, the circuits completed, the switches thrown and so on, there will or will not be a flash on the screen, the beam may or may not be deflected, the reading on the ammeter may or may not increase. We cannot make the outcomes conform to our theories. It was because the physical world is the way it is that the experiment conducted by Hertz yielded no deflection of cathode rays and the modified experiment conducted by Thomson did. It was the material differences in the experimental arrangements of the two physicists that led to the differing outcomes, not the differences in the theories held by them. It is the sense in which experimental outcomes are determined by the workings of the world rather than by theoretical views about the world that provides the possibility of testing theories against the world. This is not to say that significant results are easily achievable and infallible, nor that their significance is always straightforward. But it does help to establish the point that the attempt to test the adequacy of scientific theories against experimental results is a meaningful quest. What is more, the history of science gives us examples of cases where the challenge was successfully met.

延伸阅读

Further reading

哈金（Hacking，1983）的后半部分标志着科学哲学家对实验产生了新的兴趣，这是一个重要的早期进展。其他对这一主题的探讨包括富兰克林（Franklin，1986）、富兰克林（Franklin，1990）、加利森（Galison，1987）和梅奥（Mayo，1996）的著作，但这些详尽的论述只有在结合第十三章“新实验主义”的视角才能充分理解。

The second half of Hacking (1983) was an important early move in the new interest philosophers of science have taken in experiment. Other explorations of the topic are Franklin (1986), Franklin (1990), Galison (1987) and Mayo (1996), although these detailed treatments will take on their full significance only in the light of chapter 13, on the ‘new experimentalism’.

第四章

CHAPTER 4

从事实推导出理论：归纳法

Deriving theories from the facts: induction

介绍

Introduction

在本书的前几章中，我们一直在探讨科学知识的特征在于它源于事实。我们已经详细考察了作为科学知识基础的观察和实验事实的性质，尽管我们也看到，这些事实的确立并非如人们通常认为的那样直接和可靠。那么，让我们假设在科学中可以确立适当的事实。现在，我们必须面对这样一个问题：如何从这些事实中推导出科学知识？

In these early chapters of the book we have been considering the idea that what is characteristic of scientific knowledge is that it is derived from the facts. We have reached a stage where we have given some detailed attention to the nature of the observational and experimental facts that can be considered as the basis from which scientific knowledge might be derived, although we have seen that those facts cannot be established as straightforwardly and securely as is commonly supposed. Let us assume, then, that appropriate facts can be established in science. We must now face the question of how scientific knowledge can be derived from those facts.

“科学源于事实”这种说法可以理解为：科学知识的构建首先在于确立事实，然后构建理论来与之相符。我们在第一章讨论过这种观点，并认为它不合理。我想探讨的问题在于，如何从逻辑而非时间意义上来理解“源于”一词。无论事实和理论哪个先出现，我们需要探讨的问题是：理论在多大程度上得到了事实的支持。最强有力的论断是：理论可以从事实中逻辑推导而来。也就是说，在既定事实的前提下，理论可以被证明是事实的必然结果。然而，这种强有力的论断无法得到证实。为了理解个中缘由，我们必须考察逻辑推理的一些基本特征。

‘Science is derived from the facts’ could be interpreted to mean that scientific knowledge is constructed by first establishing the facts and then subsequently building the theory to fit them. We discussed this view in chapter 1 and rejected it as unreasonable. The issue that I wish to explore involves interpreting ‘derive’ in some kind of logical rather than temporal sense. No matter which comes first, the facts or the theory, the question to be addressed is the extent to which the theory is borne out by the facts. The strongest possible claim would be that the theory can be logically derived from the facts. That is, given the facts, the theory can be proven as a consequence of them. This strong claim cannot be substantiated. To see why this is so we must look at some of the basic features of logical reasoning.

婴儿逻辑

Baby logic

逻辑关注的是从已知命题中推导出其他命题，也就是探究什么能从什么中得出。本文无意对逻辑或演绎推理进行详尽的阐述和评价，而是借助一些非常简单的例子，阐明足以满足我们目的的要点。

Logic is concerned with the deduction of statements from other, given, statements. It is concerned with what follows from what. No attempt will be made to give a detailed account and appraisal of logic or deductive reasoning here. Rather, I will make the points that will be sufficient for our purpose with the aid of some very simple examples.

以下是一个完全充分的逻辑论证的例子，或者用逻辑学家的专业术语来说，是完全有效的。

Here is an example of a logical argument that is perfectly adequate or, to use the technical term used by logicians, perfectly valid.

例 1

Example 1

1. 所有哲学书籍都很枯燥。

1. All books on philosophy are boring.

2. 这是一本哲学著作。

2. This book is a book on philosophy.

3. 这本书很无聊。

3. This book is boring.

在这个论证中，(1) 和 (2) 是前提，(3) 是结论。显然，如果 (1) 和 (2) 为真，那么 (3) 也必然为真。既然 (1) 和 (2) 为真，那么 (3) 就不可能为假。断言 (1) 和 (2) 为真而否定 (3) 就是自相矛盾。这是逻辑有效演绎的关键特征。如果前提为真，那么结论也必然为真。逻辑是维护真理的。

In this argument, (1) and (2) are the premises and (3) is the conclusion. It is evident, I take it, that if (1) and (2) are true then (3) is bound to be true. It is not possible for (3) to be false once it is given that (1) and (2) are true. To assert (1) and (2) as true and to deny (3) is to contradict oneself. This is the key feature of a logically valid deduction. If the premises are true then the conclusion must be true. Logic is truth preserving.

对示例 1 稍作修改，即可得到一个无效论证的例子。

A slight modification of Example 1 will give us an instance of an argument that is not valid.

例 2

Example 2

1. 许多哲学书籍都很枯燥乏味。

1. Many books on philosophy are boring.

2. 这是一本哲学著作。

2. This book is a book on philosophy.

3. 这本书很无聊。

3. This book is boring.

在这个例子中，(3) 并非必然由 (1) 和 (2) 得出。即使 (1) 和 (2) 为真，这本书也可能成为少数几本不枯燥的哲学著作之一。接受 (1) 和 (2) 为真而认定 (3) 为假并不构成矛盾。因此，该论证无效。

In this example, (3) does not follow of necessity from (1) and (2). Even if (1) and (2) are true, then this book might yet turn out to be one of the minority of books on philosophy that are not boring. Accepting (1) and (2) as true and holding (3) to be false does not involve a contradiction. The argument is invalid.

读者现在可能已经感到无聊了。这类经历当然会对例1和例2中陈述(1)和(3)的真假产生影响。但这里需要强调的是，仅凭逻辑演绎无法确定我们例子中这类事实陈述的真假。逻辑在这方面所能提供的只是：如果前提为真且论证有效，那么结论必然为真。但前提是否为真并非诉诸逻辑就能解决的问题。即使前提为假，一个论证也可能是一个完全有效的演绎。以下就是一个例子。

The reader may by now be feeling bored. Experiences of that kind certainly have a bearing on the truth of statements (1) and (3) in Example 1 and Example 2. But a point that needs to be stressed here is that logical deduction alone cannot establish the truth of factual statements of the kind figuring in our examples. All that logic can offer in this connection is that if the premises are true and the argument is valid then the conclusion must be true. But whether the premises are true or not is not a question that can be settled by an appeal to logic. An argument can be a perfectly valid deduction even if it involves a false premise. Here is an example.

例 3

Example 3

1. 所有猫都有五条腿。

1. All cats have five legs.

2. Bugs Pussy是我的猫。

2. Bugs Pussy is my cat.

3. 虫猫有五条腿。

3. Bugs Pussy has five legs.

这是一个完全有效的推论。如果 (1) 和 (2) 为真，那么 (3) 也必然为真。恰好在这个例子中，(1) 和 (3) 为假。但这并不影响论证的有效性。

This is a perfectly valid deduction. If (1) and (2) are true then (3) must be true. It so happens that, in this example (1) and (3) are false. But this does not affect the fact that the argument is valid.

因此，从某种意义上说，逻辑本身并不能带来新的真理。构成论证前提的事实陈述的真假，不能仅凭逻辑来确立。逻辑只能揭示从我们已有的陈述中可以推导出什么，或者说，在某种意义上，什么已经包含在这些陈述之中。然而，逻辑的强大之处在于它能够保持真理。如果我们确信我们的前提为真，那么我们同样可以确信，所有从这些前提逻辑推导出的结论也都是正确的。

There is a strong sense, then, in which logic alone is not a source of new truths. The truth of the factual statements that constitute the premises of arguments cannot be established by appeal to logic. Logic can simply reveal what follows from, or what in a sense is already contained in, the statements we already have to hand. Against this limitation we have the great strength of logic, namely, its truth-preserving character. If we can be sure our premises are true then we can be equally sure that everything we logically derive from them will also be true.

科学定律可以从事实中推导出来吗？

Can scientific laws be derived from the facts?

通过对我们所处逻辑本质的讨论，可以清楚地表明，如果将“推导”解释为“逻辑推演”，那么科学知识就无法从事实中推导出来。

With this discussion of the nature of logic behind us, it can be straightforwardly shown that scientific knowledge cannot be derived from the facts if ‘derive’ is interpreted as ‘logically deduce’.

一些简单的科学知识例子足以说明这个基本观点。让我们考虑一些低层次的科学定律，例如“金属受热膨胀”或“酸会使石蕊试纸变红”。这些都是概括性的陈述，是哲学家所说的普遍性陈述的例子。它们指的是特定类型的所有事件，例如所有金属受热的情况以及所有石蕊试纸浸入酸中的情况。科学知识总是包含这类概括性的陈述。然而，对于构成事实、为一般科学定律提供证据的观察陈述而言，情况则截然不同。这些可观察的事实或实验结果是对特定时间发生的某种状态的具体描述，是哲学家所说的个别性陈述。它们包括诸如“铜棒受热后长度增加”或“石蕊试纸浸入盐酸烧杯中变红”之类的陈述。假设我们掌握了大量此类事实，并希望从中推导出一些科学知识（例如，我们例子中关于金属或酸的知识）。什么样的论证方式能够让我们从这些事实（作为前提）推导出我们想要得出的科学规律（作为结论）呢？以我们关于金属膨胀的例子为例，论证可以概括如下：

Some simple examples of scientific knowledge will be sufficient for the illustration of this basic point. Let us consider some low-level scientific laws such as ‘metals expand when heated’ or ‘acids turn litmus red’. These are general statements. They are examples of what philosophers refer to as universal statements. They refer to all events of a particular kind, all instances of metals being heated and all instances of litmus being immersed in acid. Scientific knowledge invariably involves general statements of this kind. The situation is quite otherwise when it comes to the observation statements that constitute the facts that provide the evidence for general scientific laws. Those observable facts or experimental results are specific claims about a state of affairs that obtains at a particular time. They are what philosophers call singular statements. They include statements such as ‘the length of the copper bar increased when it was heated’ or ‘the litmus paper turned red when immersed in the beaker of hydrochloric acid’. Suppose we have a large number of such facts at our disposal as the basis from which we hope to derive some scientific knowledge (about metals or acids in the case of our examples). What kind of argument can take us from those facts, as premises, to the scientific laws we seek to derive as conclusions? In the case of our example concerning the expansion of metals the argument can be schematised as follows:

前提

Premises

1. 金属 x 1在偶尔 t 1时受热膨胀。

1. Metal x1 expanded when heated on occasion t1.

2. 金属 x 2在偶尔加热时膨胀 t 2。

2. Metal x2 expanded when heated on occasion t2.

n. 金属 x n在加热时偶尔膨胀 t n。

n. Metal xn expanded when heated on occasion tn.

结论

Conclusion

所有金属受热都会膨胀。

All metals expand when heated.

这并非一个逻辑有效的论证。它缺乏此类论证的基本特征。前提为真并不意味着结论必然为真。无论我们有多少关于金属膨胀的观察结果，也就是说，无论我们例子中的样本量 n 有多大，都无法从逻辑上保证某些金属样本在加热时会收缩。声称所有已知的金属加热都导致膨胀，与“所有金属加热都会膨胀”的说法是错误的，两者之间并不矛盾。

This is not a logically valid argument. It lacks the basic features of such an argument. It is simply not the case that if the statements constituting the premises are true then the conclusion must be true. However many observations of expanding metals we have to work with, that is, however great n might be in our example, there can be no logical guarantee that some sample of metal might on some occasion contract when heated. There is no contradiction involved in claiming both that all known examples of the heating of metals has resulted in expansion and that ‘all metals expand when heated’ is false.

这个简单明了的观点可以用一个略显残酷的例子来说明，这个例子据说是伯特兰·罗素提出的。故事的主人公是一只火鸡，它在来到养鸡场的第一天早上注意到自己每天早上9点都会被喂食。在接下来的几周里，每天都是如此，这只火鸡便理所当然地得出结论：“我总是早上9点被喂食。” 然而，圣诞夜那天，火鸡并没有被喂食，而是被割喉，这无疑证明了它的结论是错误的。火鸡的论证从一系列正确的观察结果出发，最终却得出了一个错误的结论，这清楚地表明，从逻辑的角度来看，这个论证是无效的。

This straightforward point is illustrated by a somewhat gruesome example attributed to Bertrand Russell. It concerns a turkey who noted on his first morning at the turkey farm that he was fed at 9 am. After this experience had been repeated daily for several weeks the turkey felt safe in drawing the conclusuion ‘I am always fed at 9 am’. Alas, this conclusion was shown to be false in no uncertain manner when, on Christmas eve, instead of being fed, the turkey’s throat was cut. The turkey’s argument led it from a number of true observations to a false conclusion, clearly indicating the invalidity of the argument from a logical point of view.

我以金属膨胀为例所阐述的那种论证，即从有限的具体事实推导出普遍结论的论证，被称为归纳论证，区别于逻辑演绎论证。归纳论证区别于演绎论证的一个特点是，它从关于某一类事件的陈述推导出关于所有此类事件的陈述，从而超越了前提所包含的内容。一般的科学定律总是超越了可用于支持它们的有限可观察证据，这就是为什么它们永远无法通过逻辑推导从这些证据中得出。

Arguments of the kind I have illustrated with the example concerning the expansion of metals, which proceed from a finite number of specific facts to a general conclusion, are called inductive arguments, as distinct from logical, deductive arguments. A characteristic of inductive arguments that distinguishes them from deductive ones is that, by proceeding as they do from statements about some to statements about all events of a particular kind, they go beyond what is contained in the premises. General scientific laws invariably go beyond the finite amount of observable evidence that is available to support them, and that is why they can never be proven in the sense of being logically deduced from that evidence.

好的归纳论证应具备哪些要素？

What constitutes a good inductive argument?

我们已经看到，如果要将科学知识理解为源于事实，那么“源于”一词必须理解为归纳而非演绎。但是，一个好的归纳论证应具备哪些特征呢？这个问题至关重要，因为显然并非所有基于可观察事实的概括都是合理的。有些概括我们会认为过于草率或证据不足，例如，我们可能会谴责仅仅因为与一对邻居有过一些不愉快的经历就将某种特征归于整个族群的做法。那么，究竟在什么情况下，我们才能合法地断言某个科学定律是从有限的观察和实验证据中“推导”出来的呢？

We have seen that if scientific knowledge is to be understood as being derived from the facts, then ‘derive’ must be understood in an inductive rather than a deductive sense. But what are the characteristics of a good inductive argument? The question is of fundamental importance because it is clear that not all generalisations from the observable facts are warranted. Some of them we will wish to regard as overhasty or based on insufficient evidence, as when, perhaps, we condemn the attribution of some characteristic to an entire ethnic group based on some unpleasant encounters with just one pair of neighbours. Under precisely what circumstances is it legitimate to assert that a scientific law has been ‘derived’ from some finite body of observational and experimental evidence?

对这个问题的初步解答涉及这样一个要求：如果要证明从可观察的事实到规律的归纳推理是合理的，那么必须满足以下条件：

A first attempt at an answer to this question involves the demand that, if an inductive inference from observable facts to laws is to be justified, then the following conditions must be satisfied:

1. 构成概括基础的观察数量必须很大。

1. The number of observations forming the basis of a generalisation must be large.

2. 必须在各种条件下重复进行观察。

2. The observations must be repeated under a wide variety of conditions.

3. 任何被接受的观察陈述都不应与推导出的定律相冲突。

3. No accepted observation statement should conflict with the derived law.

条件1被认为是必要的，因为仅仅根据对一根铁棒膨胀的一次观察就得出所有金属受热都会膨胀的结论显然是不合理的，正如仅仅根据对一个醉酒的澳大利亚人的一次观察就得出所有澳大利亚人都是酒鬼的结论一样。在证明任何概括的合理性之前，似乎都需要大量的独立观察。一个好的归纳论证不会草率下结论。

Condition 1 is regarded as necessary because it is clearly not legitimate to conclude that all metals expand when heated on the basis of just one observation of an iron bar’s expansion, say, any more than it is legitimate to conclude that all Australians are drunkards on the basis of one observation of an intoxicated Australian. A large number of independent observations would appear to be necessary before either generalisation can be justified. A good inductive argument does not jump to conclusions.

增加上述例子中观察次数的一种方法是反复加热同一块金属，或者持续观察某个澳大利亚人夜复一夜、甚至可能天天早上都喝醉。显然，以这种方式获得的观察记录清单对于相应的概括而言是非常不充分的。这就是条件2的必要性所在。“所有金属受热膨胀”这一概括只有在其所依据的膨胀观察涵盖各种条件的情况下才是合理的。应该加热各种金属，例如长条、短条、银条、铜条等等，并在高压、低压、高温、低温等条件下进行加热。只有在所有这些情况下都观察到膨胀，才能通过归纳法得出普遍规律。此外，显而易见，如果观察到某个特定金属样品在加热时没有膨胀，那么得出该规律的概括就不成立。条件3至关重要。

One way of increasing the number of observations in the examples mentioned would be to repeatedly heat a single bar of metal or to continually observe a particular Australian getting drunk night after night, and perhaps morning after morning. Clearly, a list of observation statements acquired in such a way would form a very unsatisfactory basis for the respective generalisations. That is why Condition 2 is necessary. ‘All metals expand when heated’ will be a legitimate generalisation only if the observations of expansion on which it is based range over a wide variety of conditions. Various kinds of metals should be heated, long bars, short bars, silver bars, copper bats, etc. should be heated at high and low pressures and high and low temperatures and so on. Only if on all such occasions expansion results is it legitimate to generalise by induction to the general law. Further, it is evident that if a particular sample of metal is observed not to expand when heated, then the generalisation to the law will not be justified. Condition 3 is essential.

以上内容可以用以下归纳原理的陈述来概括。

The above can be summed up by the following statement of the principle of induction.

如果在各种条件下观察到大量的A ，并且所有这些A无一例外地具有性质B，那么所有A都具有性质B。

If a large number of As have been observed under a wide variety of conditions, and if all those As without exception possess the property B, then all As have the property B.

这种对归纳法的描述存在严重问题。我们来看条件一，即对大量观察数据的要求。其中一个问题是“大量”一词的模糊性。究竟需要一百次、一千次还是更多观察数据？如果我们试图通过引入一个数字来保证精确性，那么所选数字必然带有很大的随意性。问题还不止于此。在许多情况下，对大量实例的要求似乎并不恰当。例如，二战末期，第一颗原子弹投向广岛，引发了公众对核战争的强烈反对。这种反对源于人们认识到原子弹会造成广泛的破坏和人类的苦难。然而，这种广泛而合理的信念仅仅基于一次震撼人心的观察。同样，如果一个研究者坚持多次将手伸入火中才得出“火会燃烧”的结论，那他未免也太固执了。让我们来看一个与科学实践相关的、不那么虚构的例子。假设我重复了近期某科学期刊上发表的一项实验，并将结果投稿发表。期刊编辑肯定会拒稿，理由是这项实验已经有人做过了！条件1存在诸多问题。

There are serious problems with this characterisation of induction. Let us consider Condition 1, the demand for large numbers of observations. One problem with it is the vagueness of ‘large’. Are a hundred, a thousand or more observations required? If we do attempt to introduce precision by introducing a number here, then there would surely be a great deal of arbitrariness in the number chosen. The problems do not stop here. There are many instances in which the demand for a large number of instances seems inappropriate. To illustrate this, consider the strong public reaction against nuclear warfare that was provoked by the dropping of the first atomic bomb on Hiroshima towards the end of the Second World War. That reaction was based on the realisation of the extent to which atomic bombs cause widespread destruction and human suffering. And yet this widespread, and surely reasonable, belief was based on just one dramatic observation. In a similar vein, it would be a very stubborn investigator who insisted on putting his hand in the fire many times before concluding that fire burns. Let us consider a less fanciful example related to scientific practice. Suppose I reproduced an experiment reported in some recent scientific journal, and sent my results off for publication. Surely the editor of the journal would reject my paper, explaining that the experiment had already been done! Condition 1 is riddled with problems.

条件2也存在严重问题，其根源在于如何界定何为显著的环境变化。在研究加热金属膨胀的实验中，何为显著的环境变化？是否需要改变金属种类、压力和时间？对于第一种情况，答案是“是”，对于第二种情况，答案可能也是“是”，但对于第三种情况，答案是否定的。那么，这个答案的依据是什么呢？这个问题至关重要，因为如果无法解答，那么可以通过不断添加其他变化因素（例如实验室的大小和实验者袜子的颜色）来无限扩展变化列表。除非能够消除这些“多余的”变化，否则归纳推理成立的条件就永远无法满足。那么，我们凭什么认为一系列可能的变化是多余的呢？常识性的答案其实很简单。我们会利用对情况的先验知识来区分哪些因素可能影响我们正在研究的系统，哪些因素则不会。我们对金属及其作用方式的了解，使我们预期金属的物理行为取决于金属种类和周围压力，而与一天中的时间或实验者袜子的颜色无关。我们运用现有的知识储备来判断在研究某种效应的普遍性时，哪些相关因素需要改变。

Condition 2 has serious problems too, stemming from difficulties surrounding the question of what counts as a significant variation in circumstances. What counts as a significant variation in the circumstances under which the expansion of a heated metal is to be investigated? Is it necessary to vary the type of metal, the pressure and the time of day? The answer is ‘yes’ in the first and possibly the second case but ‘no’ in the third. But what are the grounds for that answer? The question is important because unless it can be answered the list of variations can be extended indefinitely by endlessly adding further variations, such as the size of the laboratory and the colour of the experimenter’s socks. Unless such ‘superfluous’ variations can be eliminated, the conditions under which an inductive inference can be accepted can never be satisfied. What are the grounds, then, for regarding a range of possible variations as superfluous? The commonsense answer is straightforward enough. We draw on our prior knowledge of the situation to distinguish between the factors that might and those that cannot influence the system we are investigating. It is our knowledge of metals and the kinds of ways that they can be acted on that leads us to the expectation that their physical behaviour will depend on the type of metal and the surrounding pressure but not on the time of day or the colour of the experimenter’s socks. We draw on our current stock of knowledge to help judge what is a relevant circumstance that might need to be varied when investigating the generality of an effect under investigation.

这种对问题的回应无疑是正确的。然而，它对“科学知识应当通过归纳法从事实中推导而来”这一论断提出了一个足够强有力的问题。问题在于，当我们提出这样的问题：在判断某些情况与所研究现象（例如金属的膨胀）的相关性时，所援引的知识本身又该如何得到验证？如果我们要求这种知识本身必须通过归纳法获得，那么我们的问题就会再次出现，因为这些进一步的归纳论证本身又需要对相关情况进行具体说明，如此循环往复。每一个归纳论证都涉及对先前知识的诉求，而这些先前知识又需要归纳论证来证明其合理性，如此往复，形成一个永无止境的循环。要求所有知识都必须通过归纳法来证明其合理性，最终将成为一个无法满足的要求。

This response to the problem is surely correct. However, it poses a problem for a sufficiently strong version of the claim that scientific knowledge should be derived from the facts by induction. The problem arises when we pose the question of how the knowledge appealed to when judging the relevance or otherwise of some circumstances to a phenomenon under investigation (such as the expansion of metals) is itself vindicated. If we demand that that knowledge itself is to be arrived at by induction, then our problem will recur, because those further inductive arguments will themselves require the specification of the relevant circumstances and so on. Each inductive argument invovles an appeal to prior knowledge, which needs an inductive argument to justify it, which involves an appeal to further prior knowledge and so on in a never-ending chain. The demand that all knowledge be justified by induction becomes a demand that cannot be met.

即使是条件3也存在问题，因为几乎没有科学知识能够经受住“不存在任何已知例外”这一要求的考验。这一点将在第七章详细讨论。

Even Condition 3 is problematic since little scientific knowledge would survive the demand that there be no known exceptions. This is a point that will be discussed in some detail in chapter 7.

归纳主义的进一步问题

Further problems with inductivism

我们将那种认为科学知识应通过某种归纳推理从可观察事实中推导出来的立场称为归纳主义，并将持这种观点的人称为归纳主义者。我们已经指出了这种观点固有的一个严重问题，即如何准确地说明概括在何种条件下才构成有效的归纳推理。也就是说，归纳究竟意味着什么并不明确。归纳主义立场还存在其他问题。

Let us call the position according to which scientific knowledge is to be derived from the observable facts by some kind of inductive inference inductivism and those who subscribe to that view inductivists. We have already pointed to a serious problem inherent in that view, namely, the problem of stating precisely under what conditions a generalisation constitutes a good inductive inference. That is, it is not clear what induction amounts to. There are further problems with the inductivist position.

如果我们对当代科学知识抱持某种程度的真实态度，那么就不得不承认，其中很多知识都指向不可观测的事物。例如质子和电子、基因和DNA分子等等。那么，如何将这类知识纳入归纳主义的立场呢？归纳推理涉及从可观测事实进行某种概括，而这种推理似乎无法得出关于不可观测事物的知识。任何从可观测世界的事实出发的概括，除了对可观测世界的世代传承之外，别无他物。因此，我们讨论过的这种归纳推理永远无法建立关于不可观测世界的科学知识。这使得归纳主义者陷入了尴尬的境地：他们不得不拒绝许多当代科学，理由是这些科学涉及的内容超出了从可观测事物进行归纳概括所能论证的范围。

If we take contemporary scientific knowledge at anything like face value, then it has to be admitted that much of that knowledge refers to the unobservable. It refers to such things as protons and electrons, genes and DNA molecules and so on. How can such knowledge be accommodated into the inductivist position? Insofar as inductive reasoning involves some kind of generalisation from observable facts, it would appear that such reasoning is not capable of yielding knowledge of the unobservable. Any generalisation from facts about the observable world can yield nothing other than generations about the observable world. Consequently, scientific knowledge of the unobservable world can never be established by the kind of inductive reasoning we have discussed. This leaves the inductivist in the uncomfortable position of having to reject much contemporary science on the grounds that it involves going beyond what can be justified by inductive generalisation from the observable.

另一个问题源于许多科学定律都以精确的数学公式形式呈现。万有引力定律就是一个简单的例子，它指出任意两个物体之间的引力与这两个物体的质量乘积成正比，再除以它们之间距离的平方。与这些定律的精确性相比，构成其可观测证据的任何测量都存在不精确性。众所周知，所有观测都存在一定程度的误差，这体现在科学家将特定测量结果表示为x ± dx的实践中，其中dx代表估计的误差范围。如果科学定律是基于可观测事实的归纳概括，那么很难想象如何才能避免构成归纳论证前提的测量本身的不精确性。也很难想象如何能够基于不精确的证据对精确的定律进行归纳证明。

Another problem stems from the fact that many scientific laws take the form of exact, mathematically formulated laws. The law of gravitation, which states that the force between any two masses is proportional to the product of those masses divided by the square of the distance that separates them, is a straightforward example. Compared with the exactness of such laws we have the inexactness of any of the measurements that constitute the observable evidence for them. It is well appreciated that all observations are subject to some degree of error, as reflected in the practice of scientists when they write the result of a particular measurement as x ± dx, where dx represents the estimated margin of error. If scientific laws are inductive generalisations from observable facts it is difficult to see how one can escape the inexactness of the measurements that constitute the premises of the inductive arguments. It is difficult to see how exact laws can ever be inductively justified on the basis of inexact evidence.

归纳主义者面临的第三个问题是哲学界由来已久的“归纳问题”。这个问题适用于任何认同以下观点的人：科学知识的各个方面都必须通过诉诸（演绎）逻辑或从经验中推导出来证明其合理性。大卫·休谟是十八世纪的一位哲学家，他正是持这种观点的人，而他清晰地阐述了我即将着重指出的这个问题。

A third problem for the inductivist is an old philosophical chestnut called the problem of induction. The problem arises for anyone who subscribes to the view that scientific knowledge in all its aspects must be justified either by an appeal to (deductive) logic or by deriving it from experience. David Hume was an eighteenth-century philosopher who did subscribe to that view, and it was he who clearly articulated the problem I am about to highlight.

当我们提出如何证明归纳本身的合理性时，问题就出现了。归纳原则该如何得到证实？持这种观点的人只有两种选择：诉诸逻辑或诉诸经验。我们已经看到，第一种选择行不通。归纳推理并非逻辑（演绎）推理。这就只剩下第二种选择，即尝试诉诸经验来证明归纳的合理性。这样的证明会是什么样的呢？大概会是这样：归纳法已被证明在许多情况下都有效。例如，光学定律是通过实验室实验结果归纳推导出来的，并已被多次用于设计运行良好的光学仪器；行星运动定律是通过观测行星位置归纳推导出来的，并已被成功用于预测日食和合相。这份清单还可以大大扩展，列出许多基于归纳法推导出的科学定律和理论而做出的成功预测和解释。因此，有人认为，归纳法是经验所证明的。

The problem arises when we raise the question of how induction itself is to be justified. How is the principle of induction to be vindicated? Those who take the view under discussion have only two options, to justify it by an appeal to logic or by an appeal to experience. We have already seen that the first option will not do. Inductive inferences are not logical (deductive) inferences. This leaves us with the second option, to attempt to justify induction by an appeal to experience. What would such a justification be like? Presumably, it would go something like this. Induction has been observed to work on a large number of occasions. For instance, the laws of optics, derived by induction from the results of laboratory experiments, have been used on numerous occasions in the design of optical instruments that have operated satisfactorily, and the laws of planetary motion, inductively derived from the observation of planetary positions, have been successfully used to predict eclipses and conjunctions. This list could be greatly extended with accounts of successful predictions and explanations that we presume to be made on the basis of inductively derived scientific laws and theories. Thus, so the argument goes, induction is justified by experience.

这种归纳法的论证是不可接受的。这一点可以从以下以示意图形式阐明的论证形式中看出：

This justification of induction is unacceptable. This can be seen once the form of the argument is spelt out schematically as follows:

归纳法原理偶尔会成功应用一次。

The principle of induction worked successfully on occasion x1

归纳法原理偶尔会成功应用两次等等。

The principle of induction worked successfully on occasion x2 etc.

归纳原理总是有效的。

The principle of induction always works.

本文通过列举若干成功运用归纳推理的实例，推导出归纳推理原则的有效性这一普遍论断。因此，该论证本身就是一个归纳论证。由此可见，试图诉诸经验来证明归纳推理的合理性，实际上是预设了自己试图证明的内容。这种做法本质上是用归纳推理本身来证明归纳推理的合理性，因此是完全站不住脚的。

A general statement asserting the validity of the principle of induction is here inferred from a number of individual instances of its successful application. The argument is therefore itself an inductive one. Consequently, the attempt to justify induction by an appeal to experience involves assuming what one is trying to prove. It involves justifying induction by appealing to induction, and so is totally unsatisfactory.

一种规避归纳问题的方法在于弱化对科学知识必须被证明为真的要求，而满足于“根据现有证据，科学论断很可能为真”这一断言。例如，虽然大量的观测结果可以用来支持“密度大于空气的物质在地球上会向下沉降”这一论断，但这并不能证明该论断的真实性，却足以证明该论断很可能为真。基于此，我们可以将归纳原理重新表述为：“如果在各种条件下观察到大量A，并且所有这些观察到的A都具有性质B，那么所有A很可能都具有性质B。”然而，这种重新表述并没有克服归纳问题。重新表述的原理仍然是一个普遍性陈述。它基于有限数量的成功案例，暗示着该原理的所有应用都将得出很可能为真的普遍结论。因此，试图通过诉诸经验来证明归纳原则的概率版本是合理的，这涉及到诉诸归纳论证，而这种归纳论证正是该原则在其原始形式中所证明的那种论证。

One attempt to avoid the problem of induction involves weakening the demand that scientific knowledge be proven true, and resting content with the claim that scientific claims can be shown to be probably true in the light of the evidence. So the vast number of observations that can be invoked to support the claim that materials denser than air fall downwards on earth, although it does not permit us to prove the truth of the claim, does warrant the assertion that the claim is probably true. In line with this suggestion we can reformulate the principle of induction to read, ‘if a large number of As have been observed under a wide variety of conditions, and if all these observed As have the property B, then all As probably have the property B’. This reformulation does not overcome the problem of induction. The reformulated principle is still a universal statement. It implies, on the basis of a finite number of successes, that all applications of the principle will lead to general conclusions that are probably true. Consequently, attempts to justify the probabilistic version of the principle of induction by an appeal to experience involve an appeal to inductive arguments of the kind that are being justified just as the principle in its original form did.

对归纳论证的解释存在另一个根本问题，即将其解读为得出概率真理而非真理。一旦试图根据特定证据精确判断某个定律或理论的概率，这个问题就会出现。直觉上，随着对普遍规律的观察支持增加，其为真的概率也会增加，这似乎合情合理。但这种直觉经不起推敲。根据标准的概率论，我们很难不得出这样的结论：无论观察证据如何，任何普遍规律的概率都为零。通俗地讲，任何观察证据都由有限数量的观察陈述构成，而普遍规律则对无穷多种可能的情况做出断言。因此，根据现有证据，该规律的概率是一个有限数除以无穷大，无论有限数量的证据增加多少倍，该概率始终为零。换个角度来看，就像可以通过有限数量的点画出无限多条曲线一样，总会有无限多的普遍性陈述与有限数量的观察陈述相符。也就是说，总会有无限多的假设与有限数量的证据相符。因此，任何一个假设为真的概率都为零。第十二章我们将讨论解决这个问题的一种可能方法。

There is another basic problem with interpretations of inductive arguments that construe them as leading to probable truth rather than truth. This problem arises as soon as one tries to be precise about just how probable a law or theory is in the light of specified evidence. It may seem intuitively plausible that as the observational support for a general law increases the probability that it is true also increases. But this intuition does not stand up to inspection. Given standard probability theory, it is difficult to avoid the conclusion that the probability of any general law is zero whatever the observational evidence. To make the point in a non-technical way, any observational evidence will consist of a finite number of observation statements, whereas the general law will make claims about an infinity of possible cases. The probability of the law in the light of the evidence is thus a finite number divided by infinity, which remains zero by whatever factor the finite amount of evidence is increased. Looking at it in another way, there will always be an infinite number of general statements that are compatible with a finite number of observation statements, just as there is an infinity of curves that can be drawn through a finite number of points. That is, there will always be an infinite number of hypotheses compatible with a finite amount of evidence. Consequently, the probability of any one of them being true is zero. In chapter 12 we will discuss a possible way around this problem.

在本节和前一节中，我们揭示了“科学知识源于事实，并通过某种归纳推理得出”这一观点存在的两类问题。第一类问题涉及如何界定何为充分的归纳论证。第二类问题则涉及为归纳论证辩护时所陷入的循环论证。我认为前者比后者更为严重。我之所以没有过分重视归纳论证的问题，是因为任何试图解释科学的尝试都必然会遇到类似的问题。如果我们试图为所使用的每一个原则都寻找合理的论证，就必然会陷入困境，因为我们无法在不预设论证前提的情况下，为理性论证本身提供合理的论证。即使是逻辑本身，也无法在不陷入循环论证的情况下进行论证。然而，何为有效的演绎论证可以非常精确地界定，而何为良好的归纳论证却始终没有明确的答案。

In this and the preceding section we have revealed two kinds of problem with the idea that scientific knowledge is derived from the facts by some kind of inductive inference. The first concerned the issue of specifying just what an adequate inductive argument is. The second involved the circularity involved in attempts to justify induction. I regard the former problem as more severe than the latter. The reason that I do not take the problem of induction too seriously is that any attempt to provide an account of science is bound to confront a problem of a similar kind. We are bound to run into trouble if we seek rational justifications of every principle we use, for we cannot provide a rational argument for rational argument itself without assuming what we are arguing for. Not even logic can be argued for in a way that is not question begging. However, what constitutes a valid deductive argument can be specified with a high degree of precision, whereas what constitutes a good inductive argument has not been made at all clear.

归纳主义的吸引力

The appeal of inductivism

归纳主义科学观的简洁表达，即科学知识是通过归纳推理从事实中得出的观点，我们在本书的开头几章中讨论过，包含在二十世纪经济学家A.B.沃尔夫所写的以下段落中。

A concise expression of the inductivist view of science, the view that scientific knowledge is derived from the facts by inductive inference, which we have discusssed in the opening chapters of this book, is contained in the following passage written by a twentieth-century economist, A. B. Wolfe.

如果我们试着想象一个拥有超人般力量和洞察力，但在逻辑思维方面却与常人无异的头脑……会如何运用科学方法，那么这个过程大致如下：首先，所有事实都会被观察和记录，不进行任何选择，也不预先猜测它们的相对重要性。其次，对观察和记录的事实进行分析、比较和分类，除了思维逻辑中必然存在的假设或公理之外，不引入任何其他假设或公设。第三，从对事实的分析中，归纳出它们之间分类或因果关系的概括。第四，进一步的研究将结合演绎和归纳，运用先前已建立的概括进行推论。
