If we try to imagine how a mind of superhuman power and reach, but normal so far as the logical processes of its thought are concerned . . . would use the scientific method, the process would be as follows: First, all facts would be observed and recorded, without selection or a priori guess as to their relative importance. Secondly, the observed and recorded facts would be analysed, compared and classified, without hypothesis or postulates, other than those necessarily involved in the logic of thought. Third, from this analysis of the facts, generalizations would be inductively drawn as to the relations, classificatory or causal, between them. Fourth, further research would be deductive as well as inductive, employing inferences from previously established generalisations.1

我们已经看到，认为事实的收集可以而且应该先于任何知识的获取和接受而进行的观点，经不起推敲。反之，就等于认为我对澳大利亚丛林植物的观察会比训练有素的植物学家更有价值，仅仅因为我对植物学知之甚少。让我们摒弃经济学家对科学的这种描述。剩下的部分则颇具吸引力，如图2所示。构成科学知识的规律和理论，是通过归纳法，从观察和实验提供的事实基础中推导出来的。一旦掌握了这种普遍知识，就可以利用它进行预测和解释。

We have seen that the idea that the collection of facts can and should take place prior to the acquisition and acceptance of any knowledge does not bear analysis. To suggest otherwise is to believe that my observations of the flora in the Australian bush will be of more value than those of a trained botanist precisely because I know little botany. Let us reject this part of our economist’s characterisation of science. What remains is an account that has a certain appeal. It is summarised in Figure 2. The laws and theories that make up scientific knowledge are derived by induction from a factual basis supplied by observation and experiment. Once such general knowledge is available, it can be drawn on to make predictions and offer explanations.

图 2

Figure 2

请考虑以下论证：

Consider the following argument:

1. 相当纯净的水在 0°C 左右结冰（如果给予足够的时间）。

1. Fairly pure water freezes at about 0°C (if given sufficient time).

2. 我的汽车散热器里装的是相当纯净的水。

2. My car radiator contains fairly pure water.

3. 如果温度远低于 0°C，我的汽车散热器中的水就会结冰（如果时间足够长的话）。

3. If the temperature falls well below 0°C, the water in my car radiator will freeze (if given sufficient time).

这里我们举了一个有效的逻辑论证示例，该论证可以从前提1所包含的科学知识推导出预测3。如果1和2为真，那么3必然为真。然而，1、2或3的真假并非通过此推论或其他任何推论来确立。对于归纳主义者而言，科学真理的来源是经验而非逻辑。根据这种观点，1可以通过直接观察各种水结冰的实例来确定。一旦通过观察和归纳证实了1和2，那么就可以从中推导出预测3。

Here we have an example of a valid logical argument to deduce the prediction 3 from the scientific knowledge contained in premise 1. If 1 and 2 are true, 3 must be true. However, the truth of 1, 2 or 3 is not established by this or any other deduction. For the inductivist the source of scientific truth is experience not logic. On this view, 1 will be ascertained by direct observation of various instances of freezing water. Once 1 and 2 have been established by observation and induction, then the prediction 3 can be deduced from them.

不那么简单的例子会更复杂，但观察、归纳和演绎所起的作用本质上仍然相同。最后，我将探讨归纳法如何解释物理科学对彩虹的解释。

Less trivial examples will be more complicated, but the roles played by observation, induction and deduction remain essentially the same. As a final example, I will consider the inductivist account of how physical science is able to explain the rainbow.

前例中的简单前提1在此被一系列支配光行为的定律所取代，即光的反射定律和折射定律，以及关于折射量与光颜色之间关系的论断。这些普遍定律需要通过归纳法从经验中推导出来。大量的实验室实验，例如让光线从镜面和水面反射，测量光线从空气到水、从水到空气等各种路径的折射角，并在各种不同的条件下进行实验，直到满足所有被认为能够从实验结果中归纳推导出光学定律的必要条件为止。

The simple premise 1 of the previous example is here replaced by a number of laws governing the behaviour of light, namely, the laws of reflection and refraction of light and assertions about the dependence of the amount of refraction on the colour of the light. These general laws are to be derived from experience by induction. A large number of laboratory experiments are performed, reflecting rays of light from mirrors and water surfaces, measuring angles of refraction for rays of light passing from air to water, water to air and so on, under a wide variety of circumstances, until whatever conditions are presumed to be necessary to warrant the inductive derivation of the laws of optics from the experimental results are satisfied.

我们前一个例子中的前提2也将被替换为一组更复杂的陈述。这些陈述将包括这样的断言：太阳相对于地球上的观察者位于天空中的某个特定位置，以及雨滴正从相对于观察者位于某个特定区域的云层中落下。这类描述所研究装置的陈述集合将被称为初始条件。实验装置的描述就是典型的初始条件。

Premise 2 of our previous example will also be replaced by a more complex array of statements. These will include assertions to the effect that the sun is situated in some specified position in the sky relative to an observer on earth, and that raindrops are falling from a cloud situated in some specified region relative to the observer. Sets of statements like these, which describe the set-up under investigation, will be referred to as initial conditions. Descriptions of experimental set-ups will be typical initial conditions.

根据光学定律和初始条件，现在可以进行推导，从而解释观察者可见的彩虹的形成。这些推导不再像之前的例子那样显而易见，而是需要数学和文字论证。推导过程大致如下。假设雨滴近似球形，那么光线穿过雨滴的路径大致如图3所示。对于一束来自太阳的白光，当其入射到雨滴的a点时，根据折射定律，红光将沿ab传播，蓝光将沿ab₁传播。反射定律要求ab沿bc反射，ab₁沿b₁c₁反射。c点和c₁点的折射同样由折射定律决定，因此观察者在观察雨滴时会看到白光中的红光和蓝光成分分离（以及光谱中的所有其他颜色）。对于天空中任何一滴雨滴，只要它与太阳的连线与雨滴到观察者的连线之间的夹角为D ，观察者就能看到同样的颜色分离效果。几何学原理表明，只要雨云足够大，观察者就能看到一道彩色弧线。

Given the laws of optics and the initial conditions, it is now possible to perform deductions yielding an explanation of the formation of a rainbow visible to the observer. These deductions will no longer be as self-evident as in our previous examples, and will involve mathematical as well as verbal arguments. The derivation will run roughly as follows. If we assume a raindrop to be roughly spherical, then the path of a ray of light through a raindrop will be roughly as depicted in Figure 3. For a ray of white light from the sun incident on a raindrop at a, the red light will travel along ab and the blue light along ab1 according to the law of refraction. The law of reflection requires that ab be reflected along bc and ab1 along b1c1. Refraction at c and c1 will again be determined by the law of refraction, so that an observer viewing the raindrop will see the red and blue components of the white light separated (and also all the other colours of the spectrum). The same separation of colours will be visible to our observer for any raindrop that is situated in a region of the sky such that the line joining the raindrop to the sun makes an angle D with the line joining the raindrop to the observer. Geometrical considerations yield the conclusion that a coloured arc will be visible to the observer provided the rain cloud is sufficiently extended.

图 3

Figure 3

我在这里只是对彩虹的解释做了简要概述，但这足以说明其中涉及的推理的一般形式。假设光学定律是正确的（对于非专业归纳主义者来说，这可以通过归纳观察来证明），并且假设初始条件描述正确，那么彩虹的解释就必然成立。所有科学解释和预测的一般形式可以概括如下：

I have only sketched an explanation of the rainbow here, but it should suffice to illustrate the general form of the reasoning involved. Given that the laws of optics are true (and for the unqualified inductivist this can be established from observation by induction), and given that the initial conditions are correctly described, then the explanation of the rainbow necessarily follows. The general form of all scientific explanations and predictions can be summarised thus:

1. 定律和理论

1. Laws and theories

2. 初始条件

2. Initial conditions

3. 预测和解释

3. Predictions and explanations

这是图 2 右侧所示的步骤。

This is the step depicted on the right-hand side of Figure 2.

基本的归纳主义科学理论确实具有一定的吸引力。它的吸引力在于，它似乎以一种形式化的方式捕捉到了人们对科学知识特殊属性的一些普遍直觉，即科学知识的客观性、可靠性和实用性。在本节中，我们已经讨论了归纳主义对科学实用性的解释，因为它有助于预测和解释。

The basic inductivist account of science does have some immediate appeal. Its attraction lies in the fact that it does seem to capture in a formal way some of the commonly held intuitions about the special characteristics of scientific knowledge, namely, its objectivity, its reliability and its usefulness. We have discussed the inductivist account of the usefulness of science insofar as it can facilitate predictions and explanations already in this section.

归纳主义者对科学客观性的理解源于观察、归纳和演绎本身所被视为的客观程度。可观察的事实被认为是通过不带偏见地运用感官而确立的，这种方式不容许主观意见的介入。就归纳和演绎推理而言，它们的有效性取决于它们是否符合公开制定的有效性标准，因此，再次强调，个人意见没有立足之地。推论要么符合客观标准，要么不符合。

The objectivity of science as construed by the inductivist derives from the extent to which observation, induction and deduction are themselves seen as objective. Observable facts are understood to be established by an unprejudiced use of the senses in a way that leaves no room for subjective opinion to intrude. As far as inductive and deductive reasoning are concerned, these are adequate to the extent that they conform to publicly formulated criteria of adequacy, so, once again, there is no room for personal opinion. Inferences either conform to the objective standards or they don’t.

科学的可靠性源于归纳主义者关于观察以及归纳推理和演绎推理的主张。根据纯粹的归纳主义者的观点，构成科学事实基础的观察陈述可以通过仔细运用感官直接可靠地确立。此外，只要满足充分归纳概括的条件，这种可靠性也会传递到从这些事实归纳推导出的规律和理论。这由归纳原则保证，而归纳原则被认为是科学的基础。

The reliability of science follows from the inductivist’s claims about observation and both inductive and deductive reasoning. According to the unqualified inductivist, observation statements that form the factual basis for science can be securely established directly by careful use of the senses. Further, this security will be transmitted to the laws and theories inductively derived from those facts provided the conditions for adequate inductive generalisations are met. This is guaranteed by the principle of induction which is presumed to form the basis of science.

尽管归纳主义立场看似很有吸引力，但我们已经看到，它充其量需要进行严格的限定，最坏的情况是，它完全不适用。我们已经看到，足以用于科学的事实绝非唾手可得，而是需要通过实践构建，在某些重要意义上依赖于它们所预设的知识（图2的示意图忽略了这一复杂性），并且这些事实本身也需要改进和更新。更严重的是，我们一直无法对归纳法给出精确的定义，从而区分基于事实的合理概括和仓促或草率的概括。考虑到自然界不断带来惊喜的能力（例如过冷液体可以逆流而上），这无疑是一项艰巨的任务。

Attractive as it may have appeared, we have seen that the inductivist position is, at best, in need of severe qualification and, at worst, thoroughly inadequate. We have seen that facts adequate for science are by no means straightforwardly given but have to be practically constructed, are in some important senses dependent on the knowledge that they presuppose, a complication overlooked in the schematisation in Figure 2, and are subject to improvement and replacement. More seriously, we have been unable to give a precise specification of induction in a way that will help distinguish a justifiable generalisation from the facts from a hasty or rash one, a formidable task given nature’s capacity to surprise, epitomised in the discovery that supercooled liquids can flow uphill.

第十二章我们将探讨一些近期试图挽救归纳主义科学理论困境的尝试。同时，在接下来的两章中，我们将转向一位哲学家，他试图通过提出一种不涉及归纳的科学观来规避归纳法的问题。

In chapter 12 we will discuss some recent attempts to rescue the inductivist account of science from its difficulties. Meanwhile, we will turn in the next two chapters to a philosopher who attempts to sidestep problems with induction by putting forward a view of science that does not involve induction.

延伸阅读

Further reading

休谟归纳问题的历史渊源可追溯至休谟的《人性论》（1939，第三部分）。另一部经典论述见于罗素（1912，第六章）。斯托夫（1973）对休谟论证的后果进行了全面而深入的技术性考察。波普尔声称已解决了归纳问题，相关论述见于波普尔（1979，第一章）。亨佩尔（1966）和萨尔蒙（1966）对归纳推理的阐述较为易懂，而格莱穆尔（1980）则提供了更为详尽的论述。拉卡托斯（1968）的论文集也值得一提，其中收录了拉卡托斯本人撰写的一篇颇具启发性的论文，探讨了构建归纳逻辑的各种尝试。穆斯格雷夫（1993）对该问题进行了优秀的历史回顾。

The historical source of Hume’s problem of induction is Hume’s Treatise on Human Nature (1939, Part 3). Another classic discussion of the problem is Russell (1912, chapter 6). A thorough, technical investigation of the consequences of Hume’s argument is Stove (1973). Karl Popper’s claim to have solved the problem of induction is in Popper (1979, chapter 1). Reasonably accessible accounts of inductive reasoning can be found in Hempel (1966) and Salmon (1966), and a more detailed treatment is found in Glymour (1980). See also Lakatos (1968) for a collection of essays, including a provocative survey by Lakatos himself, of attempts to construct an inductive logic. Musgrave (1993) is a good historical survey of the problem.

第五章

CHAPTER 5

引入证伪主义

Introducing falsificationism

介绍

Introduction

卡尔·波普尔是“证伪主义”这一替代归纳主义理论的最有力倡导者。波普尔于20世纪20年代在维也纳接受教育，当时一群被称为“维也纳学派”的哲学家正在阐述逻辑实证主义。其中最著名的人物之一是鲁道夫·卡尔纳普，他的支持者与波普尔的支持者之间的冲突和辩论，在20世纪60年代之前一直是科学哲学的一个显著特征。波普尔本人讲述了他如何对“科学的特殊之处在于它可以从事实中推导出来，而且事实越多越好”这种观点感到失望。他开始怀疑弗洛伊德主义者和马克思主义者是如何通过解释各种各样的人类行为或历史变迁的实例来支持他们的理论，并声称这些实例因此得到了支持。在波普尔看来，这些理论似乎永远不会出错，因为它们足够灵活，可以容纳任何与自身理论相符的人类行为或历史变迁。因此，尽管这些理论看似强大，并得到了大量事实的证实，但实际上它们什么也解释不了，因为它们无法排除任何可能性。波普尔将此与爱丁顿在1919年进行的一项著名的爱因斯坦广义相对论检验进行了比较。爱因斯坦的理论认为，光线在靠近太阳等大质量物体时会发生弯曲。因此，位于太阳之外的恒星在观测方向上应该与没有这种弯曲时的方向有所不同。为了寻找这种偏移，爱丁顿在日食遮蔽太阳光线时观测了这颗恒星。结果发现确实观测到了这种偏移，爱因斯坦的理论得到了证实。但波普尔指出，情况并非总是如此。通过做出一个具体的、可检验的预测，广义相对论本身就面临着风险。 It ruled out observations that clashed with that prediction. Popper drew the moral that genuine scientific theories, by making definite predictions, rule out a range of observable states of affairs in a way that he considered Freudian and Marxist theory failed to do. He arrived at his key idea that scientific theories are falsifiable .

Karl Popper was the most forceful advocate of an alternative to inductivism that I will refer to as ‘falsificationism’. Popper was educated in Vienna in the 1920s, at a time when logical positivism was being articulated by a group of philosophers who became known as the Vienna Circle. One of the most famous of these was Rudolph Carnap, and the clash and debate between his supporters and those of Popper was to be a feature of philosophy of science up until the 1960s. Popper himself tells the story of how he became disenchanted with the idea that science is special because it can be derived from the facts, the more facts the better. He became suspicious of the way in which he saw Freudians and Marxists supporting their theories by interpreting a wide range of instances, of human behaviour or historical change respectively, in terms of their theory and claiming them to be supported on this account. It seemed to Popper that these theories could never go wrong because they were sufficiently flexible to accommodate any instances of human behaviour or historical change as compatible with their theory. Consequently, although giving the appearance of being powerful theories confirmed by a wide range of facts, they could in fact explain nothing because they could rule out nothing. Popper compared this with a famous test of Einstein’s theory of general relativity carried out by Eddington in 1919. Einstein’s theory had the implication that rays of light should bend as they pass close to massive objects such as the sun. As a consequence, a star situated beyond the sun should appear displaced from the direction in which it would be observed in the absence of this bending. Eddington sought for this displacement by sighting the star at a time when the light from the sun was blocked out by an eclipse. It transpired that the displacement was observed and Einstein’s theory was borne out. But Popper makes the point that it might not have been. By making a specific, testable prediction the general theory of relativity was at risk. It ruled out observations that clashed with that prediction. Popper drew the moral that genuine scientific theories, by making definite predictions, rule out a range of observable states of affairs in a way that he considered Freudian and Marxist theory failed to do. He arrived at his key idea that scientific theories are falsifiable.

证伪主义者坦然承认，观察受理论指导并以其为前提。他们也乐于放弃任何暗示理论可以根据观察证据被证实为真或可能为真的论断。理论被视为人类智力自由创造的推测性、试探性的猜想或推测，旨在克服先前理论遇到的问题，从而对世界或宇宙的某些方面做出充分的解释。一旦提出，推测性理论就必须通过观察和实验进行严格而无情的检验。经不起观察和实验检验的理论必须被摒弃，并由新的推测性猜想取而代之。科学的进步是通过反复试验、提出猜想和反驳来实现的。只有最合适的理论才能生存下来。虽然我们永远无法真正断言某个理论是正确的，但我们可以乐观地说，它是目前最好的理论；它优于以往任何理论。对于证伪主义者来说，归纳法的特征和正当性方面不存在任何问题，因为在他们看来，科学不涉及归纳法。

Falsificationists freely admit that observation is guided by and presupposes theory. They are also happy to abandon any claim implying that theories can be established as true or probably true in the light of observational evidence. Theories are construed as speculative and tentative conjectures or guesses freely created by the human intellect in an attempt to overcome problems encountered by previous theories to give an adequate account of some aspects of the world or universe. Once proposed, speculative theories are to be rigorously and ruthlessly tested by observation and experiment. Theories that fail to stand up to observational and experimental tests must be eliminated and replaced by further speculative conjectures. Science progresses by trial and error, by conjectures and refutations. Only the fittest theories survive. Although it can never be legitimately said of a theory that it is true, it can hopefully be said that it is the best available; that it is better than anything that has come before. No problems about the charactisation and justification of induction arises for the falsificationists because, according to them, science does not involve induction.

本文对证伪主义的简要概述内容将在接下来的两章中进行补充。

The content of this condensed summary of falsificationism will be filled out in the next two chapters.

支持证伪主义的一个逻辑论点

A logical point in favour of falsificationism

根据证伪主义，某些理论可以通过诉诸观察和实验结果来证明其错误。这里有一个简单而合乎逻辑的论点似乎支持证伪主义者的观点。我在第四章已经指出，即使我们假设能够以某种方式获得真实的观察陈述，也永远不可能仅凭此进行逻辑演绎来得出普遍规律和理论。然而，我们可以从个别的观察陈述出发，进行逻辑演绎，从而得出普遍规律和理论的错误结论。例如，如果我们得到这样的陈述：“在时间t ，在地点x观察到一只不是黑色的渡鸦”，那么由此逻辑地可以得出“所有渡鸦都是黑色的”是错误的。也就是说，论证如下：

According to falsificationism, some theories can be shown to be false by an appeal to the results of observation and experiment. There is a simple, logical point that seems to support the falsificationist here. I have already indicated in chapter 4 that, even if we assume that true observational statements are available to us in some way, it is never possible to arrive at universal laws and theories by logical deductions on that basis alone. However, it is possible to perform logical deductions starting from singular observation statements as premises, to arrive at the falsity of universal laws and theories by logical deduction. For example, if we are given the statement, ‘A raven which was not black was observed at place x at time t’, then it logically follows from this that ‘All ravens are black’ is false. That is, the argument:

前提——一只不是黑色的渡鸦在时间t位于地点x。

Premise – A raven, which was not black, was at place x at time t.

结论——并非所有的渡鸦都是黑色的。

Conclusion – Not all ravens are black.

这是一个逻辑上有效的推论。如果前提成立而结论不成立，则会产生矛盾。再举一两个例子有助于说明这个看似简单的逻辑要点。如果通过观察某个实验证明，一个十公斤的物体和一个一公斤的物体在自由落体运动中下落的速度大致相同，那么就可以得出结论：物体下落的速度与其重量成正比的说法是错误的。如果能够毫无疑问地证明，一束光线经过太阳附近时会发生偏转，那么就不能断言光必然沿直线传播。

is a logically valid deduction. If the premise is asserted and the conclusion denied, a contradiction is involved. One or two more examples will help illustrate this fairly trivial logical point. If it can be established by observation in some test experiment that a ten-kilogram weight and a one-kilogram weight in free fall move downwards at roughly the same speed, then it can be concluded that the claim that bodies fall at speeds proportional to their weight is false. If it can be demonstrated beyond doubt that a ray of light passing close to the sun is deflected in a curved path, then it is not the case that light necessarily travels in straight lines.

普遍命题的虚假性可以从适当的个别命题推导出来。证伪主义者充分利用了这一逻辑要点。

The falsity of universal statements can be deduced from suitable singular statements. The falsificationist exploits this logical point to the full.

可证伪性作为理论的标准

Falsifiability as a criterion for theories

证伪主义者将科学视为一系列假设的集合，这些假设被初步提出，旨在准确描述或解释世界或宇宙某些方面的运行规律。然而，并非任何假设都能胜任。任何假设或假设体系若要被赋予科学定律或理论的地位，都必须满足一个基本条件：可证伪性。在进一步探讨之前，有必要明确证伪主义者对“可证伪性”一词的用法。

The falsificationist sees science as a set of hypotheses that are tentatively proposed with the aim of accurately describing or accounting for the behaviour of some aspect of the world or universe. However, not any hypothesis will do. There is one fundamental condition that any hypothesis or system of hypotheses must satisfy if it is to be granted the status of a scientific law or theory. If it is to form part of science, a hypothesis must be falsifiable. Before proceeding any further, it is important to be clear about the falsificationist’s usage of the term ‘falsifiable’.

以下是一些简单且可证伪的断言示例，这些断言在预期的意义上是可以证伪的。

Here are some examples of some simple assertions that are falsifiable in the sense intended.

1. 星期三从来不下雨。

1. It never rains on Wednesdays.

2. 所有物质受热都会膨胀。

2. All substances expand when heated.

3. 砖块等重物在地球表面附近释放时，如果没有受到阻碍，就会垂直向下坠落。

3. Heavy objects such as a brick when released near the surface of the earth fall straight downwards if not impeded.

4. 当一束光线从平面镜反射时，入射角等于反射角。

4. When a ray of light is reflected from a plane mirror, the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.

断言1是可证伪的，因为可以通过观察星期三下雨来证伪它。断言2也是可证伪的。它可以通过观察某种物质x在时间t加热时没有膨胀来证伪。接近冰点的水可以用来证伪断言2。断言1和2都是可证伪的，并且是错误的。断言3和4可能是真的，就我所知。然而，它们在预期的意义上是可证伪的。从逻辑上讲，下一块被释放的砖块有可能向上“落下”。“砖块被释放后向上落下”这一断言本身并不包含逻辑矛盾，尽管可能没有任何观察结果支持这一断言。断言4是可证伪的，因为一束以一定倾斜角度入射到镜子上的光线，理论上可以沿垂直于镜子的方向反射。如果反射定律成立，这种情况永远不会发生，但即便成立，也不会产生逻辑矛盾。即使第3点和第4点可能为真，它们也都是可证伪的。

Assertion 1 is falsifiable because it can be falsified by observing rain to fall on a Wednesday. Assertion 2 is falsifiable. It can be falsified by an observation statement to the effect that some substance, x, did not expand when heated at time t. Water near its freezing point would serve to falsify 2. Both 1 and 2 are falsifiable and false. Assertions 3 and 4 may be true, for all I know. Nevertheless, they are falsifiable in the sense intended. It is logically possible that the next brick to be released will ‘fall’ upwards. No logical contradiction is involved in the assertion, ‘The brick fell upwards when released’, although it may be that no such statement is ever supported by observation. Assertion 4 is falsifiable because a ray of light incident on a mirror at some oblique angle could conceivably be reflected in a direction perpendicular to the mirror. This will never happen if the law of reflection happens to be true, but no logical contradiction would be involved if it did. Both 3 and 4 are falsifiable, even though they may be true.

如果存在逻辑上可能的观察陈述或一组观察陈述与某个假设不一致，即如果证实该假设为真，则会证伪该假设，那么该假设就是可证伪的。

A hypothesis is falsifiable if there exists a logically possible observation statement or set of observation statements that are inconsistent with it, that is, which, if established as true, would falsify the hypothesis.

以下是一些不符合此要求且因此不可证伪的陈述示例。

Here are some examples of statements that do not satisfy this requirement and that are consequently not falsifiable.

5. 要么下雨，要么没下雨。

5. Either it is raining or it is not raining.

6. 欧几里得圆上的所有点到圆心的距离都相等。

6. All points on a Euclidean circle are equidistant from the centre.

7. 体育投机中也可能存在运气成分。

7. Luck is possible in sporting speculation.

任何逻辑上合理的观察陈述都无法反驳第5条。无论天气如何，它都是正确的。断言6必然为真，因为欧几里得圆的定义决定了这一点。如果圆上的点到某个定点的距离不相等，那么这个图形就不是欧几里得圆。“所有单身汉都是未婚的”也因类似的原因而无法证伪。断言7引自报纸上的星座运势。它体现了算命先生惯用的狡猾伎俩。该断言无法证伪。它相当于告诉读者，如果他今天下注，他可能会赢，无论他是否下注，这个说法都成立；即使他下注了，无论他是否赢，这个说法也成立。

No logically possible observation statement could refute 5. It is true whatever the weather is like. Assertion 6 is necessarily true because of the definition of a Euclidean circle. If points on a circle were not equidistant from some fixed point, then that figure would just not be a Euclidean circle. ‘All bachelors are unmarried’ is unfalsifiable for a similar reason. Assertion 7 is quoted from a horoscope in a newspaper. It typifies the fortune-teller’s devious strategy. The assertion is unfalsifiable. It amounts to telling the reader that if he has a bet today he might win, which remains true whether he bets or not, and if he does, whether he wins or not.

证伪主义者要求科学假设必须是可证伪的，其含义如上所述。他们坚持这一点，是因为只有排除一组逻辑上可能的观察陈述，定律或理论才能提供信息。如果一个陈述不可证伪，那么世界可以拥有任何属性，可以以任何方式运行，而不会与该陈述相冲突。与断言1、2、3和4不同，断言5、6和7并没有告诉我们任何关于世界的信息。理想情况下，科学定律或理论应该提供一些关于世界实际运行方式的信息，从而排除那些（逻辑上）可能存在但实际上并非如此的运行方式。“所有行星都围绕太阳做椭圆运动”这条定律是科学的，因为它断言行星确实做椭圆运动，并排除了方形或椭圆形轨道。仅仅因为这条定律对行星轨道做出了明确的断言，它就具有信息价值，并且是可证伪的。

Falsificationists demand that scientific hypotheses be falsifiable, in the sense discussed. They insist on this because it is only by ruling out a set of logically possible observation statements that a law or theory is informative. If a statement is unfalsifiable, then the world can have any properties whatsoever, and can behave in any way whatsoever, without conflicting with the statement. Assertions 5, 6 and 7, unlike assertions 1, 2, 3 and 4, tell us nothing about the world. A scientific law or theory should ideally give us some information about how the world does in fact behave, thereby ruling out ways in which it could (logically) possibly behave but in fact does not. The law ‘All planets move in ellipses around the sun’ is scientific because it claims that planets in fact move in ellipses and rules out orbits that are square or oval. Just because the law makes definite claims about planetary orbits, it has informative content and is falsifiable.

粗略地看一下一些可能被视为科学理论典型组成部分的定律，就会发现它们符合可证伪性标准。“异性磁极相互吸引”、“酸加碱生成盐和水”等定律很容易被解释为可证伪的。然而，证伪主义者认为，有些理论虽然表面上看起来具备优秀科学理论的特征，但实际上只是伪装成科学理论，因为它们不可证伪，应该被驳斥。波普尔声称，至少马克思的历史理论、弗洛伊德的精神分析和阿德勒心理学的某些版本都存在这种缺陷。以下对阿德勒心理学的讽刺画可以说明这一点。

A cursory glance at some laws that might be regarded as typical components of scientific theories indicates that they satisfy the falsifiability criterion. ‘Unlike magnetic poles attract each other’, ‘An acid added to a base yields a salt plus water’ and similar laws can easily be construed as falsifiable. However, the falsificationist maintains that some theories, while they may superficially appear to have the characteristics of good scientific theories, are in fact only posing as scientific theories because they are not falsifiable and should be rejected. Popper has claimed that some versions at least of Marx’s theory of history, Freudian psychoanalysis and Adlerian psychology suffer from this fault. The point can be illustrated by the following caricature of Adlerian psychology.

阿德勒理论的一个基本信条是，人类的行为是由某种自卑感驱动的。在我们的例子中，以下事件佐证了这一点。一个男人站在一条湍急的河岸边，这时附近一个孩子落水。男人要么跳进河里救孩子，要么袖手旁观。如果他跳了下去，阿德勒的支持者会指出这如何支持他的理论。显然，男人需要克服自卑感，证明自己有足够的勇气不顾危险跳进河里。如果男人没有跳下去，阿德勒的支持者又可以再次声称他的理论得到了支持。男人通过展现自己有足够的意志力留在岸边，平静地看着孩子溺水，从而克服了自卑感。

A fundamental tenet of Adler’s theory is that human actions are motivated by feelings of inferiority of some kind. In our caricature, this is supported by the following incident. A man is standing on the bank of a treacherous river at the instant a child falls into the river nearby. The man will either leap into the river in an attempt to save the child or he will not. If he does leap in, the Adlerian responds by indicating how this supports his theory. The man obviously needed to overcome his feelings of inferiority by demonstrating that he was brave enough to leap into the river, in spite of the danger. If the man does not leap in, the Adlerian can again claim support for his theory. The man was overcoming his feelings of inferiority by demonstrating that he had the strength of will to remain on the bank, unperturbed, while the child drowned.

如果这种漫画式的描述是阿德勒理论运作方式的典型特征，那么该理论就无法证伪。它似乎与任何人类行为都相符，正因如此，它对人类行为本身却一无所知。当然，要以此为由驳斥阿德勒的理论，必须深入研究该理论的细节，而非仅仅关注漫画式的描述。然而，许多社会、心理和宗教理论都让人怀疑，它们试图解释一切，结果却什么也解释不了。例如，我们可以将慈爱的上帝的存在与灾难的发生相协调，只需将灾难解释为上帝派来考验我们或惩罚我们，无论哪种解释似乎最符合实际情况即可。许多动物行为的例子都可以被视为支持“动物的设计是为了更好地履行其被赋予的功能”这一论断的证据。以这种方式运作的理论家犯了算命先生的回避错误，理应受到证伪主义者的批评。一个理论要想具有参考价值，就必须承担被证伪的风险。

If this caricature is typical of the way in which Adlerian theory operates, then the theory is not falsifiable. It is consistent with any kind of human behaviour, and just because of that, it tells us nothing about human behaviour. Of course, before Adler’s theory can be rejected on these grounds, it would be necessary to investigate the details of the theory rather than a caricature. But there are plenty of social, psychological and religious theories that give rise to the suspicion that in their concern to explain everything they explain nothing. The existence of a loving God and the occurrence of some disaster can be made compatible by interpreting the disaster as being sent to try us or to punish us, whichever seems most suited to the situation. Many examples of animal behaviour can be seen as evidence supporting the assertion, ‘Animals are designed so as best to fulfil the function for which they were intended’. Theorists operating in this way are guilty of the fortune-teller’s evasion and are subject to the falsificationist’s criticism. If a theory is to have informative content, it must run the risk of being falsified.

可证伪程度、清晰度和精确度

Degree of falsifiability, clarity and precision

一个好的科学定律或理论之所以可证伪，仅仅是因为它对世界做出了明确的断言。对于证伪主义者来说，由此很容易得出这样的结论：一个理论越可证伪越好（这里“越好”指的是某种程度上的“越好”）。一个理论的断言越多，就越有可能证明世界实际上并非按照该理论所描述的方式运行。一个非常好的理论会对世界做出非常广泛的断言，因此它具有很高的可证伪性，并且在接受检验时能够经受住证伪的考验。

A good scientific law or theory is falsifiable just because it makes definite claims about the world. For the falsificationist, it follows fairly readily from this that the more falsifiable a theory is the better, in some loose sense of more. The more a theory claims, the more potential opportunities there will be for showing that the world does not in fact behave in the way laid down by the theory. A very good theory will be one that makes very wide-ranging claims about the world, and which is consequently highly falsifiable, and is one that resists falsification whenever it is put to the test.

这一点可以通过一个简单的例子来说明。请看以下定律：

The point can be illustrated by means of a trivial example. Consider these laws:

（a）火星绕太阳做椭圆运动。

(a) Mars moves in an ellipse around the sun.

（b）所有行星都围绕其太阳做椭圆运动。

(b) All planets move in ellipses around their sun.

我认为，(b) 作为一项科学知识，其地位显然高于 (a)。定律 (b) 不仅包含了 (a) 所包含的所有内容，而且还包含更多内容。定律 (b) 作为更可取的定律，比 (a) 更容易被证伪。如果对火星的观测结果最终证伪了 (a)，那么它们也会证伪 (b)。任何对 (a) 的证伪都将证伪 (b)，但反之则不然。那些可能证伪 (b) 的关于金星、木星等天体的轨道观测结果与 (a) 无关。如果我们沿用波普尔的观点，将那些可能证伪某条定律或理论的观测结果称为该定律或理论的潜在证伪者，那么我们可以说，(a) 的潜在证伪者构成了一个类，而这个类又是 (b) 的潜在证伪者的子类。法律（b）比法律（a）更容易被证伪，这相当于说它要求更多，它是更好的法律。

I take it that it is clear that (b) has a higher status than (a) as a piece of scientific knowledge. Law (b) tells us all that (a) tells us and more besides. Law (b), the preferable law, is more falsifiable than (a). If observations of Mars should turn out to falsify (a), then they would falsify (b) also. Any falsification of (a) will be a falsification of (b), but the reverse is not the case. Observation statements referring to the orbits of Venus, Jupiter, etc. that might conceivably falsify (b) are irrelevant to (a). If we follow Popper and refer to those sets of observation statements that would serve to falsify a law or theory as potential falsifiers of that law or theory, then we can say that the potential falsifiers of (a) form a class that is a subclass of the potential falsifiers of (b). Law (b) is more falsifiable than law (a), which is tantamount to saying that it claims more, that it is the better law.

一个不那么牵强的例子涉及开普勒太阳系理论和牛顿理论之间的关系。我把开普勒的理论理解为他的行星运动三大定律。该理论的潜在证伪点在于一些描述行星在特定时间相对于太阳位置的陈述。牛顿的理论更为完善，取代了开普勒的理论。它由牛顿运动定律和万有引力定律组成，后者指出宇宙中所有物体之间都存在相互吸引的力，该力与它们之间距离的平方成反比。牛顿理论的一些潜在证伪点也与行星在特定时间的位置有关。但还有许多其他的证伪点，例如关于落体运动和摆的运动、潮汐与太阳和月亮位置的相关性等等。相比之下，证伪牛顿理论的机会要多得多。然而，根据证伪主义者的说法，牛顿的理论能够经受住各种证伪尝试，从而确立了其优于开普勒的理论。

A less-contrived example involves the relation between Kepler’s theory of the solar system and Newton’s. Kepler’s theory I take to be his three laws of planetary motion. Potential falsifiers of that theory consist of sets of statements referring to planetary positions relative to the sun at specified times. Newton’s theory, a better theory that superseded Kepler’s, is more comprehensive. It consists of Newton’s laws of motion plus his law of gravitation, the latter asserting that all pairs of bodies in the universe attract each other with a force that varies inversely as the square of their separation. Some of the potential falsifiers of Newton’s theory are sets of statements of planetary positions at specified times. But there are many others, including those referring to the behaviour of falling bodies and pendulums, the correlation between the tides and the locations of the sun and moon, and so on. There are many more opportunities for falsifying Newton’s theory than for falsifying Kepler’s theory. And yet, so the falsificationist story goes, Newton’s theory was able to resist attempted falsifications, thereby establishing its superiority over Kepler’s.

因此，只要尚未被证伪，高度可证伪的理论就应该优于可证伪性较低的理论。这一限定对证伪主义者至关重要。已被证伪的理论必须被无情地摒弃。科学事业包含提出高度可证伪的假设，然后进行审慎而坚持不懈的尝试来证伪它们。引用波普尔（1969，第231页，原文斜体）：

Highly falsifiable theories should be preferred to less falsifiable ones, then, provided they have not in fact been falsified. The qualification is important for the falsificationist. Theories that have been falsified must be ruthlessly rejected. The enterprise of science involves the proposal of highly falsifiable hypotheses, followed by deliberate and tenacious attempts to falsify them. To quote Popper (1969, p. 231, italics in original):

因此，我欣然承认，像我这样的证伪主义者，宁愿尝试用大胆的猜想来解决一个有趣的问题，即便（尤其）这个猜想很快就被证明是错误的，也不愿罗列一连串无关紧要的陈词滥调。我们之所以如此，是因为我们相信这是从错误中学习的途径，而且当我们发现自己的猜想是错误的时，我们就能对真理有更深入的了解，并更接近真理。

I can therefore gladly admit that falsificationists like myself much prefer an attempt to solve an interesting problem by a bold conjecture, even (and especially) if it soon turns out to be false, to any recital of a sequence of irrelevant truisms. We prefer this because we believe that this is the way in which we can learn from our mistakes, and that in finding that our conjecture was false we shall have learnt much about the truth, and shall have got nearer to the truth.

我们从错误中学习。科学的进步离不开反复试验。由于逻辑上的必然性，即无法从观察结果中推导出普遍规律和理论，却可以证伪它们，证伪便成为科学发展的重要里程碑、显著成就和主要进步点。这种极端证伪主义者对证伪意义的某种反直觉的强调，将在后续章节中受到批判。

We learn from our mistakes. Science progresses by trial and error. Because of the logical situation that renders the derivation of universal laws and theories from observation statements impossible, but the deduction of their falsity possible, falsifications become the important landmarks, the striking achievements, the major growing-points in science. This somewhat counter-intuitive emphasis of the more extreme falsificationists on the significance of falsifications will be criticised in later chapters.

由于科学旨在构建信息量丰富的理论，证伪主义者欢迎大胆的推测性猜想。只要这些猜想是可证伪的，并且在被证伪后被驳斥，就应该鼓励这些大胆的推测。这种孤注一掷的态度与极端归纳主义者所倡导的谨慎截然相反。后者认为，只有那些能够被证明为真或可能为真的理论才能被科学所接纳。我们应该超越经验的直接结果，但只能在合法的归纳推理所能达到的范围内进行探索。相反，证伪主义者认识到归纳推理的局限性以及观察对理论的服从性。只有借助巧妙而深刻的理论，才能揭示自然的奥秘。被世界现实检验的推测性理论越多，这些推测性理论越是具有推测性，科学取得重大进展的可能性就越大。推测性理论的泛滥并无危险，因为任何不足以描述世界的理论都可以通过观察或其他检验而被无情地排除。

Because science aims at theories with a large informative content, the falsificationist welcomes the proposal of bold speculative conjectures. Rash speculations are to be encouraged, provided they are falsifiable and provided they are rejected when falsified. This do-or-die attitude clashes with the caution advocated by the extreme inductivist. According to the latter, only those theories that can be shown to be true or probably true are to be admitted into science. We should proceed beyond the immediate results of experience only so far as legitimate inductions will take us. The falsificationist, by contrast, recognises the limitation of induction and the subservience of observation to theory. Nature’s secrets can only be revealed with the aid of ingenious and penetrating theories. The greater the number of conjectured theories that are confronted by the realities of the world, and the more speculative those conjectures are, the greater will be the chances of major advances in science. There is no danger in the proliferation of speculative theories because any that are inadequate as descriptions of the world can be ruthlessly eliminated as the result of observational or other tests.

要求理论具有高度可证伪性，由此产生了一个颇具吸引力的结果：理论应当表述清晰、精确。如果一个理论表述含糊不清，以至于其主张究竟是什么都不清楚，那么当通过观察或实验进行检验时，总能找到与检验结果相符的解释。这样一来，它就能抵御证伪。例如，歌德（1970，第295页）曾这样描述电：

The demand that theories should be highly falsifiable has the attractive consequence that theories should be clearly stated and precise. If a theory is so vaguely stated that it is not clear exactly what it is claiming, then when tested by observation or experiment it can always be interpreted so as to be consistent with the results of those tests. In this way, it can be defended against falsifications. For example, Goethe (1970, p. 295) wrote of electricity that:

它虚无缥缈，仅为零，不过是一个点，然而它却存在于一切表象之中，同时也是万物起源之点，从中，在最轻微的刺激下，便会呈现出双重表象，而这种表象的显现仅仅是为了消逝。激发这种表象的条件千差万别，取决于具体物体的性质。

it is nothing, a zero, a mere point, which, however, dwells in all apparent existences, and at the same time is the point of origin whence, on the slightest stimulus, a double appearance presents itself, an appearance which only manifests itself to vanish. The conditions under which this manifestation is excited are infinitely varied, according to the nature of particular bodies.

如果我们按字面意思理解这段引文，很难想象有什么物理条件能够证伪它。仅仅因为它含糊不清（至少在脱离语境的情况下），它就无法被证伪。政客和算命先生可以通过让自己的断言含糊不清来避免被指责犯错，因为这样他们的断言总是可以被解读为与任何可能发生的情况都相符。对高度可证伪性的要求排除了这种伎俩。证伪主义者要求理论必须表述得足够清晰，以至于能够承担被证伪的风险。

If we take this quotation at face value, it is very difficult to see what possible set of physical circumstances could serve to falsify it. Just because it is so vague and indefinite (at least when taken out of context), it is unfalsifiable. Politicians and fortune-tellers can avoid being accused of making mistakes by making their assertions so vague that they can always be construed as compatible with whatever may eventuate. The demand for a high degree of falsifiability rules out such manoeuvres. The falsificationist demands that theories be stated with sufficient clarity to run the risk of falsification.

类似的情况也存在于精确性方面。理论表述得越精确，就越容易被证伪。如果我们接受理论越容易被证伪越好（前提是它尚未被证伪），那么我们也必须接受理论的断言越精确越好。“行星绕太阳做椭圆运动”比“行星绕太阳做闭合环路运动”更精确，因此也更容易被证伪。椭圆轨道会证伪前者，但不会证伪后者；而能够证伪后者的轨道也会证伪前者。证伪主义者必然会倾向于前者。同样地，证伪主义者也必然会倾向于“真空中的光速为299.8 × 10⁶米/秒”这一断言，而不是精度较低的“真空中的光速约为300 × 10⁶米/秒”这一断言，仅仅因为前者比后者更容易被证伪。

A similar situation exists with respect to precision. The more precisely a theory is formulated the more falsifiable it becomes. If we accept that the more falsifiable a theory is the better (provided it has not been falsified), then we must also accept that the more precise the claims of a theory are the better. ‘Planets move in ellipses around the sun’ is more precise than ‘Planets move in closed loops around the sun’, and is consequently more falsifiable. An oval orbit would falsify the first but not the second, whereas an orbit that falsifies the second will also falsify the first. The falsificationist is committed to preferring the first. Similarly, the falsificationist must prefer the claim that the velocity of light in a vacuum is 299.8 × 106 metres per second to the less-precise claim that it is about 300 × 106 metres per second, just because the first is more falsifiable than the second.

对精确性和表达清晰度的密切要求，都是从证伪主义者对科学的论述中自然而然产生的。

The closely associated demands for precision and clarity of expression both follow naturally from the falsificationist’s account of science.

伪证主义与进步

Falsificationism and progress

证伪主义者眼中的科学进步可以概括如下：科学始于问题，这些问题与解释世界或宇宙某些方面的运行规律相关。科学家提出可证伪的假设来解决问题。这些假设随后会受到批判和检验。有些假设很快就会被排除，而另一些则可能更成功。这些更成功的假设必须接受更加严格的批判和检验。当一个成功经受住各种严格检验的假设最终被证伪时，一个新的问题——希望它与最初解决的问题截然不同——就出现了。这个新问题需要提出新的假设，然后再次进行批判和检验。如此循环往复，永无止境。无论一个理论经受住了多么严格的检验，我们都不能断言它是正确的，但我们或许可以说，当前的理论优于其先前的理论，因为它能够经受住那些证伪先前理论的检验。

The progress of science as the falsificationist sees it might be summed up as follows. Science starts with problems, problems associated with the explanation of the behaviour of some aspects of the world or universe. Falsifiable hypotheses are proposed by scientists as solutions to a problem. The conjectured hypotheses are then criticised and tested. Some will be quickly eliminated. Others might prove more successful. These must be subject to even more stringent criticism and testing. When a hypothesis that has successfully withstood a wide range of rigorous tests is eventually falsified, a new problem, hopefully far removed from the original solved problem, has emerged. This new problem calls for the invention of new hypotheses, followed by renewed criticism and testing. And so the process continues indefinitely. It can never be said of a theory that it is true, however well it has withstood rigorous tests, but it can hopefully be said that a current theory is superior to its predecessors in the sense that it is able to withstand tests that falsified those predecessors.

在我们通过一些例子来阐释这种证伪主义的科学进步观之前，有必要先谈谈“科学始于问题”这一论断。以下列举一些科学家过去曾面临的问题：蝙蝠的眼睛明明很小很弱，它们为何能在夜间如此灵巧地飞行？为什么简单的气压计在高海拔地区的读数比低海拔地区低？为什么伦琴实验室里的感光底片会不断变黑？为什么水星的近日点会不断前进？这些问题都源于或多或少直接的观察。那么，既然我们坚持认为科学始于问题，那么对于证伪主义者和朴素的归纳主义者来说，科学难道不是始于观察吗？答案是绝对的“否”。上述构成问题的观察结果，只有在某些理论的框架下才显得有问题。第一个问题，在“生物体用眼睛‘看’”这一理论的框架下，就显得有问题；第二个问题对伽利略理论的支持者来说是个难题，因为它与他们所接受的“真空力”理论相冲突，而“真空力”理论被用来解释为什么水银不会从气压计管中落下；第三个问题对伦琴来说是个难题，因为当时人们默认不存在任何能够穿透照相底片容器并使其变暗的辐射或辐射；第四个问题之所以棘手，是因为它与牛顿的理论不符。科学始于问题的说法与理论优先于观察和观察结果陈述的观点完全一致。科学并非始于直接的观察。

Before we look at some examples to illustrate this falsificationist conception of the progress of science, a word should be said about the claim that ‘Science starts with problems’. Here are some problems that have confronted scientists in the past. How are bats able to fly so dexterously at night, when in fact they have very small, weak eyes? Why is the height of a simple barometer lower at high altitudes than at low altitudes? Why were the photographic plates in Roentgen’s laboratory continually becoming blackened? Why does the perihelion of the planet Mercury advance? These problems arise from more or less straightforward observations. In insisting on the fact that science starts with problems, then, is it not the case that, for the falsificationist just as for the naive inductivist, science starts from observation? The answer to this question is a firm ‘No’. The observations cited above as constituting problems are only problematic in the light of some theory. The first is problematic in the light of the theory that living organisms ‘see’ with their eyes; the second was problematic for the supporters of Galileo’s theories because it clashed with the ‘force of a vacuum’ theory accepted by them as an explanation of why the mercury does not fall from a barometer tube; the third was problematic for Roentgen because it was tacitly assumed at the time that no radiation or emanation of any kind existed that could penetrate the container of the photographic plates and darken them; the fourth was problematic because it was incompatible with Newton’s theory. The claim that science starts with problems is perfectly compatible with the priority of theories over observation and observation statements. Science does not start with stark observation.

结束这段题外话后，我们将回到证伪主义的科学进步观，即科学进步是一个从问题到推测性假设，再到对假设的批判和最终证伪，然后又提出新问题的过程。我们将举两个例子，第一个例子很简单，是关于蝙蝠飞行的；第二个例子则更为宏大，是关于物理学进步的。

After this digression, we return to the falsificationist conception of the progress of science as the progression from problems to speculative hypotheses, to their criticism and eventual falsification and thence to new problems. Two examples will be offered, the first a simple one concerning the flight of bats, the second a more ambitious one concerning the progress of physics.

我们从一个问题开始。蝙蝠能够轻松快速地飞行，避开树枝、电线、其他蝙蝠等等，还能捕捉昆虫。然而，蝙蝠的视力很弱，而且它们大部分时间都在夜间飞行。这就构成了一个问题，因为它似乎否定了动物（像人类一样）用眼睛“看”东西这一看似合理的理论。证伪主义者会试图通过提出猜想或假设来解决这个问题。他可能会提出，虽然蝙蝠的视力看似很弱，但它们仍然能够以某种我们尚未了解的方式有效地利用眼睛在夜间视物。这个假设是可以检验的。实验者将一些蝙蝠放入一个黑暗的房间里，房间里放置一些障碍物，并测量它们避开障碍物的能力。然后，将同样的蝙蝠蒙上眼睛，再次放入这个房间。在实验之前，实验者可以做出以下推断。演绎推理的一个前提是他的假设，该假设表述得非常明确：“蝙蝠能够利用眼睛飞行并避开障碍物，而不能利用眼睛飞行。”第二个前提是对实验装置的描述，其中包括“这组蝙蝠被蒙住眼睛，因此它们无法使用眼睛。”基于这两个前提，实验者可以演绎地得出结论：这组蝙蝠无法有效地避开实验室中的障碍物。实验进行后发现，蝙蝠避开碰撞的效率与之前一样高。假设被证伪了。现在需要发挥想象力，提出新的猜想、假设或推测。或许有科学家提出，蝙蝠的耳朵在某种程度上参与了它们避开障碍物的能力。为了验证这个假设，可以在将蝙蝠放入实验室之前堵住它们的耳朵。这次发现蝙蝠躲避障碍物的能力显著下降。假设得到了证实。证伪主义者现在必须尝试使假设更加精确，以便更容易证伪。有人提出，蝙蝠听到的是自己吱吱声从固体物体上反射回来的回声。为了验证这一假设，研究人员先堵住蝙蝠的嘴，然后再放开它们。结果蝙蝠再次撞到障碍物，假设再次得到证实。证伪主义者似乎找到了一个初步的解决方案，尽管尚未得到证明。通过实验研究蝙蝠在飞行中如何避免碰撞。然而，许多因素都可能表明该假设是错误的。例如，蝙蝠或许并非用耳朵而是用耳朵附近的敏感区域来感知回声，而当蝙蝠的耳朵被堵住时，这些敏感区域的功能就受到了影响。又或者，不同种类的蝙蝠感知障碍物的方式截然不同，因此实验中使用的蝙蝠并不具有真正的代表性。

We start with a problem. Bats are able to fly with ease and at speed, avoiding the branches of trees, telegraph wires, other bats, etc., and can catch insects. And yet bats have weak eyes, and in any case do most of their flying at night. This poses a problem because it apparently falsifies the plausible theory that animals, like humans, see with their eyes. A falsificationist will attempt to solve the problem by making a conjecture or hypothesis. Perhaps he suggests that, although bats’ eyes are apparently weak, nevertheless in some way that is not understood they are able to see efficiently at night by use of their eyes. This hypothesis can be tested. A sample of bats is released into a darkened room containing obstacles and their ability to avoid the obstacles measured in some way. The same bats are now blindfolded and again released into the room. Prior to the experiment, the experimenter can make the following deduction. One premise of the deduction is his hypothesis, which made quite explicit reads, ‘Bats are able to fly avoiding obstacles by using their eyes, and cannot do so without the use of their eyes’. The second premise is a description of the experimental set-up, including the statement, ‘This sample of bats is blindfolded so that they do not have the use of their eyes’. From these two premises, the experimenter can derive, deductively, that the sample of bats will not be able to avoid the obstacles in the test laboratory efficiently. The experiment is now performed and it is found that the bats avoid collisions just as efficiently as before. The hypothesis has been falsified. There is now a need for a fresh use of the imagination, a new conjecture or hypothesis or guess. Perhaps a scientist suggests that in some way the bat’s ears are involved in its ability to avoid obstacles. The hypothesis can be tested, in an attempt to falsify it, by plugging the ears of bats before releasing them into the test laboratory. This time it is found that the ability of the bats to avoid obstacles is considerably impaired. The hypothesis has been supported. The falsificationist must now try to make the hypothesis more precise so that it becomes more readily falsifiable. It is suggested that the bat hears echoes of its own squeaks rebounding from solid objects. This is tested by gagging the bats before releasing them. Again the bats collide with obstacles and again the hypothesis is supported. The falsificationist now appears to be reaching a tentative solution to the problem, although it has not been proved by experiment how bats avoid collisions while flying. Any number of factors may turn up that show the hypothesis to have been wrong. Perhaps the bat detects echoes not with its ears but with sensitive regions close to the ears, the functioning of which was impaired when the bat’s ears were plugged. Or perhaps different kinds of bats detect obstacles in very different ways, so the bats used in the experiment were not truly representative.

从亚里士多德到牛顿再到爱因斯坦，物理学的发展历程提供了一个更宏观的例证。证伪主义者对这一发展历程的描述大致如下：亚里士多德物理学在某种程度上相当成功，它能够解释多种现象。例如，它可以解释为什么重物会落到地面（因为它们会回到宇宙中心），它可以解释虹吸管和提升泵的工作原理（其解释基于真空不可能存在），等等。但最终，亚里士多德物理学在许多方面都被证伪了。例如，从匀速运动的船桅顶端扔下的石头会落在桅杆底部的甲板上，而不是像亚里士多德的理论预测的那样落在离桅杆一段距离的地方。木星的卫星实际上是围绕木星运行，而不是围绕地球运行。在十七世纪，还积累了许多其他证伪证据。然而，牛顿物理学一旦建立起来，并在伽利略和牛顿等人的猜想基础上发展完善，便成为一种超越亚里士多德理论的卓越理论。牛顿理论能够解释物体下落、虹吸管和提升泵的运作，以及亚里士多德理论能够解释的一切现象，还能解释那些令亚里士多德学派感到困惑的现象。此外，牛顿理论还能解释亚里士多德理论未曾涉及的现象，例如潮汐与月球位置之间的关联，以及重力随海拔高度的变化。牛顿理论在两个世纪里都取得了成功。也就是说，试图通过引用其预测的新现象来证伪它的尝试均以失败告终。该理论甚至促成了新行星——海王星的发现。然而，尽管牛顿理论取得了如此巨大的成功，但最终，持续不断的证伪尝试还是取得了成功。牛顿的理论在许多方面都被证伪了。它无法解释水星轨道的细节，也无法解释放电管中高速运动电子质量的变化。因此，随着十九世纪迈向二十世纪，物理学家们面临着诸多挑战性难题，需要提出新的推测性假设，以逐步克服这些问题。爱因斯坦成功应对了这一挑战。他的相对论能够解释那些证伪牛顿理论的现象，同时在牛顿理论已被证明成功的领域也能与之相符。此外，爱因斯坦的理论还预言了一些惊人的新现象。他的狭义相对论预言质量是速度的函数，并且质量和能量可以相互转化；他的广义相对论则预言光线会在强引力场的作用下发生弯曲。试图通过新现象来反驳爱因斯坦理论的尝试均告失败。证伪爱因斯坦的理论仍然是现代物理学家面临的一项挑战。如果他们最终成功，这将标志着物理学发展迈出了新的一步。

The progress of physics from Aristotle through Newton to Einstein provides an example on a larger scale. The falsificiationist account of that progression goes something like this. Aristotelian physics was to some extent quite successful. It could explain a wide range of phenomena. It could explain why heavy objects fall to the ground (seeking their natural place at the centre of the universe), it could explain the action of siphons and liftpumps (the explanation being based on the impossibility of a vacuum), and so on. But eventually Aristotelian physics was falsified in a number of ways. Stones dropped from the top of the mast of a uniformly moving ship fell to the deck at the foot of the mast and not some distance from the mast, as Aristotle’s theory predicted. The moons of Jupiter can be seen to orbit Jupiter and not the earth. A host of other falsifications were accumulated during the seventeenth century. Newton’s physics, however, once it had been created and developed by way of the conjectures of the likes of Galileo and Newton, was a superior theory that superseded Aristotle’s. Newton’s theory could account for falling objects, the operation of siphons and liftpumps and anything else that Aristotle’s theory could explain, and could also account for the phenomena that were problematic for the Aristotelians. In addition, Newton’s theory could explain phenomena not touched on by Aristotle’s theory, such as correlations between the tides and the location of the moon, and the variation in the force of gravity with height above sea level. For two centuries Newton’s theory was successful. That is, attempts to falsify it by reference to the new phenomena predicted with its help were unsuccessful. The theory even led to the discovery of a new planet, Neptune. But in spite of its success, sustained attempts to falsify it eventually proved successful. Newton’s theory was falsified in a number of ways. It was unable to account for the details of the orbit of the planet Mercury and was unable to account for the variable mass of fast-moving electrons in discharge tubes. Challenging problems faced physicists, then, as the nineteenth century gave way to the twentieth, problems calling for new speculative hypotheses designed to overcome these problems in a progressive way. Einstein was able to meet this challenge. His relativity theory was able to account for the phenomena that falsified Newton’s theory, while at the same time being able to match Newton’s theory in those areas where the latter had proved successful. In addition, Einstein’s theory yielded the prediction of spectacular new phenomena. His special theory of relativity predicted that mass should be a function of velocity and that mass and energy could be transformed into one another, and his general theory predicted that light rays should be bent by strong gravitational fields. Attempts to refute Einstein’s theory by reference to the new phenomena failed. The falsification of Einstein’s theory remains a challenge for modern physicists. Their success, if it should eventuate, would mark a new step forward in the progress of physics.

这就是典型的证伪论证物理学发展历程的描述。稍后我们将有理由质疑其准确性和有效性。

So runs a typical falsification account of the progress of physics. Later we shall have cause to doubt its accuracy and validity.

综上所述，进步的概念，即科学的发展，显然是证伪主义科学理论的核心概念。下一章将对此问题进行更详细的探讨。

From the foregoing, it is clear that the concept of progress, of the growth of science, is a conception that is a central one in the falsificationist account of science. This issue is pursued in more detail in the next chapter.

延伸阅读

Further reading

经典的证伪主义著作是波普尔的《科学发现的逻辑》（1972），该书最初于1934年以德文出版，1959年译成英文。他较新的文集包括《波普尔》（1969）和《波普尔》（1979）。波普尔在其1969年版著作的第一章中讲述了他如何通过比较弗洛伊德、阿德勒、马克思和爱因斯坦的思想而得出其基本思想。下一章末尾将提供更多与证伪主义相关的资料。

The classic falsificationist text is Popper in The Logic of Scientific Discovery (1972), first published in German in 1934 and translated into English in 1959. More recent collections of his writings are Popper (1969) and Popper (1979). Popper’s own story about how he came to his basic idea through comparing Freud, Adler and Marx with Einstein is in chapter 1 of his 1969 text. More sources related to falsificationism will be given at the end of the next chapter.

第六章

CHAPTER 6

精密的证伪主义、新颖的预测与科学的发展

Sophisticated falsificationism, novel predictions and the growth of science

可证伪性的相对程度而非绝对程度

Relative rather than absolute degrees of falsifiability

前一章提到了一些假设要值得科学家考虑，必须满足的条件。假设应当是可证伪的，越可证伪越好，但又不能被证伪。更成熟的证伪主义者意识到，仅凭这些条件是不够的。另一个条件与科学进步的需要有关。假设应当比它所替代的假设更容易被证伪。

The previous chapter mentioned some conditions that a hypothesis should satisfy in order to be worthy of a scientist’s consideration. A hypothesis should be falsifiable, the more falsifiable the better, and yet should not be falsified. More sophisticated falsificationists realise that those conditions alone are insufficient. A further condition is connected with the need for science to progress. A hypothesis should be more falsifiable than the one for which it is offered as a replacement.

这种精细的证伪主义科学观强调科学的发展，将关注点从单一理论的优劣转移到相互竞争的理论的相对优劣。它展现了科学的动态图景，而非最幼稚的证伪主义者所描绘的静态图景。与其询问一个理论“它是否可证伪？”、“它的可证伪程度如何？”以及“它是否已被证伪？”，不如更恰当地询问“这个新提出的理论能否有效地替代它所挑战的理论？”。一般来说，如果一个新提出的理论比其竞争对手更具可证伪性，尤其如果它预测了一种竞争对手未曾涉及的新型现象，那么它就值得科学家们认真考虑。

The sophisticated falsificationist account of science, with its emphasis on the growth of science, switches the focus of attention from the merits of a single theory to the relative merits of competing theories. It gives a dynamic picture of science rather than the static account of the most naive falsificationists. Instead of asking of a theory, ‘Is it falsifiable?’, ‘How falsifiable is it?’ and ‘Has it been falsified?’, it becomes more appropriate to ask, ‘Is this newly proposed theory a viable replacement for the one it challenges?’ In general, a newly proposed theory will be acceptable as worthy of the consideration of scientists if it is more falsifiable than its rival, and especially if it predicts a new kind of phenomenon not touched on by its rival.

对一系列理论可证伪程度的比较，源于对科学作为不断发展演进的知识体系的强调，这使得一些技术性问题得以绕过。因为要准确界定一个理论的可证伪程度非常困难。绝对的可证伪性无法定义，因为一个理论的潜在证伪者永远是无穷无尽的。很难想象“牛顿万有引力定律的可证伪程度如何？”这个问题能够得到解答。另一方面，比较定律或理论的可证伪程度通常是可行的。例如，“所有物体对之间都存在相互吸引，其作用力与它们之间距离的平方成反比”这一论断比“太阳系中的行星之间都存在相互吸引，其作用力与它们之间距离的平方成反比”这一论断更具可证伪性。后者是由前者所蕴含的。任何能证伪第二个理论的，也必然能证伪第一个理论，但反之则不然。理想情况下，证伪主义者希望能够说，构成科学历史演进的一系列理论都是可证伪的，而且系列中的每一个理论都比其前一个理论更容易被证伪。

The emphasis on the comparison of degrees of falsifiability of series of theories, which is a consequence of the emphasis on a science as a growing and evolving body of knowledge, enables a technical problem to be bypassed. For it is very difficult to specify just how falsifiable a single theory is. An absolute measure of falsifiability cannot be defined simply because the number of potential falsifiers of a theory will always be infinite. It is difficult to see how the question ‘How falsifiable is Newton’s law of gravitation?’ could be answered. On the other hand, it is often possible to compare the degrees of falsifiability of laws or theories. For instance, the claim ‘All pairs of bodies attract each other with a force that varies inversely as the square of their separation’ is more falsifiable than the claim. ‘The planets in the solar system attract each other with a force that varies inversely as the square of their separation’. The second is implied by the first. Anything that falsifies the second will falsify the first, but the reverse is not true. Ideally, the falsificationist would like to be able to say that the series of theories that constitute the historical evolution of a science is made up of falsifiable theories, each one in the series being more falsifiable than its predecessor.

提高可证伪性和临时修改

Increasing falsifiability and ad hoc modifications

随着科学的发展，理论必须越来越易于​​证伪，因而内容也越来越丰富，信息量也越来越大，这种要求排除了仅仅为了保护理论免受可能被证伪的检验而进行的理论修改。对理论的修改，例如增加一个额外的假设或改变某些现有假设，如果其结果并非原理论所没有的，则被称为“临时性修改”。本节余下部分将通过一些例子来阐明“临时性修改”的概念。我将首先探讨一些证伪主义者会拒绝的临时性修改，然后将其与一些并非临时性的、证伪主义者会欢迎的修改进行对比。

The demand that as a science progresses its theories should become more and more falsifiable, and consequently have more and more content and be more and more informative, rules out modifications in theories that are designed merely to protect a theory from a threatening falsification. A modification in a theory, such as the addition of an extra postulate or a change in some existing postulate, that has no testable consequences that were not already testable consequences of the unmodified theory will be called ad hoc modifications. The remainder of this section will consist of examples designed to clarify the notion of an ad hoc modification. I will first consider some ad hoc modifications, which the falsificationist would reject, and afterwards these will be contrasted with some modifications that are not ad hoc and which the falsificationist would consequently welcome.

我先举一个相当简单的例子。我们来看“面包能滋养”这个概括。这个基础理论，如果更详细地阐述，就是：如果小麦以正常方式种植，以正常方式制成面包，并被人类以正常方式食用，那么这些人就能获得营养。这个看似无害的理论在法国的一个村庄遇到了麻烦：当时小麦以正常方式种植，以正常方式制成面包，但大多数食用面包的人都患上了重病，许多人甚至死亡。“（所有）面包都能滋养”的理论被证伪了。为了避免这种证伪，我们可以修改这个理论，将其改为“（所有）面包，除了那个法国村庄生产的那批面包之外，都能滋养”。这是一种临时性的修改。修改后的理论无法用任何不同时检验原理论的方法来检验。任何人食用任何面包都构成对原理论的检验，而对修正理论的检验则仅限于食用除导致法国灾难性后果的那批面包之外的其他面包。修正后的假设比原假设更难证伪。证伪主义者反对这种退守之举。

I begin with a rather trivial example. Let us consider the generalisation ‘Bread nourishes’. This low-level theory, if spelt out in more detail, amounts to the claim that if wheat is grown in the normal way, converted into bread in the normal way and eaten by humans in a normal way, then those humans will be nourished. This apparently innocuous theory ran into trouble in a French village on an occasion when wheat was grown in a normal way, converted into bread in a normal way and yet most people who ate the bread became seriously ill and many died. The theory ‘(All) bread nourishes’ was falsified. The theory can be modified to avoid this falsification by adjusting it to read, ‘(All) bread, with the exception of that particular batch of bread produced in the French village in question, nourishes’. This is an ad hoc modification. The modified theory cannot be tested in any way that was not also a test of the original theory. The consuming of any bread by any human constitutes a test of the original theory, whereas tests of the modified theory are restricted to the consuming of bread other than that batch of bread that led to such disastrous results in France. The modified hypothesis is less falsifiable than the original version. The falsificationist rejects such rearguard actions.

下一个例子不那么骇人听闻，也更有趣。它取材于十七世纪伽利略与一位亚里士多德主义对手之间的一次真实对话。伽利略用他新发明的望远镜仔细观察了月球，发现月球并非光滑的球体，而是表面布满山脉和陨石坑。他的亚里士多德主义对手在重复观察后不得不承认，月球表面的确如此。但这一观察结果挑战了许多亚里士多德主义者的一个基本观念，即所有天体都是完美的球体。面对明显的证伪，伽利略的对手以一种明显牵强的方式捍卫了自己的理论。他提出月球上存在一种看不见的物质，它填充了陨石坑，覆盖了山脉，使得月球呈现出完美的球形。当伽利略询问如何才能探测到这种看不见的物质时，对方的回答是：根本无法探测到。因此，毫无疑问，修正后的理论并未得出任何新的可检验的结论，对于证伪主义者而言，这完全不可接受。恼怒的伽利略以其特有的机智方式，揭露了对手立场的不足。他宣称，他准备承认月球上存在这种看不见、无法探测的物质，但他坚持认为，这种物质的分布方式并非如对手所言，而是堆积在山顶上，使得山峰的高度远超望远镜观测到的实际高度。在为理论辩护而编造各种临时方案的徒劳游戏中，伽利略成功地智胜了对手。

The next example is less gruesome and more entertaining. It is an example based on an interchange that actually took place in the seventeenth century between Galileo and an Aristotelian adversary. Having carefully observed the moon through his newly invented telescope, Galileo was able to report that the moon was not a smooth sphere but that its surface abounded in mountains and craters. His Aristotelian adversary had to admit that things did appear that way when he repeated the observations for himself. But the observations threatened a notion fundamental for many Aristotelians, namely, that all celestial bodies are perfect spheres. Galileo’s rival defended his theory in the face of the apparent falsification in a way that was blatantly ad hoc. He suggested that there was an invisible substance on the moon filling the craters and covering the mountains in such a way that the moon’s shape was perfectly spherical. When Galileo inquired how the presence of the invisible substance might be detected, the reply was that there was no way in which it could be detected. There is no doubt, then, that the modified theory led to no new testable consequences and would be quite unacceptable to a falsificationist. An exasperated Galileo was able to show up the inadequacy of his rival’s position in a characteristically witty way. He announced that he was prepared to admit that the invisible, undetectable substance existed on the moon, but insisted that it was not distributed in the way suggested by his rival but in fact was piled up on top of the mountains so that they were many times higher than they appeared through the telescope. Galileo was able to outmanoeuvre his rival in the fruitless game of the invention of ad hoc devices for the protection of theories.

科学史上另一个可能属于临时假设的例子将简要提及。在拉瓦锡之前，燃素说是燃烧的标准理论。根据该理论，物质燃烧时会释放出燃素。然而，当人们发现许多物质燃烧后重量会增加时，燃素理论受到了挑战。为了克服这一明显的矛盾，有人提出燃素具有负重量。如果这个假设只能通过测量物质燃烧前后的重量来验证，那么它就是临时假设，因为它并没有带来任何新的实验结果。

One other example of a possibly ad hoc hypothesis from the history of science will be briefly mentioned. Prior to Lavoisier, the phlogiston theory was the standard theory of combustion. According to that theory, phlogiston is emitted from substances when they are burnt. This theory was threatened when it was discovered that many substances gain weight after combustion. One way of overcoming the apparent falsification was to suggest that phlogiston has negative weight. If this hypothesis could be tested only by weighing substances before and after combustion, then it was ad hoc. It led to no new tests.

为了克服某个难题而对理论进行的修改并非一定是临时性的。以下是一些并非临时性的修改示例，因此从证伪主义的角度来看，这些修改是可以接受的。

Modifications of a theory in an attempt to overcome a difficulty need not be ad hoc. Here are some examples of modifications that are not ad hoc, and which consequently are acceptable from a falsificationist point of view.

让我们回到“面包有营养”这一论断的证伪，看看如何对其进行合理的修正。一个合理的修正方案是用“所有面包都有营养，除了用被某种真菌污染的小麦制成的面包”（并具体说明这种真菌及其一些特征）这一论断来取代原先被证伪的理论。这种修正后的理论并非临时拼凑，因为它引出了新的检验方法。用波普尔（1972，第193页）的话来说，它是可以独立检验的。可能的检验方法包括：检测制作有毒面包的小麦中是否存在这种真菌；在特制的小麦上培养这种真菌，并检验用它制成的面包的营养效果；对真菌进行化学分析，检测其中是否存在已知的毒素等等。所有这些检验方法，其中许多并非针对原假设的检验，都可能导致修正后的假设被证伪。如果经过修改、更易于证伪的假设在新测试面前经受住了证伪，那么就表明我们学到了新的东西，取得了进步。

Let us return to the falsification of the claim ‘Bread nourishes’ to see how this could be modified in an acceptable way. An acceptable move would be to replace the original falsified theory by the claim ‘All bread nourishes except bread made from wheat contaminated by a particular kind of fungus’ (followed by a specification of the fungus and some of its characteristics). This modified theory is not ad hoc because it leads to new tests. It is independently testable, to use Popper’s (1972, p. 193) phrase. Possible tests would include testing the wheat from which the poisonous bread was made for the presence of the fungus, cultivating the fungus on some specially prepared wheat and testing the nourishing effect of the bread produced from it, chemically analysing the fungus for the presence of known poisons, and so on. All these tests, many of which do not constitute tests of the original hypothesis, could result in the falsification of the modified hypothesis. If the modified, more falsifiable, hypothesis resists falsification in the face of the new tests, then something new will have been learnt and progress will have been made.

现在，让我们转向科学史，寻找一个不那么人为的例子：海王星的发现历程。19世纪对天王星运动的观测表明，它的轨道与基于牛顿万有引力理论的预测存在显著偏差，这对该理论构成了挑战。为了克服这一难题，法国的勒维耶和英国的亚当斯提出，在天王星附近存在一颗此前未被探测到的行星。他们认为，这颗假想行星与天王星之间的引力作用可以解释天王星偏离其最初预测轨道的原因。事实证明，这一假设并非凭空捏造。如果这颗假想行星体积适中，并且能够对天王星的轨道造成扰动，那么就可以估算出它与天王星轨道的大致距离。一旦确定了大致位置，就可以利用望远镜观测天空中的相应区域来验证这一新假设。正是通过这种方式，加勒首次观测到了如今被称为海王星的行星。这并非偶然之举，而是为了避免牛顿的理论因天王星的轨道而被证伪，从而促成了对该理论的一种全新检验，并且最终以一种戏剧性且渐进的方式通过了考验。

Turning now to the history of science for a less artificial example, we might consider the chain of events that led to the discovery of the planet Neptune. Nineteenth-century observations of the motion of the planet Uranus indicated that its orbit departed considerably from that predicted on the basis of Newton’s gravitational theory, thus posing a problem for that theory. In an attempt to overcome the difficulty, it was suggested by Leverrier in France and by Adams in England that there existed a previously undetected planet in the vicinity of Uranus. The attraction between the conjectured planet and Uranus was to account for the latter’s departure from its initially predicted orbit. This suggestion was not ad hoc, as events were to show. It was possible to estimate the approximate vicinity of the conjectured planet if it were to be of a reasonable size and to be responsible for the perturbation of Uranus’s orbit. Once this had been done, it was possible to test the new proposal by inspecting the appropriate region of the sky through a telescope. It was in this way that Galle came to make the first sighting of the planet now known as Neptune. Far from being ad hoc, the move to save Newton’s theory from falsification by Uranus’s orbit led to a new kind of test of that theory, which it was able to pass in a dramatic and progressive way.

在证伪主义科学理论中，证实

Confirmation in the falsificationist account of science

前一章引入证伪主义作为归纳主义的替代方案时，证伪（即理论无法经受观察和实验检验）被描绘成至关重要的。文中论证，根据现有的观察结果，逻辑上只允许我们证明理论的谬误，而不能证明其真理。此外，文中还强调，科学的进步应该通过提出大胆且极易证伪的猜想来解决问题，然后毫不留情地尝试证伪这些新猜想。与此同时，有人提出，当这些大胆的猜想被证伪时，科学就会取得重大进展。自称证伪主义者的波普尔在第62页引用的段落中也表达了类似的观点（斜体字为他所加）。然而，仅仅关注证伪的例子，就歪曲了更为复杂的证伪主义者的立场。上一节结尾的例子就对此有所暗示。通过推测性假设来拯救牛顿理论的独立可检验的尝试取得了成功，因为该假设被海王星的发现所证实，而不是因为它被证伪了。

When falsificationism was introduced as an alternative to inductivism in the previous chapter, falsifications (that is, the failures of theories to stand up to observational and experimental tests) were portrayed as being of key importance. It was argued that the logical situation permits the establishment of the falsity but not of the truth of theories in the light of available observation statements. It was also urged that science should progress by the proposal of bold, highly falsifiable conjectures as attempts to solve problems, followed by ruthless attempts to falsify the new proposals. Along with this came the suggestion that significant advances in science come about when those bold conjectures are falsified. The self-avowed falsificationist Popper says as much in the passage quoted on p. 62, where the italics are his. However, exclusive attention to falsifying instances amounts to a misrepresentation of the more sophisticated falsificationist’s position. More than a hint of this is contained in the example with which the previous section concluded. The independently testable attempt to save Newton’s theory by a speculative hypothesis was a success because that hypothesis was confirmed by the discovery of Neptune and not because it was falsified.

将大胆且极易证伪的猜想的证伪视为科学取得重大进展的标志是错误的，波普尔在这一点上需要纠正。当我们考虑各种极端情况时，这一点就显而易见了。一方面，理论以大胆且冒险的猜想形式出现；另一方面，理论则是谨慎的猜想，其提出的主张似乎不涉及任何重大风险。如果任何一种猜想未能通过观察或实验检验，它就会被证伪；如果它通过了检验，我们就说它被证实了。重大进展的标志是大胆猜想的证实或谨慎猜想的证伪。前者具有启发意义，并对科学知识做出重要贡献，仅仅因为它们标志着发现了以前闻所未闻或被认为不太可能的事物。海王星和无线电波的发现，以及爱丁顿证实了爱因斯坦关于光线在强引力场中会弯曲的冒险预言，都属于此类重大进展。冒险的预言得到了证实。对谨慎猜想的证伪具有启发意义，因为它表明那些被认为是理所当然的真理实际上是错误的。罗素证明基于看似不证自明的命题的朴素集合论存在矛盾，就是一个对看似无风险的猜想进行启发性证伪的例子。相比之下，对大胆猜想的证伪或对谨慎猜想的证实却鲜有启发。如果一个大胆猜想被证伪，那么我们所了解到的仅仅是又一个疯狂的想法被证明是错误的。开普勒关于行星轨道间距可以用柏拉图的五种正多面体来解释的推测被证伪，这并非物理学发展史上的重大里程碑。同样，对谨慎假设的证实也意义不大。这类证实仅仅表明，某些已被广泛接受且被认为无可争议的理论再次被成功应用。例如，证实通过某种新工艺从矿石中提取的铁样品会像其他铁一样在加热时膨胀，意义不大。

It is a mistake to regard the falsification of bold, highly falsifiable conjectures as the occasions of significant advance in science, and Popper needs to be corrected on this point. This becomes clear when we consider the various extreme possibilities. At one extreme we have theories that take the form of bold, risky conjectures, while at the other we have theories that are cautious conjectures, making claims that seem to involve no significant risks. If either kind of conjecture fails an observational or experimental test it will be falsified, and if it passes such a test we will say it is confirmed. Significant advances will be marked by the confirmation of bold conjectures or the falsification of cautious conjectures. Cases of the former kind will be informative, and constitute an important contribution to scientific knowledge, simply because they mark the discovery of something that was previously unheard of or considered unlikely. The discovery of Neptune and of radio waves and Eddington’s confirmation of Einstein’s risky prediction that light rays should bend in strong gravitational fields all constituted significant advances of this kind. Risky predictions were confirmed. The falsification of cautious conjectures is informative because it establishes that what was regarded as unproblematically true is in fact false. Russell’s demonstration that naive set theory, which was based on what appear to be almost self-evident propositions, is inconsistent is an example of an informative falsification of a conjecture apparently free from risk. By contrast, little is learnt from the falsification of a bold conjecture or the confirmation of a cautious conjecture. If a bold conjecture is falsified, then all that is learnt is that yet another crazy idea has been proved wrong. The falsification of Kepler’s speculation that the spacing of the planetary orbits could be explained by reference to Plato’s five regular solids does not mark one of the significant landmarks in the progress of physics. Similarly, the confirmation of cautious hypotheses is uninformative. Such confirmations merely indicate that some theory that was well established and regarded as unproblematic has been successfully applied once again. For instance, the confirmation of the conjecture that samples of iron extracted from its ore by some new process will, like other iron, expand when heated would be of little consequence.

证伪主义者希望摒弃临时性的假设，鼓励提出大胆的假设，作为对已证伪理论的潜在改进。这些大胆的假设将带来新的、可检验的预测，而这些预测并非源自原先已被证伪的理论。然而，尽管一个假设能够带来新的检验可能性，使其值得研究，但它只有在经受住至少一部分检验之后，才能被视为对原有问题理论的改进。这相当于说，一个新提出的、大胆的理论，在能够被视为对已证伪理论的充分替代之前，必须做出一些已被证实的全新预测。许多天马行空、轻率的推测经不起后续的检验，因此不会被视为对科学知识增长的贡献。而那些偶尔出现的、天马行空、轻率的推测，如果确实能够带来新颖的、看似不太可能的预测，并且最终被观察或实验证实，那么它们将成为科学发展史上的一大亮点。在证伪主义对科学发展的解释中，对大胆猜想所产生的新预测的证实非常重要。

The falsificationist wishes to reject ad hoc hypotheses and to encourage the proposal of bold hypotheses as potential improvements on falsified theories. Those bold hypotheses will lead to novel, testable predictions, which do not follow from the original, falsified theory. However, although the fact that it does lead to the possibility of new tests makes a hypothesis worthy of investigation, it will not rank as an improvement on the problematic theory it is designed to replace until it has survived at least some of those tests. This is tantamount to saying that before it can be regarded as an adequate replacement for a falsified theory, a newly and boldly proposed theory must make some novel predictions that are confirmed. Many wild and rash speculations will not survive subsequent testing and consequently will not be rated as contributing to the growth of scientific knowledge. The occasional wild and rash speculation that does lead to a novel, unlikely prediction, which is nevertheless confirmed by observation or experiment, will thereby become established as a highlight in the history of the growth of science. The confirmations of novel predictions resulting from bold conjectures are very important in the falsificationist account of the growth of science.

大胆、新颖和背景知识

Boldness, novelty and background knowledge

关于“大胆”和“新颖”这两个形容词分别用于描述假设和预测，还需要进一步说明。它们都是相对的历史概念。在科学史的某个阶段被视为大胆的猜想，在后来的阶段可能就不再是了。1864年，麦克斯韦提出他的“电磁场动力学理论”时，这的确是一个大胆的猜想。之所以说它大胆，是因为它与当时普遍接受的理论相悖。这些理论假设电磁系统（磁体、带电体、载流导体）在真空中会瞬间相互作用，并且电磁效应只能以有限的速度在物质中传播。麦克斯韦的理论与这些普遍接受的假设相冲突，是因为它预言光是一种电磁现象，并且还预言（后来证实了这一点），波动电流会发出一种新型辐射——无线电波，这种辐射以有限的速度在真空中传播。因此，在1864年，麦克斯韦的理论可谓大胆，而他随后对无线电波的预测更是前所未闻。如今，麦克斯韦理论能够准确描述多种电磁系统的行为已是公认的科学常识，关于无线电波的存在及其性质的论断也不再算是新颖的预测。

A little more needs to be said about the adjectives ‘bold’ and ‘novel’ as applied to hypotheses and predictions respectively. They are both historically relative notions. What rates as a bold conjecture at one stage in the history of science may no longer be bold at some later stage. When Maxwell proposed his ‘dynamical theory of the electromagnetic field’ in 1864, it was a bold conjecture. It was bold because it conflicted with theories generally accepted at the time, theories that included the assumption that electromagnetic systems (magnets, charged bodies, current-carrying conductors) act upon each other instantaneously across empty space and that electromagnetic effects can be propagated at a finite velocity only through material substances. Maxwell’s theory clashed with these generally accepted assumptions because it predicted that light is an electromagnetic phenomenon and also predicted, as was to be realised later, that fluctuating currents should emit a new kind of radiation, radio waves, travelling at a finite velocity through empty space. In 1864, therefore, Maxwell’s theory was bold and the subsequent prediction of radio waves was a novel prediction. Today, the fact that Maxwell’s theory can give an accurate account of the behaviour of a wide range of electromagnetic systems is a generally accepted part of scientific knowledge, and assertions about the existence and properties of radio waves will not rate as novel predictions.

如果我们把科学史上某个阶段被普遍接受并确立的科学理论体系称为当时的背景知识，那么我们就可以说，如果一个猜想的主张在当时的背景知识看来不太可能成立，那么这个猜想就是大胆的。爱因斯坦的广义相对论在1915年是大胆的，因为当时的背景知识包含光沿直线传播的假设。这与广义相对论的一个推论相冲突，即光线在强引力场中会发生弯曲。哥白尼的天文学在1543年是大胆的，因为它与地球静止于宇宙中心的背景假设相冲突。在今天，它不会被认为是大胆的。

If we call the complex of scientific theories generally accepted and well established at some stage in the history of science the background knowledge of the time, then we can say that a conjecture will be bold if its claims are unlikely in the light of the background knowledge of the time. Einstein’s general theory of relativity was a bold one in 1915 because at that time background knowledge included the assumption that light travels in straight lines. This clashed with one consequence of general relativity, namely, that light rays should bend in strong gravitational fields. Copernicus’s astronomy was bold in 1543 because it clashed with the background assumption that the earth is stationary at the centre of the universe. It would not be considered bold today.

正如人们会根据相关的背景知识来判断猜想是否大胆一样，如果预测涉及当时背景知识中未曾提及或明确排除的现象，也会被认为是新颖的。1846年关于海王星的预测就是新颖的，因为当时的背景知识中根本没有关于海王星的记载。1818年，泊松根据菲涅耳的光波动理论推导出的预测——即在从另一侧适当照射的不透明圆盘的一侧中心应该观察到一个亮点——也是新颖的，因为当时的背景知识中包含的光粒子理论排除了这种亮点的存在。

Just as conjectures will be considered bold or otherwise by reference to the relevant background knowledge, so predictions will be judged novel if they involve some phenomenon that does not figure in, or is perhaps explicitly ruled out by, the background knowledge of the time. The prediction of Neptune in 1846 was a novel one because the background knowledge at that time contained no reference to such a planet. The prediction that Poisson deduced from Fresnel’s wave theory of light in 1818, namely, that a bright spot should be observed at the centre of one side of an opaque disc suitably illuminated from the other, was novel because the existence of that bright spot was ruled out by the particle theory of light that formed part of the background knowledge of the time.

前文论述了科学知识增长的重大贡献要么源于大胆猜想的证实，要么源于谨慎猜想的证伪。背景知识的概念使我们能够理解，这两种可能性会在同一实验中同时发生。背景知识包含谨慎的假设，因为这些知识已被充分确立，且被认为无可争议。大胆猜想的证实必然意味着对构成该猜想基础的背景知识的某些部分进行证伪。

In the previous section it was argued that major contributions to the growth of scientific knowledge come about either when a bold conjecture is confirmed or when a cautious conjecture is falsified. The idea of background knowledge enables us to see that these two possibilities will occur together as the result of a single experiment. Background knowledge consists of cautious hypotheses just because that knowledge is well established and considered to be unproblematic. The confirmation of a bold conjecture will involve the falsification of some part of the background knowledge with respect to which the conjecture was bold.

对证实论的归纳主义观点和证伪主义观点的比较

Comparison of the inductivist and falsificationist view of confirmation

我们已经看到，在老练的证伪主义者看来，证实对于科学而言扮演着重要的角色。然而，这并不能完全否定“证伪主义”这一标签。老练的证伪主义者仍然坚持认为，理论可以被证伪和否定，但否认理论可以被确立为真或可能为真。科学的目标是证伪理论，并用更好的理论取而代之，这些更好的理论能够经受住检验。新理论的证实之所以重要，是因为它们构成了新理论优于被其取代的理论的证据，而取代的理论正是被新理论所证实并被新理论所证伪的证据所证伪的。一旦一个新提出的大胆理论成功地取代了它的竞争对手，那么它反过来又成为一个新的目标，需要接受严格的检验，而这些检验需要借助更多大胆的猜想理论来设计。

We have seen that confirmation has an important role to play in science as interpreted by the sophisticated falsificationist. However, this does not totally invalidate the labelling of that position ‘falsificationism’. It is still maintained by the sophisticated falsificationist that theories can be falsified and rejected, while it is denied that theories can ever be established as true or probably true. The aim of science is to falsify theories and to replace them by better theories, theories that demonstrate a greater ability to withstand tests. Confirmations of new theories are important insofar as they constitute evidence that a new theory is an improvement on the theory it replaces, the theory that is falsified by the evidence unearthed with the aid of, and confirming, the new theory. Once a newly proposed bold theory has succeeded in ousting its rival, then it in turn becomes a new target at which stringent tests should be directed, tests devised with the aid of further boldly conjectured theories.

由于证伪主义者强调科学的发展，他们对证实的解释与归纳主义者截然不同。根据第四章所述的极端归纳主义立场，某些证实性实例的意义完全取决于被证实的观察陈述与它们所支持的理论之间的逻辑关系。伽勒对海王星的观测对牛顿理论的支持程度，与现代对海王星的观测所提供的支持程度并无二致。证据获得的历史背景无关紧要。只要能为理论提供归纳支持，这些实例就是证实性实例；而且，已确立的证实性实例越多，对该理论的支持就越大，该理论就越有可能为真。这种脱离历史的证实理论似乎会带来一个令人不悦的后果：无数关于落石、行星位置等的观测，只要能提高对万有引力定律为真概率的估计，就构成有价值的科学活动。

Because of the falsificationists’ emphasis on the growth of science, their account of confirmation is significantly different from that of the inductivists. The significance of some confirming instances of a theory according to the extreme inductivist position described in chapter 4 is determined solely by the logical relationship between the observation statements that are confirmed and the theory that they support. The degree of support given to Newton’s theory by Galle’s observation of Neptune is no different from the degree of support given by a modern observation of Neptune. The historical context in which the evidence is acquired is irrelevant. Confirming instances are such if they give inductive support to a theory, and the greater the number of confirming instances established, the greater the support for the theory and the more likely it is to be true. This ahistorical theory of confirmation would seem to have the unappealing consequence that innumerable observations made on falling stones, planetary positions, etc., will constitute worthwhile scientific activity insofar as they will lead to increases in the estimate of the probability of the truth of the law of gravitation.

相比之下，在证伪主义的论述中，证实的意义很大程度上取决于其历史背景。如果证​​实源于对一项新颖预测的检验，那么这项证实就赋予了该理论很高的价值。也就是说，如果根据当时的背景知识估计，某项证实不太可能发生，那么这项证实就具有重要意义。那些早已被预设的结论则无关紧要。如果我今天通过向地面扔一块石头来证实牛顿的理论，那么我对科学没有任何有价值的贡献。另一方面，如果明天我证实了一个推测性的理论，即两个物体之间的引力取决于它们的温度，并在这一过程中证伪了牛顿的理论，那么我就对科学知识做出了重大贡献。牛顿的万有引力理论及其一些局限性是当前的背景知识，而引力与温度的依赖关系则不是。以下是另一个支持证伪主义者引入到证实中的历史视角的例子。赫兹探测到第一束无线电波时证实了麦克斯韦的理论。我听收音机时也验证了麦克斯韦的理论。这两种情况的逻辑原理相似。理论都预测应该能探测到无线电波，而实际探测到的无线电波也都为理论提供了一定的归纳支持。然而，赫兹因其验证成果而闻名遐迩，而我频繁的验证在科学界却被忽视了。赫兹取得了重大进展，而我听收音机只是在消磨时间而已。历史背景决定了一切。

By contrast, in the falsificationist account, the significance of confirmations depends very much on their historical context. A confirmation will confer some high degree of merit on a theory if that confirmation resulted from the testing of a novel prediction. That is, a confirmation will be significant if it is estimated that it is unlikely to eventuate in the light of the background knowledge of the time. Confirmations that are foregone conclusions are insignificant. If today I confirm Newton’s theory by dropping a stone to the ground, I contribute nothing of value to science. On the other hand, if tomorrow I confirm a speculative theory implying that the gravitational attraction between two bodies depends on their temperature, falsifying Newton’s theory in the process, I would have made a significant contribution to scientific knowledge.
