It is only in the long term (that is, from a historical perspective) that Lakatos’s methodology can be used to meaningfully compare research programs. In this connection, Lakatos came to make a distinction between the appraisal of research programs, which can only be done with historical hindsight, and advice to scientists, which he denied it was the purpose of his methodology to offer. ‘There is no instant rationality in science’ became one of Lakatos’s slogans, capturing the sense in which he considered positivism and falsificationism, insofar as they can be interpreted as offering criteria that can be used for the acceptance and rejection of theories, as striving for too much.

拉卡托斯方法论的问题

Problems with Lakatos’s methodology

正如我们所见，拉卡托斯认为用科学史来检验方法论是恰当的。因此，即使按照他自己的标准，质疑他的方法论在描述上是否充分也是合理的。我们有理由怀疑它是否充分。例如，科学史中是否存在能够识别研究纲领的“核心要素”？反证来自科学家们有时试图通过调整他们所研究的理论或纲领的基本原理来解决问题的程度。例如，哥白尼本人就曾将太阳略微移出行星轨道中心，认为月球绕地球而非太阳运行，并运用各种方法调整周转运动的细节，以至于这些运动不再均匀。那么，哥白尼纲领的核心要素究竟是什么？在十九世纪，人们曾认真尝试通过修正平方反比引力定律来解决诸如水星运动之类的问题。因此，历史上确实存在一些违背拉卡托斯本人提出的一些硬核例子的例子。

As we have seen, Lakatos regarded it as appropriate to test methodologies against the history of science. It is therefore legitimate, even in his own terms, to raise the question of whether his methodology is descriptively adequate. There are grounds for doubting that it is. For instance, are there such things as ‘hard cores’ serving to identify research programs to be found in the history of science? Counter evidence comes from the extent to which scientists do on occasions attempt to solve problems by adjusting the fundamentals of the theories or programs in which they work. Copernicus himself, for example, moved the sun a little to the side of the centres of planetary orbits, had the moon orbit the earth rather than the sun, and came to use all sorts of devices to adjust the details of the epicyclical motions, to the extent that those motions ceased to be uniform. So what exactly was the hard core of the Copernican program? In the nineteenth century there were serious attempts to cope with problems such as the motion of the planet Mercury by modifying the inverse square law of attraction. There are violations of some of Lakatos’s own prime examples of hard cores to be found in history, therefore.

更深层次的问题在于，在拉卡托斯对科学的论述中扮演重要角色的方法论决策究竟是真实存在的还是虚构的。例如，正如我们所见，根据拉卡托斯（1970，第133页）的说法，一个项目的核心之所以无法证伪，是因为“其参与者的方法论决策”。这些决策是历史事实，还是拉卡托斯想象的产物？拉卡托斯并没有真正给出他所需要的答案的证据，而且我们也不清楚什么样的研究能够提供这样的证据。这个问题对拉卡托斯来说至关重要，因为方法论决策正是他与库恩立场的根本区别所在。库恩和拉卡托斯都认同科学家们在一定的框架内协同工作。至少在库恩的某些观点中，他认为科学家们如何以及为何这样做，需要通过社会学分析来揭示。而拉卡托斯则认为这会导致一种不可接受的相对主义。因此，在他看来，这种凝聚力源于理性的方法论决策。拉卡托斯既没有回应这些决策缺乏历史（或当代）现实性的指责，也没有明确回答这些决策在何种意义上应被视为理性。

A deeper problem concerns the reality or otherwise of the methodological decisions that play such an important role in Lakatos’s account of science. For instance, as we have seen, according to Lakatos (1970, p. 133) the hard core of a program is rendered unfalsifiable by ‘the methodological decisions of its protagonists’. Are these decisions a historical reality or a figment of Lakatos’s imagination? Lakatos does not really give any evidence for the answer that he needs, and it is not totally clear what kind of study would provide that evidence. The issue is a vital one for Lakatos, for the methodological decisions are the locus of the distinction between his own position and that of Kuhn. Both Kuhn and Lakatos agree that scientists work in a coordinated way within a framework. For Kuhn, in one of his moods at least, the question of how and why they do so is to be revealed by sociological analysis. For Lakatos this leads to an unacceptable relativism. So for him, the cohesion is brought about by methodological decisions that are rational. Lakatos does not provide an answer to the charge that these decisions have no historical (or contemporary) reality, nor does he give a clear answer to the question of the sense in which they should be regarded as rational.

对拉卡托斯的另一项根本性批评与本书的核心主题直接相关，即科学知识究竟有何特征（如果有的话）。至少从拉卡托斯的修辞来看，他的方法论旨在对这个问题给出明确的答案。他声称，“科学哲学的核心问题是——阐明一个理论成为科学的普遍条件的问题”，这个问题“与科学的理性问题密切相关”，其解决方案“应当指导我们判断何时接受一个科学理论是理性的，何时不理性”（Worrall and Currie, 1978a, pp. 168–9, 原文斜体）。拉卡托斯（1970, p. 176）将他的方法论描述为解决这些问题的方案，该方案将“帮助我们制定遏制——思想污染”的法则。 “我（拉卡托斯）给出了一个研究项目内部进步与停滞的标准，以及‘淘汰’整个研究项目的规则”（沃勒尔和柯里，1978a，第112页）。从拉卡托斯的立场细节以及他本人对这些细节的评论来看，很明显，拉卡托斯的方法论无法达到这些预期。他没有给出淘汰整个研究项目的规则，因为坚持一个正在衰落的研究项目，寄希望于它能够复兴，这在理性上是合理的。如果坚持哥白尼理论一个世纪，直到它取得显著成果，是科学的，那么当代马克思主义者（拉卡托斯的主要批评对象之一）在试图发展历史唯物主义，使其取得显著成果时，为什么就不是科学的呢？拉卡托斯实际上承认，一旦他认识到并承认，在物理科学的语境下，他的方法论只能在事后借助历史的后见之明做出判​​断，那么他的方法论就无法将任何当代理论诊断为非科学的“思想污染”。如果不存在“即时理性”，那么就不可能立即否定马克思主义、社会学或拉卡托斯所憎恶的任何其他理论。

Another fundamental criticism of Lakatos is directly connected with the central theme of this book, the question of what, if anything, is characteristic of scientific knowledge. Lakatos’s rehetoric, at least, suggests that his methodology was intended to give a definitive answer to that question. He claimed that the ‘central problem in the philosophy of science is – the problem of stating universal conditions under which a theory is scientific’, a problem that is ‘closely linked with the problem of the rationality of science’ and whose solution ‘ought to give us guidance as to when the acceptance of a scientific theory is rational or not’ (Worrall and Currie, 1978a, pp. 168–9, italics in original). Lakatos (1970, p. 176) portrayed his methodology as a solution to these problems that would ‘help us in devising laws for stemming – intellectual pollution’. ‘I [Lakatos] give criteria for progression and stagnation within a program and also rules for the “elimination” of whole research programs’ (Worrall and Currie, 1978a, p. 112). It is clear from the details of Lakatos’s position, and his own comments on those details, that Lakatos’s methodology was not capable of living up to these expectations. He did not give rules for the elimination of whole research programs because it is rational to stick to a degenerating program in the hope that it will make a comeback. And if it was scientific to stick to the Copernican theory for the century that it took for that theory to bear significant fruit, why aren’t contemporary Marxists (one of Lakatos’s prime targets) scientific in attempting to develop historical materialism to a point where it will bear significant fruit? Lakatos in effect conceded that his methodology was in no position to diagnose any contemporary theory as non-scientific ‘intellectual pollution’ once he recognised and acknowledged, in the context of physical science, that his methodology could only make judgments in retrospect, with the benefit of historical hindsight. If there is no ‘instant rationality’ then there can be no on-the-spot rejection of Marxism, sociology or any other of Lakatos’s bêtes noir.

拉卡托斯方法论的另一个根本问题在于他认为有必要用科学史研究来支撑其理论。拉卡托斯及其追随者通过对过去三百年物理科学的案例研究来论证其必要性。但如果将这种方法论用于评判其他领域，例如马克思主义或占星术，那么实际上就等于不加论证地假定所有研究领域，如果要被视为“科学”，就必须具备物理学的基本特征。保罗·费耶阿本德（1976）就曾以此方式批评过拉卡托斯。拉卡托斯的方法无疑回避了一个重要的根本性问题，而这个问题只需明确提出便显而易见。至少有一些初步的理由表明，用于评判物理学的方法论和标准可能并不适用于其他领域。物理学可以通过在受控实验的人为环境下分离出各种机制——例如引力、电磁力、基本粒子碰撞时的机制等等——来进行研究，而且这种做法也经常发生。然而，如果用同样的方式研究人类和社会，就会破坏研究对象本身。生命系统要正常运作，其复杂性至关重要，因此，即使是生物学，也必然会与物理学存在一些显著差异。在社会科学中，所产生的知识本身就是所研究系统的重要组成部分。例如，经济理论会影响个人在市场中的行为方式，因此，理论的改变会导致所研究的经济系统发生改变。这种复杂性在物理科学中并不存在。行星的运动不会因为我们关于其运动的理论而改变。无论从这些反思中可以得出多么有力的论证，拉卡托斯仍然不加论证地预设，所有科学知识在某种根本意义上都应该像过去三百年的物理学一样。

Another basic problem with Lakatos’s methodology stems from the way in which he deemed it necessary to support it by studies from the history of science. Lakatos and his followers made the necessary case by means of case studies of physical sciences over the last three hundred years. But if the methodology supported in this way is then used to judge other areas, such as Marxism or astrology, what is in effect being assumed without argument is that all areas of study, if they are to be regarded as ‘scientific’, must share the basic characteristics of physics. Paul Feyerabend (1976) has criticised Lakatos in this way. Lakatos’s procedure certainly begs an important fundamental question and has only to be explicitly stated to reveal a problem. There are a number of prima facie reasons at least why one might expect that a methodology and set of standards for judging physics might not be appropriate in other areas. Physics can, and often does, proceed by isolating individual mechanisms – gravity, electromagnetic forces, the mechanisms at work when fundamental particles collide and so on – in the artificial circumstances of a controlled experiment. People and societies cannot in general be treated in this way without destroying what it is that is being investigated. A great deal of complexity is necessary for living systems to function as such, so even biology can be expected to exhibit some important differences from physics. In social sciences the knowledge that is produced itself forms an important component of the systems being studied. So, for example, economic theories can affect the way in which individuals operate in the market place, so that a change in theory can bring about a change in the economic system being studied. This is a complication that does not apply in the physical sciences. The planets do not change their motions in the light of our theories about those motions. Whatever the force of the arguments that can be developed from reflections such as these, it remains the case that Lakatos presupposes, without argument, that all scientific knowledge should in some fundamental sense be like the physics of the last three hundred years.

当我们考察拉卡托斯（Lakatos，1976a）的遗作《牛顿对科学标准的影响》时，另一个根本性问题便浮出水面。在该研究中，拉卡托斯论证了牛顿实际上改变了科学标准，而他显然认为这种改变是进步的。然而，拉卡托斯能够得出这样的结论，与他反复提出的假设——即对科学的评价必须以某种“普遍”标准为依据——并不相符。如果牛顿确实提高了科学标准，那么我们不禁要问：“这种改变是以何种标准为依据的？”我们面临的问题与库恩所面临的问题类似。这个问题我们将在本书后续章节中探讨，或者说，或许是加以解决。

Another fundamental issue is brought to light when we consider the implications of a study by Lakatos (1976a), published posthumously, on ‘Newton’s effect on scientific standards’. In that study, Lakatos makes the case that Newton, in practice, brought about a change in scientific standards, a change that Lakatos clearly regards as progressive. But the fact that Lakatos can make such a case does not rest easily with the assumption he makes repeatedly elsewhere, that an appraisal of science must be made with respect to some ‘universal’ criterion. If Newton changed scientific standards for the better, then one can ask, ‘with respect to what standard was the change progressive?’ We have a problem of a similar kind to the one that confronted Kuhn. It is a problem we will need to confront, or perhaps dispel, later in this book.

延伸阅读

Further reading

拉卡托斯方法论的核心文本是他1970年出版的《证伪与科学研究纲领的方法论》。其他大部分重要论文都收录在沃勒尔和柯里（1978a和1978b）的著作中。拉卡托斯（1968）的《归纳逻辑问题》和（1971）的《对批评者的回应》也十分重要。拉卡托斯的《证明与反驳》（1976b）精彩地阐述了他如何将自己的思想应用于数学领域。豪森（1976）收录了一些旨在支持拉卡托斯观点的历史案例研究。拉卡托斯和扎哈尔（1975）也进行了类似的研究。科恩、费耶阿本德和沃托夫斯基（1976）的论文集是为了纪念拉卡托斯而作。费耶阿本德（1976）对拉卡托斯的方法论进行了重要的批判。 Musgrave (1974b)、Worrall (1985)、Worrall (1989a) 和 Mayo (1996) 讨论了新颖预测的概念。B. Larvor (1998) 的《Lakatos: An Introduction》对 Lakatos 的工作进行了有益的概述。

The central text for Lakatos’s methodology is his 1970 text, ‘Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes’. Most of the other key papers have been collected in Worrall and Currie (1978a and 1978b). Also important is Lakatos (1968), The Problem of Inductive Logic, and (1971), ‘Replies to Critics’. A fascinating account of Lakatos’s application of his ideas to mathematics is his Proofs and Refutations (1976b). Howson (1976) contains historical case studies designed to support Lakatos’s position. Another such study is Lakatos and Zahar (1975). Cohen, Feyerabend and Wartofsky (1976) is a collection of essays in memory of Lakatos. Feyerabend (1976) is an important critique of Lakatos’s methodology. The notion of a novel prediction is discussed by Musgrave (1974b), Worrall (1985), Worrall (1989a) and Mayo (1996). A useful overview of Lakatos’s work is B. Larvor (1998), Lakatos: An Introduction.

第十章

CHAPTER 10

费耶阿本德的无政府主义科学理论

Feyerabend’s anarchistic theory of science

故事梗概

The story so far

我们似乎在探寻科学的特征时遇到了困难，这种特征能够帮助我们区分科学与其他知识类型。我们最初的想法源于二十世纪早期极具影响力的实证主义者，他们认为科学的特殊之处在于它源于事实。然而，这种尝试最终失败了，因为事实本身并不足够简单明了，不足以支撑这一观点。事实“依赖于理论”，且易出错；此外，我们也找不到关于如何从事实“推导出”理论的清晰解释。证伪主义的情况也好不到哪里去，主要是因为在任何现实的科学情境中，我们都无法找到错误预测的根源，因此，如何证伪理论几乎和如何证实理论一样难以捉摸。库恩和拉卡托斯都试图通过关注科学家所处的理论框架来解决这个问题。然而，库恩则强调了不同范式下的学者们“生活在不同的世界”的程度，以至于他缺乏足够的资源来阐明在科学革命过程中，范式转变如何能被视为一种进步。拉卡托斯试图避免落入这个陷阱，但除了他在回答中随意援引的方法论选择本身存在问题之外，他最终得到的科学特征标准过于宽松，以至于几乎排除了所有可能的学术追求。保罗·费耶阿本德是一位科学哲学家，他对这些缺陷并不感到意外，并试图阐明他认为的全部含义。本章将描述和评估费耶阿本德颇具争议但影响深远的“无政府主义”科学理论。

We seem to be having trouble with our search for the characterisation of science that will serve to pick out what distinguishes it from other kinds of knowledge. We started with the idea, adopted by the positivists who were so influential earlier in the twentieth century, that science is special because it is derived from the facts, but this attempt floundered because facts are not sufficiently straightforward for this view to be sustained, since they are ‘theory-dependent’ and fallible, and because no clear account of how theories can be ‘derived’ from the facts could be found. Falsificationism did not fare much better, mainly because in any realistic situation in science it is not possible to locate the cause of a faulty prediction, so a clear sense of how theories can be falsified becomes almost as elusive as a clear sense of how they can be confirmed. Both Kuhn and Lakatos tried to solve the problem by focusing attention on the theoretical framework in which scientists work. However, Kuhn, for his part, stressed the extent to which workers in rival paradigms ‘live in different worlds’ to such a degree that he left himself with inadequate resources for elucidating a sense in which a change from one paradigm to another in the course of a scientific revolution is a step forward. Lakatos tried to avoid that trap, but, apart from problems concerning the reality of the methodological decisions he freely invoked in his answer, he ended up with a criterion for characterising science that was so lax that few intellectual pursuits could be ruled out. One philosopher of science who was not surprised by, and who attempted to draw out what he saw to be the full implications of, these failures was Paul Feyerabend, whose controversial but nevertheless influential ‘anarchistic’ account of science is described and assessed in this chapter.

费耶阿本德反对该方法

Feyerabend’s case against method

保罗·费耶阿本德是一位奥地利人，他的学术生涯大部分时间都在加州伯克利度过，但也曾在伦敦与波普尔和拉卡托斯有过交往（甚至针锋相对）。1975年，他出版了《反对方法：无政府主义知识论纲要》一书。 书中，他挑战了所有试图阐明科学方法以彰显其特殊地位的尝试，认为根本不存在所谓的科学方法，而且科学本身也不具备任何使其必然优于其他知识形式的特征。费耶阿本德最终宣称，如果说科学方法存在一个单一不变的原则，那就是“一切皆可”。费耶阿本德早期和晚期的著作中都有一些段落，可以用来对《反对方法》主体部分所包含的极端无政府主义科学观进行严厉的批判。然而，为了达到我们的目的，坚持采用未经限定的、无政府主义的科学理论，看看我们能从中学到什么，将是最有启发意义的。无论如何，费耶阿本德立场的极端形式在文献中留下了深刻的印记，科学哲学家们也曾费尽周折地试图反驳它。

Paul Feyerabend, an Austrian who was based in Berkeley, California, for most of his academic career, but who also spent time interacting with (and antagonising) Popper and Lakatos in London, published a book in 1975 with the title Against Method: Outline of an Anarchistic Theory of Knowledge. In it he challenged all of the attempts to give an account of scientific method that would serve to capture its special status by arguing that there is no such method and, indeed, that science does not possess features that render it necessarily superior to other forms of knowledge. If there is a single, unchanging principle of scientific method, Feyerabend came to profess, it is the principle ‘anything goes’. There are passages in Feyerabend’s writings, both early and late, that can be drawn on to severely qualify the extreme anarchistic account of science that is contained in the bulk of Against Method. However, it will be most instructive for our purpose to stick to the unqualified, anarchistic theory of science to see what we can learn from it. In any case, it is the extreme form of Feyerabend’s position that has made its mark in the literature and which philosophers of science have, not without difficulty, attempted to counter.

费耶阿本德的主要论证思路是，通过挑战哲学家们对科学方法和进步的描述，从而削弱他们的论点。他列举了一些科学变革的例子，这些变革被他的对手（包括绝大多数哲学家）视为科学进步的经典案例。他指出，从历史事实来看，这些变革并不符合这些哲学家提出的科学理论。（费耶阿本德本人并不需要认同这些事件是进步的，他的论证才能成立。）费耶阿本德引用的主要例子是伽利略在物理学和天文学领域取得的成就。费耶阿本德的观点是，如果一种关于科学方法和进步的理论甚至无法解释伽利略的创新，那么它就称不上是对科学的真正阐释。在对费耶阿本德的观点进行概述时，我将主要以伽利略的例子为例，主要是因为它足以说明费耶阿本德的观点，而且这个例子也很容易理解，无需诉诸深奥的技术细节。

Feyerabend’s main line of argument attempts to undermine characterisations of method and progress in science offered by philosophers by challenging them on their own ground in the following way. He takes examples of scientific change which his opponents (including the vast majority of philosophers) consider to be classic instances of scientific progress and shows that, as a matter of historical fact, those changes did not conform to the theories of science proposed by those philosophers. (Feyerabend does not have to himself agree that the episodes in question were progressive for his argument to go through.) The main example appealed to by Feyerabend involves the advances in physics and astronomy made by Galileo. Feyerabend’s point is that if an account of method and progress in science cannot even make sense of Galileo’s innovations, then it is not much of an account of science. In this outline of Feyerabend’s position I will stick largely to the Galileo example, mainly because it is sufficient to illustrate Feyerabend’s position, but also because the example is readily understood without requiring resort to recondite technicalities.

费耶阿本德的许多观点大家应该都很熟悉，因为我在本书前面已经出于各种目的引用过它们。

A number of Feyerabend’s points will be familiar because I have already drawn on them for various purposes earlier in this book.

本书第一章引用的文献体现了实证主义或归纳主义的观点，即伽利略的创新可以用他对可观察事实的重视程度以及他构建理论以使其与事实相符的程度来解释。费耶阿本德（1975，第100-101页）引用的伽利略《关于两大世界体系的对话》（1967）中的以下段落表明，伽利略的想法并非如此。

Quotations invoked in chapter 1 of this book illustrate the positivist or inductivist view that Galileo’s innovations can be explained in terms of the extent to which he took the observable facts seriously and built his theories to fit them. The following passage from Galileo’s Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems (1967), cited by Feyerabend (1975, pp. 100–1), indicates that Galileo thought otherwise.

你或许会疑惑为何毕达哥拉斯关于地球自转的观点如此鲜为人知，而我则惊讶于至今竟有人接受并遵循这一观点。我永远也无法充分赞赏那些接受这一观点并将其视为真理之人的卓越洞察力：他们凭借纯粹的理性力量，竟如此违背自己的感官，宁愿相信理性告诉他们的，也不愿相信感官经验所明确表明的相反事实。因为正如我们所见，我们已经考察过的反对地球自转的论证非常有说服力：而托勒密学派、亚里士多德学派及其所有追随者都将其视为确凿的论证，这本身就足以证明其有效性。但是，那些明显与年度运动相矛盾的经验，其明显的力量确实要大得多，以至于，我再说一遍，当我想到阿里斯塔克斯和哥白尼能够使理性战胜感觉，以至于前者违背了后者，成为了他们信仰的主宰时，我的惊讶之情难以言表。

You wonder that there are so few followers of the Pythagorean opinion [that the earth moves] while I am astonished that there have been any up to this day who have embraced and followed it. Nor can I ever sufficiently admire the outstanding acumen of those who have taken hold of this opinion and accepted it as true: they have, through sheer force of intellect done such violence to their own senses as to prefer what reason told them over that which sensible experience plainly showed them to the contrary. For the arguments against the whirling of the earth we have already examined are very plausible, as we have seen: and the fact that the Ptolemaics and the Aristotelians and all their disciples took them to be conclusive is indeed a strong argument of their effectiveness. But the experiences which overtly contradict the annual movement are indeed so much greater in their apparent force that, I repeat, there is no limit to my astonishment when I reflect that Aristarchus and Copernicus were able to make reason so conquer sense that, in defiance of the latter, the former became mistress of their belief.

伽利略（1967，第328页）远非接受同时代人认为由感官证实的那些事实，而是必须用理性征服感官，甚至用“一种更优越、更精妙的感官”——望远镜——来取代感官。让我们来看两个伽利略需要“征服”感官证据的例子：他驳斥了地球静止不动的说法，以及他驳斥了金星和火星的视大小在一年中变化不大的说法。

Far from accepting the facts considered to be borne out by the senses by his contemporaries, it was necessary for Galileo (1967, p. 328) to conquer sense by reason and even to replace the senses by ‘a superior and better sense’, namely, the telescope. Let us consider two instances where Galileo needed to ‘conquer’ the evidence of the senses – his rejection of the claim that the earth is stationary and his rejection of the claim that the apparent sizes of Venus and Mars do not change appreciably during the course of the year.

如果从塔顶扔下一块石头，它会落到塔底。这以及其他类似的经验可以作为地球静止的证据。因为如果地球在运动，比如绕着轴自转（伽利略在引文中提到的地球自转），那么在石头下落的过程中，地球难道不应该从石头下方移动，从而使石头落到距离塔底一定距离的地方吗？伽利略是通过诉诸事实来反驳这个论点的吗？正如费耶阿本德所指出的，伽利略在《对话录》中显然不是这样做的。伽利略（1967，第125页及之后）是通过“启发”读者的思考来达到目的的。他的论证如下：一个球沿着光滑的斜坡向下滚动，其速度会增加，因为它在某种程度上是“落向”地心的。相反，一个球沿着光滑的斜坡向上滚动，其速度会降低，因为它是“远离”地心的。在说服读者接受这个显而易见的事实之后，接下来会问：如果斜坡完全水平，球的速度会发生什么变化？答案似乎是：速度既不会增加也不会减少，因为球既不会上升也不会下降。球的水平运动持续且保持不变。虽然这不符合牛顿惯性定律，但它是一个匀速运动持续存在且无因的例子，足以让伽利略反驳一系列反对地球自转的论点。伽利略由此推断，从塔上掉落的石头，由于地球自转而与塔一起运动，其水平运动保持不变。这就是为什么石头会留在塔上，并撞击塔底的原因。因此，塔的论证并不能像许多人认为的那样证明地球是静止的。伽利略自己也承认，他的论证之所以成功，并非基于观察和实验的结果。 （我在此指出，在伽利略时代，获得无摩擦斜坡比现在更加困难，而且测量小球在斜坡上不同位置的速度在当时也是不可能实现的。）

If a stone is dropped from the top of a tower it falls to the base of the tower. This, and other experiences like it, can be taken as evidence that the earth is stationary. For if the earth moves, spinning on its axis, say (the whirling of the earth referred to by Galileo in the passage cited), then should it not move from beneath the stone during its fall, with the result that the stone should fall some distance from the base of the tower? Did Galileo reject this argument by appealing to the facts? That is certainly not how Galileo did it in the Dialogue, as Feyerabend pointed out. Galileo (1967, p. 125 ff) achieved the desired result by ‘picking the brains’ of the reader. He argued as follows. The speed of a ball set rolling down a frictionless slope will increase, because it is ‘falling’ towards the centre of the earth to some degree. Conversely, the speed of a ball rolled up a frictionless slope will decrease because it is rising away from the centre of the earth. Having persuaded the reader to accept this as obvious, he or she is now asked what will happen to the speed of the ball if the slope is perfectly horizontal. It would seem that the answer is that the speed will neither increase nor decrease since the ball will be neither rising nor falling. The horizontal motion of the ball persists and remains constant. Although this falls short of Newton’s law of inertia, it is an example of a uniform motion that persists without a cause, and it is sufficient for Galileo to counter a range of arguments against the spinning earth. Galileo draws the implication that the horizontal motion of the stone falling from the tower, which it shares with the tower as the earth spins, remains unchanged. That is why it stays with the tower, striking the ground at its foot. So the tower argument does not establish that the earth is stationary in the way many had supposed. To the extent that Galileo’s case was successful it did not involve appealing to the results of observation and experiment, at his own admittance. (I point out here that frictionless slopes were even harder to obtain in Galileo’s time than they are now, and that measuring the speed of a ball at various locations on the slope lay beyond what was feasible at the time.)

我们在第一章中看到，金星和火星的视大小之所以重要，是因为哥白尼的理论预测它们的大小会发生显著变化，而肉眼观测并未证实这一预测。一旦接受了望远镜观测数据而非肉眼观测数据，这个问题就迎刃而解了。但是，如何才能捍卫对望远镜数据的偏好呢？费耶阿本德对这种情况的描述以及伽利略对此的回应如下：在天文领域接受望远镜的观测结果绝非易事。伽利略并没有一套充分或详细的望远镜理论，因此他无法通过理论来捍卫望远镜观测数据。诚然，在地球上，人们可以通过反复试验来验证望远镜观测结果。例如，肉眼无法辨认的远处建筑物上的铭文，可以通过靠近建筑物来验证；远处船只的货物识别，也可以在船只抵达港口后得到证实。但是，地面观测的合理性并不能直接用于天文观测。地面观测得益于一系列天文观测所缺乏的视觉线索。由于我们熟悉观测对象，因此能够区分真实的图像和望远镜的诸多伪影。例如，如果望远镜显示远处船只的桅杆呈波浪状，一侧是红色，另一侧是蓝色，上方还漂浮着黑色斑点，那么这些扭曲、颜色和斑点都可以被认定为伪影。然而，当我们仰望星空时，我们身处陌生的领域，缺乏清晰的指引来区分真实景象和伪影。此外，利用与熟悉物体的比较来判断大小，以及利用视差和重叠来判断远近，在天文学中是一种普遍不具备的优势。伽利略当然不可能通过靠近行星并用肉眼观察来验证望远镜观测到的行星数据。甚至有直接证据表明，望远镜数据本身就存在偏差，因为它对月球的放大倍数与对行星和恒星的放大倍数并不相同。

We saw in chapter 1 that the apparent sizes of Venus and Mars were important insofar as the Copernican theory predicted that they should change appreciably, a prediction not borne out by naked-eye observations. The problem is resolved once the telescopic rather than the naked-eye data is accepted. But how was the preference for the telescopic data to be defended? Feyerabend’s rendering of the situation and Galileo’s response to it run as follows. Accepting what the telescope revealed in the astronomical context was by no means straightforward. Galileo did not have an adequate or detailed theory of the telescope, so he could not defend the telescopic data by appeal to one. It is true that in a terrestrial context there were trial and error methods of vindicating telescopic sightings. For instance, the reading of an inscription on a distant building, indiscernible to the naked eye, could be checked by going close to the building, and the identification of the cargo of a distant ship could be vindicated once the ship arrived in port. But the vindication of terrestrial use could not be straightforwardly employed to justify astronomical use of the telescope. Terrestrial use of the telescope is aided by a range of visual cues absent in the astronomical case. Genuine images can be distinguished from many artifacts of the telescope because we are familiar with the kinds of things being inspected. So, for instance, if the telescope reveals the mast of a distant ship to be wavy, red on one side and blue on the other and accompanied by black specks hovering above it, the distortions, colours and specks can be dismissed as artifacts. However, when looking into the heavens, we are in unfamiliar territory and lack clear guidance as to what is really there as opposed to an artifact. What is more, comparison with familiar objects to help judge size, and the use of parallax and overlap to help judge what is far and what is near, is a luxury not in general available in astronomy and it is certainly not the case that Galileo could check telescopic sightings of planets by moving closer to them to check with the naked eye. There was even direct evidence that the telescopic data was erratic insofar as it magnified the moon to a different degree than it magnified the planets and stars.

费耶阿本德（1975，第141页）指出，这些困难如此之大，以至于仅仅依靠辩论不足以说服那些既否认哥白尼理论又否认天文观测数据的反对者。因此，伽利略不得不诉诸宣传和诡计。

According to Feyerabend (1975, p. 141), these difficulties were such that recourse to argument would have been inadequate for the task of convincing those opponents who wished to deny both the Copernican theory and the telescopic data relating to the heavens. Consequently, Galileo needed to, and did, resort to propaganda and trickery.

另一方面，有些望远镜观测到的现象显然符合哥白尼的理论。伽利略将这些现象作为独立的证据来支持哥白尼的观点，但实际情况是，一种已被驳斥的观点——哥白尼主义——与另一种已被驳斥的观点——望远镜观测到的现象是天空的真实影像——之间存在某种相似之处。伽利略之所以能够成功，是因为他文笔优美、论证巧妙，他用意大利语而非拉丁语写作，而且他迎合了那些天性反对旧观念及其相关学术标准的人的口味。

On the other hand, there are some telescopic phenomena which are plainly Copernican. Galileo introduces these phenomena as independent evidence for Copernicus while the situation is rather that one refuted view – Copernicanism – has a certain similarity to phenomena emerging from another refuted view – the idea that telescopic phenomena are faithful images of the sky. Galileo prevails because of his style and his clever techniques of persuasion, because he writes in Italian rather than in Latin, and because he appeals to people who are temperamentally opposed to the old ideas and the standards of learning connected with them.

显而易见，如果费耶阿本德对伽利略方法论的解读是正确的，并且是科学的典型特征，那么标准的实证主义、归纳主义和证伪主义科学理论就难以将其纳入考量。费耶阿本德认为，伽利略的方法论可以融入拉卡托斯的方法论，但这仅仅是因为拉卡托斯的方法论过于宽松，几乎可以容纳任何观点。费耶阿本德戏谑地称拉卡托斯为“无政府主义同道”，尽管他“伪装”了身份，并戏谑地将《反对方法》一书献给拉卡托斯的“朋友和无政府主义同道”。费耶阿本德将亚里士多德的静止地球理论（以肉眼观测数据为支撑）和哥白尼的地球运动理论（以望远镜观测数据为支撑）视为相互排斥的思想体系，这种解读方式让人联想到库恩对范式的描述，即范式是看待世界的两种相互排斥的方式。事实上，这两位哲学家都独立地创造了“不可通约性”一词，用来描述两种理论或范式之间的关系，由于缺乏可供比较的理论中立事实，它们无法进行逻辑比较。库恩主要通过诉诸社会共识来恢复法律和秩序，从而避免了费耶阿本德的无政府主义结论。费耶阿本德（1970）驳斥了库恩诉诸科学界社会共识的做法，部分原因是他认为库恩没有区分达成共识的合法途径和非法途径（例如，通过杀害所有反对者），也因为他认为诉诸共识无法区分科学与其他活动，例如神学和有组织犯罪。

It should be clear that if Feyerabend’s construal of Galileo’s methodology is correct and typical of science, then standard positivist, inductivist and falsificationist accounts of science have serious problems accommodating it. It can be accommodated into Lakatos’s methodology, according to Feyerabend, but only because that methodology is so lax that it can accommodate almost anything. Feyerabend teased Lakatos by welcoming him as a ‘fellow anarchist’, albeit one ‘in disguise’, playfully dedicating Against Method to Lakatos ‘friend and fellow anarchist’. The way in which Feyerabend construes the two frameworks, the Aristotelian stationary earth framework backed up by naked-eye data and the Copernican, moving earth theory supported by telescopic data, as mutually exclusive circles of thought, as it were, is reminiscent of Kuhn’s portrayal of paradigms as mutually exclusive ways of seeing the world. Indeed, the two philosophers both independently coined the word ‘incommensurable’ to describe the relationship between two theories or paradigms that cannot be logically compared for lack of theory-neutral facts to exploit in the comparison. Kuhn avoided Feyerabend’s anarchistic conclusions essentially by appealing to social consensus to restore law and order. Feyerabend (1970) rejected Kuhn’s appeal to the social consensus of the scientific community, partly because he did not think Kuhn distinguished between legitimate and illegitimate ways (for example by killing all opponents) of achieving consensus, and also because he did not think the appeal to consensus was capable of distinguishing between science and other activities such as theology and organised crime.

鉴于人们试图捕捉科学知识的特殊属性（这些属性使其优于其他知识形式）的努力均告失败——费耶阿本德自认为已经证实了这一点——他得出结论：科学在我们社会中被赋予的崇高地位，以及人们假定它不仅优于马克思主义，甚至优于黑魔法和巫术等事物，都是没有道理的。费耶阿本德认为，对科学的过度推崇是一种危险的教条，它扮演着压制性的角色，类似于他所描述的基督教在十七世纪所扮演的角色，他指的是伽利略与教会的斗争。

Given the failure of attempts to capture the special features of scientific knowledge that render it superior to other forms, which failure Feyerabend considered himself to have established, he drew the conclusion that the high status attributed to science in our society, and the superiority it is presumed to have not only over Marxism, say, but over such things as black magic and voodoo, are not justified. According to Feyerabend, the high regard for science is a dangerous dogma, playing a repressive role similar to that which he portrays Christianity as having played in the seventeenth century, having in mind such things as Galileo’s struggles with the Church.

费耶阿本德对自由的倡导

Feyerabend’s advocacy of freedom

费耶阿本德的科学理论植根于一个高度重视个人自由的伦理框架，这种伦理框架包含着费耶阿本德称之为“人道主义态度”的观点。根据这种态度，个人应当享有自由，其自由程度类似于十九世纪哲学家约翰·斯图亚特·密尔（1975）在其论文《论自由》中所捍卫的自由。费耶阿本德（1975，第20页）宣称自己赞成“努力增进自由，过上充实而有意义的生活”，并支持密尔倡导“培养个性，因为只有个性才能培养出健全的人”。从这种人道主义视角出发，费耶阿本德支持其无政府主义的科学观，理由是它通过使科学家摆脱方法论的束缚来增加他们的自由，更广泛地说，它赋予个人在科学与其他知识形式之间进行选择的自由。

Feyerabend’s theory of science is situated in an ethical framework that places a high value on individual freedom, involving an attitude that Feyerabend described as the ‘humanitarian attitude’. According to that attitude, individual humans should be free and possess liberty in something like the sense the nineteenth-century philosopher John Stuart Mill (1975) defended in his essay ‘On Liberty’. Feyerabend (1975, p. 20) declared himself in favour of ‘the attempt to increase liberty, to lead a full and rewarding life’ and supports Mill in advocating ‘the cultivation of individuality which alone produces, or can produce, well-developed human beings’. From this humanitarian point of view, Feyerabend supports his anarchistic account of science on the grounds that it increases the freedom of scientists by removing them from methodological constraints and, more generally, leaves individuals the freedom to choose between science and other forms of knowledge.

在费耶阿本德看来，科学在我们社会中的制度化与人道主义态度相悖。例如，在学校里，科学被当作必修课来教授。“因此，尽管美国人现在可以选择自己喜欢的宗教，但他仍然不能要求自己的孩子在学校学习魔法而不是科学。政教分离，但政学分离”（1975，第299页）。费耶阿本德写道（1975，第307页），鉴于此，我们需要做的是“将社会从意识形态僵化的科学的束缚中解放出来，正如我们的祖先将我们从唯一真宗教的束缚中解放出来一样！”在费耶阿本德构想的自由社会中，科学不会凌驾于其他知识形式或其他传统之上。在一个自由社会中，成熟的公民是“一个学会独立思考并做出最适合自己的选择的人”。科学将作为一种历史现象进行研究，“与其他童话故事，例如‘原始’社会的传说”一起进行研究，以便每个人“都能获得做出自由决定所需的信息”（1975年，第308页，原文斜体）。在费耶阿本德的理想社会中，国家在各种意识形态之间保持中立，以确保个人享有选择的自由，并且不会被迫接受违背其意愿的意识形态。

From Feyerabend’s point of view, the institutionalisation of science in our society is inconsistent with the humanitarian attitude. In schools, for example, science is taught as a matter of course. ‘Thus, while an American can now choose the religion he likes, he is still not permitted to demand that his children learn magic rather than science at school. There is a separation between state and Church, there is no separation between state and science’ (1975, p. 299). What we need to do in the light of this, wrote Feyerabend (1975, p. 307), is to ‘free society from the strangling hold of an ideologically petrified science just as our ancestors freed us from the strangling hold of the One True Religion!’ In Feyerabend’s image of a free society, science will not be given preference over other forms of knowledge or over other traditions. A mature citizen in a free society is ‘a person who has learned to make up his mind and who has then decided in favour of what he thinks suits him best’. Science will be studied as a historical phenomenon ‘together with other fairy tales such as the myths of “primitive” societies’ so that each individual ‘has the information needed for arriving at a free decision’ (1975, p. 308, italics in original). In Feyerabend’s ideal society the state is ideologically neutral between ideologies to ensure that individuals maintain freedom of choice and do not have an ideology imposed on them against their will.

费耶阿本德反对方法论的论点，以及他对个人某种自由的倡导，最终形成了他的无政府主义知识论（1975 年，第 284-285 页，原文斜体）。

The culmination of Feyerabend’s case against method, together with his advocacy of a particular brand of freedom for the individual, is his anarchistic theory of knowledge (1975, pp. 284–5, italics in original).

卡尔纳普、亨佩尔、内格尔（三位著名的实证主义者）、波普尔甚至拉卡托斯想要用来理性化科学变革的方法，无一能够应用；而唯一可行的方法——反驳——其效力也大大降低。最终剩下的，只有审美判断、品味判断、形而上学偏见、宗教欲望，简而言之，剩下的，只有我们的主观愿望：科学在其最先进、最普遍的层面，反而将个人在其较为平凡的部分似乎失去的自由归还给了个人。

None of the methods which Carnap, Hempel, Nagel [three prominent positivists], Popper or even Lakatos want to use for rationalising scientific changes can be applied, and the one that can be applied, refutation, is greatly reduced in strength. What remains are aesthetic judgments, judgments of taste, metaphysical prejudices, religious desires, in short, what remains are our subjective wishes: science at its most advanced and general returns to the individual a freedom he seems to lose in its more pedestrian parts.

那么，就没有科学方法可言了。科学家们应该随心所欲，什么都可以做。

There is no scientific method, then. Scientists should follow their subjective wishes. Anything goes.

对费耶阿本德个人主义的批判

Critique of Feyerabend’s individualism

对费耶阿本德关于人类自由的理解进行批判，将有助于我们评估他对方法论的批判。费耶阿本德自由概念的核心问题在于其消极性过强，即自由被理解为摆脱约束的自由。个人应该尽可能地摆脱约束，从而能够随心所欲地追求自己的主观愿望。这种观点忽略了问题的积极方面，即个人在多大程度上能够获得实现愿望的途径。例如，言论自由可以而且经常被解读为摆脱约束的自由，例如免受国家压制、诽谤法等形式的约束。因此，举例来说，如果学生在校园里扰乱一位学者的讲座，而这位学者表达了同情法西斯主义的观点，那么学生很可能会被指责剥夺了演讲者的言论自由。他们被指责阻碍了演讲者行使自然权利。然而，从积极的角度来看，言论自由可以从个人拥有哪些资源来表达自己的观点这一角度来理解。例如，个人能够接触到哪些媒体？这种观点使我们的例子呈现出不同的面貌。或许可以这样解释：演讲者获得了大学讲堂、麦克风、媒体宣传等资源，而其他持不同观点的人却没有。十八世纪哲学家大卫·休谟对约翰·洛克的社会契约论的批判，很好地阐释了我的观点。洛克认为社会契约是由民主社会的成员自由订立的，并主张任何不愿接受契约的人都可以自由移居他国。休谟的回应如下：

A critique of Feyerabend’s understanding of human freedom will act as a useful preliminary to an appraisal of his critique of method. A central problem with Feyerabend’s notion of freedom stems from the degree to which it is entirely negative, in the sense that freedom is understood as freedom from constraints. Individuals should be free of constraints to the extent that they can follow their subjective wishes and do what they like. This overlooks the positive side of the issue, the extent to which individuals have access to the means to fulfil their wishes. For example, freedom of speech can be, and often is, discussed in terms of freedom from constraints, in the form of state suppression, libel laws and the like. So, for example, if students disrupt a lecture on campus by an academic expressing views sympathetic to Fascism they might well be accused of denying the speaker freedom of speech. They are accused of putting an obstacle in the way of the speaker’s natural right. However, freedom of speech can be considered, from the positive point of view, in terms of the resources available to individuals to have their views heard by others. What access does a particular individual have to the media, for example? This point of view puts our example in a different light. The disruption of the lecture could perhaps be justified on the grounds that the speaker was given access to a university lecture hall, microphone, media advertising and so on in a way that those advocating other views were not. The eighteenth-century philosopher David Hume nicely illustrated the point I am getting at when he criticised John Locke’s idea of the Social Contract. Locke had construed the social contract as being freely adopted by members of a democratic society and argued that anyone not wishing to subscribe to the contract was free to emigrate. Hume responded as follows:

我们真的能说，一个不懂外语、不了解当地礼仪、只能靠微薄收入勉强糊口的贫苦农民或工匠，有自由选择离开祖国的权利吗？这岂不是和断言一个人留在船上就等于自愿接受船长的支配一样荒谬？即便他是睡着时被抬上船的，一旦离开船就必须跳入大海葬身大海。

Can we seriously say, that a poor peasant or artisan has a free choice to leave his country, when he knows no foreign language or manners, and lives from day to day, by the small wages which he acquires? We may as well assert that a man, by remaining in a vessel, freely consents to the domination of the master; though he was carried on board while asleep, and must leap into the ocean and perish, the moment he leaves her.1

个人生于一个先于其存在的社会，从这个意义上讲，社会拥有他们无法选择也无法选择的特征。他们可选择的行动路线，以及由此而来的自由的具体含义，取决于他们实际能够获取哪些资源来实现各种行动。在科学领域，任何希望为科学做出贡献的人都将面对既有的现状：各种理论、数学方法、仪器和实验技术。科学家总体上可选择的行动路径将受到客观存在的现状的限制，而特定科学家可选择的路径则取决于该科学家能够获取的现有资源子集。科学家只有在有限的选择范围内自由选择时，才能真正实现其“主观愿望”。此外，理解这种现状的前提是对个人无论是否喜欢都面临的现状进行描述。无论是科学领域的变革还是社会整体的变革，主要的理论工作都涉及理解个人所面临的处境，而不是诉诸于不受约束的自由。

Individuals are born into a society that pre-exists them and which, in that sense, possesses characteristics they do not choose and cannot be in a position to choose. The courses of action open to them, and, consequently, the precise senses in which they are free, will be determined by the access that they have in practice to the resources necessary for various courses of action. In science too an individual who wishes to make a contribution to a science will be confronted by the situation as it stands: various theories, mathematical techniques, instruments and experimental techniques. The paths of action open to scientists in general will be delimited by that objectively existing situation, while the paths open to a particular scientist will be determined by the subset of the existing resources to which that individual scientist has access. Scientists will be free to follow their ‘subjective wishes’ only insofar as they are free to choose among the restricted range of options open to them. What is more, a prerequisite for an understanding of that situation will be a characterisation of the situation that individuals face, like it or not. Whether it be changes in science or in society generally, the main theoretical work involves understanding the situations confronted by individuals rather than involving some generalised appeal to unconstrained freedom.

颇具讽刺意味的是，费耶阿本德在其科学研究中竭力否认理论中立事实的存在，却在其社会理论中诉诸于更为宏大的意识形态中立国家概念。这样的国家究竟如何产生？它将如何运作？又是什么维系着它？鉴于已有学者对“国家”的起源和本质进行了严肃的研究，费耶阿本德关于一个所有人都能自由自在地追求自身欲望的乌托邦的奇思妙想，显得幼稚可笑。

It is ironic that Feyerabend, who in his study of science goes to great lengths to deny the existence of theory-neutral facts, in his social theory appeals to the far more ambitious notion of an ideology-neutral state. How on earth would such a state come into existence, how would it function and what would sustain it? In the light of work that has been done in making serious attempts to get to grips with questions about the origin and nature of ‘the state’, Feyerabend’s fanciful speculations about a utopia in which all individuals are free to follow their inclinations in an unrestricted way appear childish.

批评费耶阿本德将科学观点置于个人主义框架内，并抱持一种幼稚的自由观念，是一回事；而要深入了解他“反对”科学方法论的论证细节，则是另一回事。下一章我们将探讨如何从费耶阿本德对方法论的批判中汲取建设性的经验。

Criticising Feyerabend for setting his views on science in an individualist framework involving a naive notion of freedom is one thing. Getting to grips with the details of the case he makes ‘against method’ in science is another. In the next chapter we will see what can be constructively salvaged from Feyerabend’s attack on method.

延伸阅读

Further reading

费耶阿本德在《自由社会中的科学》（1978）一书中发展了他在《反对方法：无政府主义知识论纲要》（1975 ）中的一些观点。《实在论、理性主义与科学方法》（费耶阿本德，1981a）和《经验主义问题》（费耶阿本德，1981b）是他的文章合集，其中一些文章的写作时间早于他的“无政府主义”时期。《给专家的安慰》（1970）和《论科学理性的批判》（1976）分别是他对库恩和拉卡托斯的批判。我曾对费耶阿本德在《伽利略对金星和火星的望远镜观测》（查尔默斯，1985）和《费耶阿本德错过的伽利略》（查尔默斯，1986）中对伽利略科学的描述提出异议。关于费耶阿本德科学哲学的书籍包括 Couvalis (1989)、Farrell (2003) 和 Oberheim (2006)。

Feyerabend develops some of the ideas of his Against Method: Outline of an Anarchistic Theory of Knowledge (1975) in Science in a Free Society (1978). Realism, Rationalism and Scientific Method (Feyerabend, 1981a) and Problems of Empiricism (Feyerabend, 1981b) are collections of his articles, a number of which predate his ‘anarchistic’ phase. ‘Consolations for the Specialist’ (1970) and ‘On the Critique of Scientific Reason’ (1976) are his critiques of Kuhn and Lakatos respectively. I have taken issue with Feyerabend’s portrayal of Galileo’s science in ‘Galileo’s Telescopic Observations of Venus and Mars’ (Chalmers, 1985) and ‘The Galileo that Feyerabend Missed’ (Chalmers, 1986). Books on Feyerabend’s philosophy of science include Couvalis (1989), Farrell (2003) and Oberheim (2006).

第十一章

CHAPTER 11

方法论的改变

Methodical changes in method

反对普遍方法

Against universal method

我们在前一章中看到，费耶阿本德对哲学家们提出的各种科学方法论提出了质疑，这些理论试图捕捉科学知识的独特特征。他采用的一个关键策略是论证这些理论与伽利略在物理学和天文学领域的成就不相符。我曾在其他著作（查尔默斯，1985年和1986年）中对费耶阿本德关于伽利略事件的历史叙述提出异议，我的一些反对意见将在下一节中介绍和阐述。我认为，一旦修正了这段历史，它仍然会对标准的科学和科学方法论构成挑战。也就是说，我认为，只要我们明确被驳斥的“方法”概念，费耶阿本德对方法论的批判在某种意义上是成立的。 费耶阿本德的论证驳斥了这样一种说法：存在一种普适的、非历史性的科学方法，其中包含着所有科学若想配得上“科学”之名就必须遵循的标准。这里，“普适”一词指的是所提出的方法适用于所有科学或假定的科学——物理学、心理学、创造科学等等——而“非历史性”则暗示了该方法的永恒性。它既可以用来评价亚里士多德的物理学，也可以用来评价爱因斯坦和德谟克利特的原子论，以及现代原子物理学。我很高兴与费耶阿本德一样，认为这种普适的、非历史性的方法极其牵强，甚至荒谬。正如费耶阿本德（1975，第295页）所言，“认为科学可以而且应该按照固定不变的普遍规则运行，这种想法既不现实又有害”，它“对科学有害，因为它忽略了影响科学变革的复杂物理和历史条件”，并且“使科学更缺乏适应性，更加教条”。如果要存在一种能够评判过去、现在和未来各种科学的科学方法，人们不禁要问，哲学家们究竟拥有哪些资源来获得这样一种强大的工具？这种工具强大到可以预先告诉我们评判未来科学的适当标准是什么。如果我们把科学视为一种不断追求知识的开放式探索，那么为什么我们不能根据所学到的知识来改进我们的方法，调整和完善我们的标准呢？

We saw in the previous chapter that Feyerabend made a case against the various accounts of scientific method that have been put forward by philosophers as attempts to capture the distinctive feature of scientific knowledge. A key strategy that he employed was to argue for the incompatibility of those accounts and Galileo’s advances in physics and astronomy. Elsewhere (in Chalmers, 1985 and 1986) I have taken issue with Feyerabend’s historical account of the Galileo episode and some of the details of my disagreement will be introduced and exploited in the next section. Once that history is corrected I believe it to remain the case that the corrected history poses problems for standard accounts of science and the scientific method. That is, I suggest there is a sense in which Feyerabend’s case against method can be sustained, provided we are clear about the notion of method that has been refuted. Feyerabend’s case tells against the claim that there is a universal, ahistorical method of science that contains standards that all sciences should live up to if they are to be worthy of the title ‘science’. Here the term ‘universal’ is used to indicate that the proposed method is to apply to all sciences or putative sciences – physics, psychology, creation science or whatever – while the term ‘ahistorical’ signals the timeless character of the method. It is to be used to appraise Aristotle’s physics as much as Einstein’s and Democritus’s atomism as much as modern atomic physics. I am happy to join Feyerabend in regarding the idea of a universal and ahistoric method as highly implausible and even absurd. As Feyerabend (1975, p. 295) says, ‘The idea that science can, and should, be run according to fixed and universal rules is both unrealistic and pernicious’, is ‘detrimental to science, for it neglects the complex physical and historical conditions which influence scientific change’ and ‘makes science less adaptable and more dogmatic’. If there is to be a scientific method capable of judging sciences of all kinds, past, present and future, one might well ask what resources philosophers have for arriving at such a potent tool, so potent that it can tell us in advance what are the appropriate standards for judging future science. If we have a conception of science as an open-ended quest to improve our knowledge, then why cannot there be room for us to improve our methods and adapt and refine our standards in the light of what we learn?

因此，如果这里所说的“方法”指的是普遍的、一成不变的方法，那么我完全可以加入费耶阿本德发起的反对“方法论”的运动。我们已经看到，费耶阿本德对反对“方法论”的回应是假定根本不存在任何方法，科学家应该遵循自己的主观意愿，一切皆可。然而，普遍的方法论和完全没有方法论这两种说法都不能穷尽所有可能性。一种折中的观点认为，科学中存在方法和标准，但它们会因学科而异，而且在同一学科内部也可以改变，并且可以朝着更好的方向改变。费耶阿本德的论证不仅没有反驳这种折中的观点，而且他举的伽利略的例子也可以被解读为支持这种观点，我将在下一节中尝试论证这一点。

I have no problem joining the campaign that Feyerabend launched against method, then, provided method is understood as universal, unchanging method. We have seen that Feyerabend’s response to the case against method is to assume that there is no method, that scientists should follow their own subjective wishes and that anything goes. However, universal method and no method at all do not exhaust the range of possibilities. A middle way would hold that there are methods and standards in science, but that they can vary from science to science and can, within a science, be changed, and changed for the better. Not only does Feyerabend’s case not tell against this intermediate view, but his Galileo example can be construed in a way that supports it, as I shall attempt to show in the next section.

我认为存在一条中间道路，即成功的科学中蕴含着一些具有历史偶然性的方法和标准。与我一样坚决反对费耶阿本德的无政府主义和极端相对主义的科学哲学家们，通常会回应说，像我这样寻求中间道路的人是在自欺欺人。例如，约翰·沃勒尔（1988）就清晰地阐述了这种论点。如果我要捍卫一种避免极端相对主义的科学方法变革，那么我就有义务证明这种变革在哪些方面是有益的。但是，这种“有益”究竟以何种标准来衡量呢？似乎除非存在一些用于评判标准变革的超标准，否则这些变革就无法以非相对主义的方式来理解。然而，超标准又会将我们带回到旨在产生这些标准的普适方法上。因此，沃勒尔的论点是，要么我们有普适方法，要么我们有相对主义。不存在中间道路。为了反驳这一论点，至少可以先从科学领域举一个标准变革的例子。下一节将专门讨论伽利略所完成的这种变革。

I hold that there is a middle way, according to which there are historically contingent methods and standards implicit in successful sciences. A common response from philosophers of science who reject Feyerabend’s anarchism and extreme relativism as firmly as I do is that those like myself who seek a middle way are kidding ourselves. John Worrall (1988), for instance, has given clear expression to the general line of argument. If I am to defend a change in scientific method in a way that avoids extreme relativism then I am obliged to show in what way such a change is for the better. But better according to what standards? It would seem that unless there are some superstandards for judging changes in standards then those changes cannot be construed in a non-relativist way. But superstandards take us back to the universal method that is meant to yield such standards. So, Worrall’s argument goes, either we have universal method or relativism. There is no middle way. As at least a preliminary to a rejoinder to this argument it is useful to take an example from science of a change in standards. The next section is devoted to such a change accomplished by Galileo.

用于肉眼观测数据的望远镜：标准的改变

Telescopic for naked-eye data: a change in standards

伽利略的一位亚里士多德主义反对者（引自伽利略，1967，第248页）将“感官和经验应当是我们进行哲学思考的指南”这一观点称为“科学本身的标准”。许多亚里士多德传统的评论家都指出，该传统的一个关键原则是，知识主张应当与在适当条件下谨慎使用感官所获得的证据相符。伽利略的传记作者卢多维科·盖蒙纳特（1965，第45页）提到，当时大多数学者都认为“只有直接的视觉才能把握真实的现实”。莫里斯·克拉维林（Maurice Clavelin，1974，第384页）在比较伽利略和亚里士多德的科学时指出，“逍遥学派物理学的主要准则就是绝不反对感官证据”。斯蒂芬·高克罗格（Stephen Gaukroger，1978，第92页）在类似的语境下写道，“亚里士多德的著作从根本上且完全依赖于感官知觉”。对这一基本标准的辩护带有目的论色彩。人们普遍认为，感官的功能是为我们提供关于世界的信息。因此，尽管感官在异常情况下可能会误导我们，例如在雾中或观察者生病或醉酒时，但如果认为感官在履行其既定任务时会系统性地误导我们，那就毫无道理了。欧文·布洛克（1961 年，第 9 页）在一篇关于亚里士多德感官知觉理论的精彩文章中，对亚里士多德的观点作了如下描述：

One of Galileo’s Aristotelian opponents (cited in Galileo, 1967, p. 248) referred to the idea that ‘the senses and experience should be our guide in philosophising’ as ‘the criterion of science itself’. A number of commentators on the Aristotelian tradition have noted that it was a key principle within that tradition that knowledge claims should be compatible with the evidence of the senses when they are used with sufficient care under suitable conditions. Ludovico Geymonat (1965, p. 45), a biographer of Galileo, refers to the belief ‘shared by most scholars at the time [of Galileo’s innovations]’ that ‘only direct vision has the power to grasp actual reality’. Maurice Clavelin (1974, p. 384), in a context where he is comparing Galilean and Aristotelian science, observes that ‘the chief maxim of Peripatetic physics was never to oppose the evidence of the senses’, and Stephen Gaukroger (1978, p. 92), in a similar context, writes of ‘a fundamental and exclusive reliance on sense-perception in Aristotle’s works’. A teleological defence of this fundamental standard was common. The function of the senses was understood to be to provide us with information about the world. Therefore, although the senses can mislead in abnormal circumstances, for instance in a mist or when the observer is sick or drunk, it makes no sense to assume that the senses can be systematically misleading when they are fulfilling the task for which they are intended. Irving Block (1961, p. 9), in an illuminating article on Aristotle’s theory of sense perception, characterises Aristotle’s view as follows:

自然界创造万物皆有其目的，而人类的目的在于通过科学理解自然。因此，如果自然界塑造人类及其器官的方式，使得所有知识和科学从一开始就必然是错误的，那将是一个自相矛盾的问题。

Nature made everything for a purpose, and the purpose of man is to understand Nature through science. Thus it would have been a contradiction for Nature to have fashioned man and his organs in such a way that all knowledge and science must, from its inception, be false.

亚里士多德的观点在几个世纪后被托马斯·阿奎那所呼应，正如布洛克（1961，第7页）所记载的那样：

Aristotle’s views were echoed by Thomas Aquinas many centuries later, as Block (1961, p.7) reports:

感官知觉对其所感知的对象总是准确的，因为自然能力通常不会在其固有的活动中出现偏差，如果出现偏差，那一定是由于某种紊乱所致。因此，感官对其所感知的对象做出错误判断的情况极为罕见，而且往往是由于某种器质性缺陷造成的，例如，发烧的人会因为舌头不适而尝到甜的东西却觉得苦。

Sense perception is always truthful with respect to its proper objects, for natural powers do not, as a general rule, fail in the activities proper to them, and if they do fail, this is due to some derangement or other. Thus, only in a minority of cases do the senses judge inaccurately of their proper objects, and then only through some organic defect, e.g. when people sick with fever taste sweet things as bitter because their tongues are ill-disposed.

伽利略当时面临的困境是，依赖感官，包括肉眼观测数据，竟然是“科学本身的准则”。为了推广望远镜，并使望远镜观测数据取代甚至推翻某些肉眼观测数据，他不得不违背这一准则。而当他最终做到这一点时，他已经改变了科学的标准。正如我们所见，费耶阿本德认为伽利略无法提出令人信服的论证，因此需要诉诸宣传和诡计。但历史事实却并非如此。

Galileo was faced with a situation in which a reliance on the senses, including naked-eye data was ‘a criterion of science itself’. In order to introduce the telescope, and have telescopic data replace and overrule some naked-eye data, he needed to fly in the face of this criterion. By the time he had done so, he had effected a change in the standards of science. As we have seen, Feyerabend did not believe it was possible for Galileo to make a compelling case and needed to resort to propaganda and trickery. The historical facts tell otherwise.

我已在第20-23页探讨了伽利略为证明其观测到木星卫星的真实性所做的论证。在此，我将重点讨论伽利略为接受望远镜所揭示的金星和火星视大小变化而提出的论证。我们在前一章已经阐述了这个问题的紧迫性，并且也接受了费耶阿本德关于接受望远镜观测天体结果所面临的困难的论述。

I have already considered (pp. 20–3) the case that Galileo made for the veracity of his sightings of the moons of Jupiter. Here I will focus on the case that Galileo was able to muster for accepting what the telescope revealed of the changing apparent sizes of Venus and Mars. We have already described, in the previous chapter, the urgency of the question and also accepted Feyerabend’s account of the difficulties that lay in the way of accepting telescopic observations of the heavens.

伽利略利用辐射现象来质疑肉眼观测行星的有效性，并以此为由推崇望远镜观测。伽利略的假设（1967，第333页）是，当人眼观察远处明亮、体积小的光源，而背景又是黑暗时，人眼会“引入自身的干扰”。正因如此，这些物体看起来“仿佛被杂乱的光线所环绕”。因此，正如伽利略（1957，第46页）在其他地方解释的那样，如果用肉眼观察恒星，“它们呈现在我们面前的并非其原本的（或者说物理的）大小，而是被某种光芒照射，并被闪烁的光线所环绕”。而对于行星而言，望远镜则可以消除这种辐射现象。

Galileo appealed to the phenomenon of irradiation to help discredit naked-eye observations of the planets and as providing grounds for preferring the telescopic observations. Galileo’s hypothesis (1967, p. 333) was that the eye ‘introduces a hindrance of its own’ when it views small, bright, distant light sources against a dark background. Because of this, such objects appear ‘festooned with adventitious and alien rays’. Thus, Galileo (1957, p. 46) explained elsewhere, if stars ‘are viewed by means of unaided vision, they present themselves to us not as of their simple (and, so to speak, their physical) size but as irradiated by a certain fulgor and as fringed with sparkling rays’. In the case of the planets irradiation is removed by the telescope.

由于伽利略的假设认为辐射是由于光源的亮度、大小和距离造成的，因此可以通过多种无需使用望远镜的方法来改变这些因素，从而检验这一假设。伽利略本人（1957，第46-47页）明确列举了多种方法。例如，可以通过云层、黑纱、彩色玻璃、管子、手指间的缝隙或卡片上的针孔来降低恒星和行星的亮度。对于行星而言，这些方法可以消除辐射，使它们“呈现出完美的圆形和清晰的边界”；而对于恒星而言，辐射永远无法完全消除，因此它们“永远无法被看作是圆形的，而是呈现出光芒四射、波光粼粼的景象”。就辐射强度与观测光源视大小的关系而言，伽利略的假设得到了月球和太阳不受辐射这一事实的证实。伽利略假设的这一方面，以及辐射强度与光源距离的关系，都可以在地球上进行直接验证。无论远近，无论白天黑夜，都可以观察点燃的手电筒。在夜晚远距离观察时，当手电筒相对于周围环境明亮时，它看起来比实际尺寸要大。因此，伽利略（1967，第361页）指出，他的前辈，包括第谷和克拉维乌斯，在估算恒星大小时应该更加谨慎。

Since Galileo’s hypothesis involves the claim that irradiation arises as a consequence of the brightness, smallness and distance of the source, it can be tested by modifying those factors in a variety of ways that do not involve use of the telescope. A number of ways are explicitly invoked by Galileo (1957, pp. 46–7). The brightness of stars and planets can be reduced by viewing them through a cloud, a black veil, coloured glass, a tube, a gap between the fingers or a pinhole in a card. In the case of planets the irradiation is removed by these techniques, so that they ‘show their globes perfectly round and definitely bounded’, whereas in the case of stars the irradiation is never completely removed, so that they are ‘never seen to be bounded by a circular periphery, but have rather the aspect of blazes whose rays vibrate about them and scintillate a great deal’. As far as the dependence of irradiation on the apparent size of the observed light source is concerned, Galileo’s hypothesis is borne out by the fact that the moon and the sun are not subject to irradiation. This aspect of Galileo’s hypothesis, as well as the associated dependence of irradiation on the distance of the source, can be subject to a direct terrestrial test. A lighted torch can be viewed from near or far and at day or night. When viewed at a distance at night, when it is bright compared with its surroundings, it appears larger than its true size. Accordingly, Galileo (1967, p. 361) remarked that his predecessors, including Tycho and Clavius, should have proceeded with more caution when estimating the size of stars.

我不相信他们认为火炬的真正圆盘是在漆黑一片中的样子，而不是在明亮的环境中看到的样子：因为我们的灯光在夜晚从远处看起来很大，但从近处看，它们的真正火焰却很小，而且有边界。

I will not believe that they thought that the true disc of a torch was as it appears in profound darkness, rather than as it is when perceived in lighted surroundings: for our lights seen from afar at night look large, but from near at hand their true flames are seen to be small and circumscribed.

辐射强度与光源相对于周围环境的亮度之间的依赖关系，可以从黄昏时分恒星的出现得到进一步证实。此时的恒星看起来比夜晚小得多；也可以从白天观测金星的现象得到进一步证实。金星在白天看起来“非常小，需要敏锐的视力才能看到​​，但到了晚上，它却像一个巨大的火炬”。后一种现象提供了一种粗略的方法来检验金星大小的预测变化，而无需借助望远镜观测。只要观测时间限制在白天或黄昏，就可以用肉眼进行检验。至少根据伽利略的说法，金星大小的变化“肉眼很容易察觉”，尽管只有用望远镜才能精确观测到（Drake，1957，第131页）。

The dependence of irradiation on the brightness of a source relative to its surroundings is further confirmed by the appearance of stars at twilight, which appear much smaller then than at night, and of Venus when observed in broad daylight, which appears ‘so small that it takes sharp eyesight to see it, though in the following night it appears like a great torch’. This latter effect provides a rough way of testing for the predicted change in size of Venus that does not involve an appeal to telescopic evidence. The test can be made with the naked eye provided observations are restricted to daytime or twilight. According to Galileo, at least, the changes in size are ‘quite perceptible to the naked eye’, although they can only be observed precisely with the telescope (Drake, 1957, p. 131).

因此，伽利略通过相当直接的实践演示表明，在地球和天体领域，当用肉眼观察相对于周围环境而言明亮的小光源时，会得到不一致的信息。伽利略提供了一系列证据来证明辐射现象的存在，而用灯泡进行的更直接的演示也表明，用肉眼观察明亮的小光源是不可靠的。这意味着，在白天用肉眼观测金星比在夜晚金星亮度更高时进行观测更为可取。前者（与后者不同）表明，金星的视大小会随季节变化。以上所有结论都无需借助望远镜。然而，当我们注意到望远镜在观测行星时可以消除辐射的影响，而且视大小的变化与白天用肉眼观测到的变化相吻合时，望远镜观测数据的优势便开始显现。

By fairly straightforward practical demonstration, then, Galileo was able to show that the naked eye yields inconsistent information when small light sources, bright compared with their surroundings, are viewed in the terrestrial and celestial domain. The phenomenon of irradiation, for which Galileo provided a range of evidence, as well as the more direct demonstration with the lamp, indicated that naked-eye observations of small, bright light sources are unreliable. One implication of this is that naked-eye observations of Venus in daylight are to be preferred to those made at night when Venus is bright compared with its surroundings. The former, unlike the latter, show that the apparent size of Venus varies during the course of the year. All this can be said without any reference to the telescope. When we now note that the telescope removes irradiation when used to observe planets and that, what is more, the variations in apparent size are compatible with the variations observable with the naked eye in daylight, a strong case for the telescopic data begins to emerge.

关于金星和火星大小的望远镜观测数据的准确性，最后一个论据是：这些数据与当时所有主流天文理论的预测完全吻合。这与费耶阿本德以及伽利略本人对这一情况的描述相矛盾，他们暗示这些数据支持哥白尼的理论而非其他理论。哥白尼理论的竞争对手是托勒密和第谷·布拉赫的理论。这两种理论都预测了与哥白尼理论完全相同的行星大小变化。托勒密体系中，行星与地球距离的变化导致了视大小的预测变化，这是因为行星在运行过程中会沿着叠加在均轮上的本轮移动，而均轮与地球的距离是等距的。在第谷·布拉赫的体系中，除了地球之外的其他行星都围绕太阳运行，而太阳本身则围绕静止的地球运行，这种现象与哥白尼理论中出现的原因相同，因为两者在几何上是等价的。德里克·J·德·S·普莱斯（1969）已经相当普遍地证明，一旦调整这些体系以符合观测到的行星和太阳的角度位置，这种情况必然成立。奥西安德在其为哥白尼的《天体运行论》所作的导言中承认，自古以来，行星的视大小一直是主要天文理论面临的一个难题。

A final argument for the veracity of the telescopic data on the sizes of Venus and Mars is that they corresponded precisely with the predictions of all of the serious astronomical theories at the time. This conflicts with the way in which Feyerabend, and Galileo himself, presented the situation, implying, as they did, that the data offers support to the Copernican theory over its rivals. The rivals to the Copernican theory were those of Ptolemy and Tycho Brahé. Both of those theories predicted precisely the same variations in size as the Copernican theory did. Variations in distance from earth, leading to predicted changes in apparent size, arise in the Ptolemaic system because the planets move closer then further from the earth as they traverse the epicycles superimposed on the deferents, which latter were equidistant from the earth. They occur in Tycho Brahé’s system, in which planets other than earth orbit the sun while the sun itself orbits a stationary earth, for the same reason that they occur in the Copernican theory, since the two are geometrically equivalent. Derek J. de S. Price (1969) has shown quite generally that this must be so once the systems are adjusted to fit the observed angular positions of the planets and the sun. That the apparent sizes of the planets had posed a problem for the major astronomical theories since antiquity is acknowledged by Osiander in his introduction to Copernicus’s Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres.

我们已经考察了伽利略如何论证接受一些重要的望远镜观测结果，我认为他的论证颇具说服力，这一观点也得到了历史事实的证实：这些论证在短时间内就说服了伽利略所有主要的竞争对手。然而，在确立其论点的过程中，伽利略迈出了科学发展中一个普遍趋势的第一步，即用仪器获取的数据取代肉眼观测数据。这样做违背了“科学本身的标准”，并导致了这一标准的改变。那么，他在这方面的成就与方法论的正反之亦然呢？

We have surveyed the way in which Galileo argued for acceptance of some significant telescopic findings, arguments that, I suggest, were compelling, a suggestion borne out by the historical fact that they convinced all of Galileo’s serious rivals in a short space of time. But in establishing his case, Galileo made the first step in what was to be a common trend in science, the replacement of naked-eye data by data acquired by way of instruments, and in doing so violated, and brought about a change in, ‘the criterion of science itself’. How does his accomplishment of this bear on the case for and against method?

理论、方法和标准的逐步改变

Piecemeal change of theory, method and standards

伽利略是如何在面对约翰·沃勒尔等人的论证（他们认为这是不可能的）时，通过理性论证改变标准而取得成功的呢？他之所以能够做到这一点，是因为他和他的竞争对手之间存在许多共同之处。他们的目标有很多重叠之处。其中一个共同的目标是描述天体的运动，并用经验证据加以验证。毕竟，托勒密的《天文学大成》中充满了行星位置的记录，而第谷·布拉赫则因其建造的大型象限仪等装置而闻名，这些装置极大地提高了此类记录的精度。伽利略指出了一些基础观测结果，他的对手别无选择，只能接受这些结果，例如夜晚从远处看，灯看起来比实际更大，以及金星在白天看起来比在夜晚看起来更小。像这样的共同观察，再加上共同的目标，足以让伽利略运用“巧妙的说服技巧”（实际上只是直截了当的论证），说服他的反对者，至少在某种情况下，他们应该愿意放弃“科学本身的标准”，接受一些望远镜数据，而不是肉眼所见的数据。

How is it that Galileo has managed to change standards by making a rational case in the face of arguments, such as John Worrall’s, to the effect that this is impossible? He was able to do so because there was much that was shared between him and his rivals. There was a large overlap in what they aimed for. Among much else, they shared the aim of giving a description of the motions of the heavenly bodies that was borne out by the empirical evidence. After all, Ptolemy’s Almagest is full of recordings of planetary positions, and Tycho Brahé is famed for his construction of massive quadrants and the like, which dramatically increased the accuracy of such recordings. There were low-level observations pointed out by Galileo that his opponents had no sensible option but to accept, such as the observation that a lamp appears larger than it really is from a distance at night, and that Venus looks smaller in the light of day than in the dark of night. Shared observations such as these, against the background of the shared aim, were sufficient for Galileo to be able to convince his opponents, using ‘clever techniques of persuasion’ that involved nothing other than straightforward argument, that in one context at least they should be willing to abandon the ‘criterion of science itself’ and accept some telescopic data rather than their naked-eye counterpart.

在任何发展阶段，一门科学都包含一些具体目标，旨在获得某种特定类型的知识；实现这些目标的方法以及评判目标实现程度的标准；以及代表当前目标实现状况的具体事实和理论。这一系列要素中的每一个都会根据研究结果进行修正。我们已经讨论过理论和事实可能出错的方式（例如，过冷液体反驳了“液体不能逆流而上”的说法），并且在上一节中也举例说明了方法和标准的改变。一门科学的目标的具体形式也会发生变化。让我举个例子。

At any stage in its development, a science will consist of some specific aims to arrive at knowledge of some specified kind, methods for arriving at those aims together with standards for judging the extent to which they have been met, and specific facts and theories that represent the current state of play as far as the realisation of the aim is concerned. Each individual item in the web of entities will be subject to revision in the light of research. We have already discussed ways in which theories and facts are fallible (remember that supercooled liquids refute the claim that liquids cannot flow uphill) and we illustrated in the previous section a change in method and standards. The detailed form that the aim of a science takes can change too. Let me give an example.

罗伯特·波义耳的实验工作被公认为十七世纪科学革命的一项重大贡献。波义耳的工作中存在两个看似矛盾的方面，从某种意义上说，它们分别代表了科学研究的新旧两种方式。在他更具哲学性的著作中，波义耳倡导“机械论”。根据这种哲学，物质世界被视为由物质微粒构成。人们理所当然地认为物质只有一种。可观察的物体是由微小的物质微粒排列而成的，而变化则应理解为微粒的重新排列。物质微粒的唯一属性是它们各自特定的大小、形状和运动，以及将物质与真空区分开来的不可穿透性。当一个微粒与其他微粒碰撞时，它的运动就会发生改变，而这种机制正是自然界一切活动和变化的根源。对某些物理过程的解释，必然涉及追溯该过程，直至其根源在于相关微粒的运动、碰撞和重组。波义耳表达了这种观点，他认同当时被视为亚里士多德世界观的恰当替代方案的新兴机械论世界观。在机械论世界观中，充分的解释即是终极解释。这些解释诉诸于微粒的形状、大小、运动和碰撞，而这些概念本身被认为无需解释。因此，从这个角度来看，科学的目标就是提供终极解释。

The experimental work of Robert Boyle is rightly seen as a major contribution to the scientific revolution of the seventeenth century. Two somewhat conflicting aspects of Boyle’s work can be discerned that, in a sense, represent the old and the new way of doing science. In his more philosophical writings Boyle advocated the ‘mechanical philosophy’. According to that philosophy, the material world is seen as consisting of pieces of matter. It is taken as obvious that there is just this one kind of matter. Observable-sized objects are made up of arrangements of microscopic corpuscles of matter, and change is to be understood in terms of the rearrangement of corpuscles. The only properties corpuscles of matter have are the specific size, shape and motion that each one possesses, together with the property of impenetrability that serves to distinguish matter from empty space. The motion of a corpuscle changes when it collides with another, and this mechanism is the source of all activity and change in nature. An explanation of some physical process will involve tracing that process back to the motions, collisions and rearrangements of the corpuscles involved. In giving expression to a version of this view, Boyle was subscribing to the new mechanical world view that was seen as the appropriate alternative to the Aristotelian one. In it, adequate explanations were ultimate explanations. They appealed to the shapes, sizes, motions and collisions of corpuscles, and these notions were themselves not considered to be in need of explanation. The aim of science, then, from this point of view, is ultimate explanations.

除了倡导机械论之外，波义耳也进行实验，尤其是在气动学和化学领域。正如波义耳的一些言论所暗示的那样，他的实验成功并未产生机械论所要求的那种科学知识。波义耳对空气物理学的实验，特别是那些利用气泵将玻璃容器中的大部分空气抽出的实验，使他能够用空气的重量和弹性来解释一系列现象，例如气压计在真空容器内外的读数。他甚至提出了一个以他名字命名的、描述一定质量气体压力和体积之间关系的定律。但从机械论的角度来看，他的解释并非科学解释，因为它们并非最终的解释。在用微粒机制解释重量和弹性本身之前，诉诸于这些性质是不可接受的。毋庸置疑，波义耳未能满足这一要求。最终，人们逐渐认识到波义耳的实验科学追求的是既实用又可行的解释。相比之下，严格意义上的机械解释则被认为是无法实现的。实际上，到了十七世纪末，物理学放弃了追求终极解释的目标。这一目标被视为乌托邦式的幻想，尤其是在与实验科学的成就相比时。

As well as advocating the mechanical philosophy, Boyle did experiments, notably his experiments in pneumatics and chemistry. As some of Boyle’s own remarks imply, his experimental successes did not yield scientific knowledge of the kind demanded within the mechanical philosophy. Boyle’s experiments on the physics of air, especially those with an air pump which enabled him to evacuate most of the air from a glass chamber, led him to explain a range of phenomena, such as the behaviour of barometers both inside and outside of evacuated chambers, in terms of the weight and elasticity of air. He was even able to suggest a version of the law connecting the pressure and volume of a fixed mass of gas that bears his name. But his explanations were not scientific explanations from the point of view of the mechanical philosophy because they were not ultimate. Appealing to weight and elasticity was not acceptable until those properties themselves had been explained in terms of corpuscular mechanisms. Needless to say, Boyle was unable to satisfy that demand. Eventually it became appreciated that Boyle’s experimental science sought explanations that were both useful and attainable. By contrast, mechanical explanations in the strict sense came to be appreciated as unattainable. In effect, by the end of the seventeenth century the aim for ultimate explanations was given up in physics. That aim came to be seen as utopian, especially when contrasted with the achievements of experimental science.

因此，其总体思路是，构成某一特定时期科学的目标、方法、标准、理论和观察事实网络中的任何部分都可以逐步改变，而网络的其余部分则为这种改变提供论证的背景。然而，我们当然不可能为一次性改变网络中的所有内容提出合理的论证，因为那样就没有任何立足之地。所以，如果科学的典型特征是，相互竞争的科学家从各自范式的角度看待一切，生活在彼此不同的世界里，以至于没有任何共同之处，那么我们确实不可能客观地把握科学进步的进程。但是，在科学、科学史乃至任何其他领域，都不存在符合这种刻板印象的情况。我们不需要一个普遍的、非历史性的科学方法论来客观地描述科学的进步，而且，我们完全可以客观地描述如何改进方法。

The general idea, then, is that any part of the web of aims, methods, standards, theories and observational facts that constitute a science at a particular time can be progressively changed, and the remaining part of the web will provide the background against which a case for the change can be made. However, it will certainly not be possible to make a reasoned case for changing everything in the web at once, for then there would be no ground on which to stand to make such a case. So if it were typical of science that rival scientists see everything differently from the point of view of their respective paradigms and live in different worlds to the extent that they share nothing, it would indeed be impossible to capture an objective sense in which science progresses. But there are no situations in science or its history or, for that matter, anywhere else that conform to this caricature. We do not need a universal, ahistorical account of scientific method to give an objective account of progress in science, and, furthermore, an objective account of how method can be changed for the better is possible.

轻松愉快的插曲

A light-hearted interlude

我可以想象约翰·沃勒尔以及其他与我观点相近的相对主义反对者和普适方法论捍卫者会如何回应我上述的论述。例如，他们会就我举的伽利略的例子指出，虽然这确实说明了标准的改变，但其中也涉及到对更高、更普遍标准的诉求。例如，伽利略和他的对手都要求他们对行星轨道的解释必须有相应的证据支持。我的批评者很可能会辩称，一旦我们阐明了这些普遍假设，那么正是这些普遍假设构成了普适方法论，也正是这些假设构成了评判伽利略所带来的变革是否具有进步性的背景。我仿佛听到他们在说，如果没有这样的背景，你就无法论证这种变革是进步的。

I can imagine how John Worrall, and like-minded opponents of relativism and defenders of universal method, would respond to the line I have taken above. They will say of my Galileo example, for instance, that, although it does illustrate a change in standards, an appeal to some higher, more general standards is involved. Both Galileo and his rivals demanded that their account of planetary orbits should be borne out by appropriate evidence, for example. Once we have spelt out these general assumptions, my critics might well argue, then it is those general assumptions that constitute universal method, and it is precisely those which form the backdrop against which the change brought about by Galileo is to be judged progressive. Without such a backdrop, I hear them say, you cannot argue that the change is progressive.

让我做出一个让步。假设我们尝试制定一些普遍原则，从亚里士多德到斯蒂芬·霍金，任何科学倡导者都应遵循这些原则。假设最终结果是“认真对待论证和现有证据，不要追求超出现有方法范围的知识或证实程度”。我们不妨称之为科学方法的常识版本。我承认，常识中确实存在一种普遍适用的方法。但我想立即消除约翰·沃勒尔及其盟友可能因赢得我的这一让步而产生的沾沾自喜之感。首先，我要指出，如果这种常识性的普遍适用的方法是正确的且充分的，那么它就会让他们所有人，包括我自己，都无事可做，因为它绝非专业哲学家能够阐述、理解或捍卫的东西。更严重的是，我指出，一旦我们进一步追问这个问题，并要求提供更多细节，例如什么才算证据和证实，以及究竟哪些主张可以辩护以及如何辩护，那么这些细节将因科学领域和历史背景而异。

Let me make a concession. Suppose we do try to formulate some general principles that any proponent of science from Aristotle to Stephen Hawking might be expected to adhere to. Suppose the result is something like ‘take argument and the available evidence seriously and do not aim for a kind of knowledge or a level of confirmation that is beyond the reach of available methods’. Let us call it the commonsense version of scientific method. I concede that there is a universal method in the commonsense. But let me immediately attempt to remove any feeling of smugness John Worrall and his allies might be enjoying having won this concession from me. Let me first point out that, to the extent that commonsense universal method is correct and adequate, it puts them all, and myself, out of business, because it is hardly the kind of thing that it takes a professional philosopher to formulate, appreciate or defend. More seriously, I point out that once we do press the issue further, and demand that more detail be given, concerning what counts as evidence and confirmation, and precisely what kind of claims can be defended and how, then those details will vary from science to science and from historical context to historical context.

对常识方法的阐述或许不足以让科学哲学家们继续从事相关工作。然而，我认为，理解常识方法足以抵制当代科学研究中的一些趋势。我指的是那些科学社会学家和后现代主义者（我们姑且称他们为“平等主义者”），他们淡化或否认科学知识应享有的特殊地位，理由是确立科学知识的权威性必然涉及科学家或科学家群体的利益，例如经济或社会地位、职业利益等等，这与任何其他社会活动并无二致。对此，我认为，增进对化学物质如何结合的了解这一目标，与提升职业化学家的社会地位这一目标之间存在着一种常识性的区别。我甚至认为，如果某些学术运动违背了这种常识，那么那些拥有这种常识的人就应该要求切断这些运动的资金来源。值得注意的是，传统的科学哲学家们自身也促成了一种局面的形成，这种局面为平等主义者提供了可乘之机。正是他们假定，只有借助某种哲学上阐述的普遍方法论，才能区分科学与其他类型的知识。因此，当这些尝试失败时——正如本书前几章所展示的那样——平等主义者似乎便有机可乘。迈克尔·穆尔凯（1979）无疑是最谦逊的平等主义者之一，他只是众多科学分析家中的一个例子，这些分析家得出结论：由于他所谓的“标准观点”的失败，对科学进行社会学分类是必要的。

A formulation of commonsense method might not be sufficiently demanding a task to keep philosophers of science in business. However, I do suggest that an appreciation of it is sufficient to resist some contemporary trends in science studies. I have in mind those sociologists of science and postmodernists (let’s call them ‘the levellers’ for short) who downplay or deny the special status to be accorded scientific knowledge on the grounds that establishing its credentials necessarily involves the interests of scientists and groups of scientists, such things as financial or social status, professional interests and the like, in much the same way as any other social task does. In response to this I suggest there is a commonsense distinction between, say, the aim to improve knowledge of how chemicals combine and the aim to improve the social standing of professional chemists. I would even go so far as to suggest that if there are academic movements that fly in the face of this commonsense, then those in possession of such sense should demand that those movements be starved of funds. It is interesting to note that traditional philosophers of science have themselves contributed to the manufacturing of a situation that opens a space for the levellers. It is they who have presumed that a distinction between science and other kinds of knowledge can only be achieved with the aid of some philosophically articulated account of universal method. Consequently, when those attempts fail, in a way that the preceding chapters of this book have shown them to have done, the way seems open for the levellers to move in. Michael Mulkay (1979), one of the most modest of levellers to be sure, provides just one of the many possible examples of an analyst of science who draws the conclusion that a sociological categorisation of science is made necessary by the failure of what he terms ‘the standard view’.1

这就引出了大约十五年前科学哲学领域辩论的焦点。我们不能就此止步，因为在此期间，出现了两个重要的思潮，值得我们关注。其中一个思潮试图通过借鉴概率论来构建一种普适方法论。我们将在下一章对此进行探讨。第二个思潮则试图通过深入研究实验及其本质，来反驳其认为长期占据主导地位的、以理论为主导的科学论述中存在的种种弊端。这种方法将在第十三章中进行讨论。

This brings us to the point at which the debate within philosophy of science stood about fifteen years ago. We cannot leave matters here, because during that period there have been two important movements that have developed since then and which warrant attention. One of these movements involves an attempt to develop an account of universal method by adapting a version of probability theory. We investigate it in the next chapter. The second movement has attempted to counter what it sees as the excesses of the theory-dominated accounts of science that have held sway for some time by taking a close look at experiment and what it involves. This approach is discussed in chapter 13.

延伸阅读

Further reading

我在《科学及其构建》（查尔默斯，1990，第二章）中更详细地阐述了我对普遍方法的反对，而《伽利略对金星和火星的望远镜观测》（查尔默斯，1985）和《费耶阿本德错过的伽利略》（查尔默斯，1986）则对费耶阿本德的伽利略案例研究进行了批判和改进。劳丹（1977）和劳丹（1984）试图在普遍方法和无政府主义之间找到一条中间道路，这与我的观点有所不同。关于我针对波义耳著作的论述，更多细节可参见《波义耳机械哲学的不足》（查尔默斯，1993）和《科学中的终极解释》（查尔默斯，1995）。

My case against universal method is made in a little more detail in Science and Its Fabrication (Chalmers, 1990, chapter 2), while ‘Galileo’s Telescopic Observations of Venus and Mars’ (Chalmers, 1985) and ‘The Galileo that Feyerabend Missed’ (Chalmers, 1986) contain a critique and improvement of Feyerabend’s Galileo case study. Laudan (1977) and Laudan (1984) involve an attempt to find a middle way between universal method and anarchism that differs from mine. More details of the case I make with relation to Boyle’s work can be found in ‘The Lack of Excellence of Boyle’s Mechanical Philosophy’ (Chalmers, 1993) and ‘Ultimate Explanation in Science’ (Chalmers, 1995).

第十二章

CHAPTER 12

贝叶斯方法

The Bayesian approach

介绍

Introduction

我们许多人对哈雷彗星最近一次回归的预测信心十足，以至于提前预订了远离城市灯光、前往乡村的周末行程，以便观测它。事实证明，我们的信心并非盲目。科学家们对自己的理论可靠性充满信心，从而将载人航天器送入太空。当其中一次任务出现意外时，科学家们借助计算机的辅助，迅速计算出如何利用剩余的火箭燃料，以恰到好处的方式点燃火箭发动机，将航天器送入能够返回地球的轨道，这让我们印象深刻，但或许并不意外。这些例子表明，我们故事中从波普尔到费耶阿本德等哲学家们所强调的理论的易错性或许被曲解或夸大了。波普尔关于所有科学理论概率为零的论断，能否与这些例子相调和呢？在此值得强调的是，我两个故事中科学家所使用的理论都是牛顿理论，而根据波普尔的论述（以及大多数其他观点），牛顿理论在二十世纪初就已被以多种方式证伪。显然，这其中肯定存在严重的问题。

Many of us had sufficient confidence in the prediction of the most recent return of Halley’s comet that we booked weekends in the country, far from city lights and well in advance, in order to observe it. Our confidence proved not to be misplaced. Scientists have enough confidence in the reliability of their theories to send manned spacecraft into space. When things went amiss in one of them, we were impressed, but perhaps not surprised, when the scientists, aided by computers, were able to rapidly calculate how the remaining rocket fuel could be utilised to fire the rocket motor in just the right way to put the craft into an orbit that would return it to earth. These stories suggest that perhaps the extent to which theories are fallible, stressed by the philosophers in our story so far, from Popper to Feyerabend, are misplaced or exaggerated. Can the Popperian claim that the probability of all scientific theories is zero be reconciled with them? It is worth stressing, in this connection, that the theory used by the scientists in both of my stories was Newtonian theory, a theory falsified in a number of ways at the beginning of the twentieth century according to the Popperian account (and most others). Surely something has gone seriously wrong.

有一群哲学家认为某些方面出现了根本性的错误，并且在过去几十年里，他们试图纠正这些错误的努力逐渐流行起来。这群哲学家就是贝叶斯主义者，之所以被称为贝叶斯主义者，是因为他们的观点基于十八世纪数学家托马斯·贝叶斯证明的概率论定理。贝叶斯主义者认为，将一个已被充分证实的理论的概率设为零是不恰当的，他们寻求某种归纳推理方法，以得出非零概率，同时避免第四章中描述的那些难题。例如，他们希望能够证明，当使用牛顿理论计算哈雷彗星或航天器的轨道时，为什么可以赋予其很高的概率。本章将概述并批判性地评价他们的观点。

One group of philosophers who do think that something has gone radically wrong, and whose attempts to put it right have become popular in the last few decades, are the Bayesians, so called because they base their views on a theorem in probability theory proved by the eighteenth-century mathematician Thomas Bayes. The Bayesians regard it as inappropriate to ascribe zero probability to a well-confirmed theory, and they seek some kind of inductive inference that will yield non-zero probabilities for them in a way that avoids the difficulties of the kind described in chapter 4. For example, they would like to be able to show how and why a high probability can be attributed to Newtonian theory when used to calculate the orbit of Halley’s comet or a spacecraft. An outline and critical appraisal of their viewpoint is given in this chapter.

贝叶斯定理

Bayes’ theorem

贝叶斯定理研究的是条件概率，即命题的概率取决于（因此也是以）与这些命题相关的证据。例如，投注者对每匹马的胜率估计取决于他对每匹马过往表现的了解。此外，当投注者到达赛马场后发现某匹马汗流浃背、看起来病恹恹的，他就会根据新的证据调整这些概率。贝叶斯定理规定了如何根据新的证据调整概率。

Bayes’ theorem is about conditional probabilities, probabilities for propositions that depend on (and hence are conditional on) the evidence bearing on those propositions. For instance, the probabilities ascribed by a punter to each horse in a race will be conditional on the knowledge the punter has of the past form of each of the horses. What is more, those probabilities will be subject to change by the punter in the light of new evidence, when, for example, he finds on arrival at the racetrack that one of the horses is sweating badly and looking decidedly sick. Bayes’ theorem is a theorem prescribing how probabilities are to be changed in the light of new evidence.

在科学领域，问题在于如何根据证据为理论或假设赋予概率。令 P( h/e ) 表示在证据e下假设h成立的概率，P( e/h ) 表示在假设 h 为真的前提下，证据e成立的概率，P( h ) 表示在不知道证据e的情况下，假设 h 成立的概率， P( e ) 表示在不对假设h的真假做任何假设的情况下，证据e成立的概率。那么，贝叶斯定理可以写成：

In the context of science the issue is how to ascribe probabilities to theories or hypotheses in the light of evidence.
